laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Rom 13:11)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Hora est jam nos de somno súrgere: nunc enim própior est nostra salus, quam cum credídimus.
laudes.capitulum.eng: And that knowing the season; that it is now the hour for us to rise from sleep. For now our salvation is nearer than when we believed.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Rom 13:13-14)
nona.capitulum.lat: Sicut in die honéste ambulémus, non in comessatiónibus et ebrietátibus, non in cubílibus et impudicítiis, non in contentióne et æmulatióne; sed induímini Dóminum Jesum Christum.
nona.capitulum.eng: Let us walk honestly, as in the day: not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and impurities, not in contention and envy: But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Spíritus Sanctus * in te descéndet, María: ne tímeas, habébis in útero Fílium Dei, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, * O Mary; fear not, thou shalt bear in thy womb the Son of God. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ne tímeas, María, * invenísti enim grátiam apud Dóminum: ecce concípies, et páries fílium, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Fear not, Mary, * for thou hast found grace with the Lord; behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son. Alleluia.

prima.antiphon.label: Antíphona
prima.antiphon.lat: In illa die * stillábunt montes dulcédinem, et colles fluent lac et mel, allelúja.
prima.antiphon.eng: In that day * the mountains shall drop down sweet wine, and the hills shall flow with milk and honey. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Jucundáre, * fília Sion, et exsúlta satis, fília Jerúsalem, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Sing, O daughter of Zion, * and rejoice with all the heart, O daughter of Jerusalem. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ecce Dóminus véniet, * et omnes Sancti ejus cum eo: et erit in die illa lux magna, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Behold, the Lord shall come, * and all His saints with Him; and it shall come to pass in that day that the light shall be great. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Omnes sitiéntes, * veníte ad aquas: quǽrite Dóminum, dum inveníri potest, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Lo, every one that thirsteth * come ye to the waters: seek ye the Lord while He may be found. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Ecce véniet * Prophéta magnus, et ipse renovábit Jerúsalem, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Behold, a great Prophet * shall arise, and He shall build up a new Jerusalem. Alleluia.

vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Hora est jam nos de somno súrgere: nunc enim própior est nostra salus, quam cum credídimus.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he comes that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut ab imminéntibus peccatórum nostrórum perículis, te mereámur protegénte éripi, te liberánte salvári:
collect.eng: Stir up, O Lord, we pray thee, thy strength, and come among us, that whereas through our sins and wickedness we do justly apprehend thy wrathful judgments hanging over us, thy bountiful grace and mercy may speedily help and deliver us;

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Angelus Dómini * nuntiávit Maríæ, et concépit de Spíritu Sancto, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The angel of the Lord * announced unto Mary, and she conceived of the Holy Ghost. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Leva, Jerúsalem, * óculos tuos, et vide poténtiam regis: ecce Salvátor venit sólvere te a vínculo.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Lift up thine eyes, * O Jerusalem, and see that thy King is mighty behold, thy Saviour shall come and loose thee from thy chain.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Rom 15:4)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Quæcúmque scripta sunt, ad nostram doctrínam scripta sunt: ut per patiéntiam, et consolatiónem Scripturárum spem habeámus.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For what things soever were written, were written for our learning: that through patience and the comfort of the scriptures, we might have hope.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Rom 15:5-6)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Deus autem patiéntiæ, et solácii det vobis idípsum sápere in altérutrum secúndum Jesum Christum: ut unánimes uno ore honorificétis Deum, et Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Now the God of patience and of comfort grant you to be of one mind one towards another, according to Jesus Christ:That with one mind, and with one mouth, you may glorify God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Rom 15:13)
nona.capitulum.lat: Deus autem spei répleat vos omni gáudio et pace in credéndo: ut abundétis in spe, et in virtúte Spíritus Sancti.
nona.capitulum.eng: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing; that you may abound in hope, and in the power of the Holy Ghost.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Joánnes autem * cum audísset in vínculis ópera Christi, mittens duos ex discípulis suis, ait illi: Tu es qui ventúrus es, an álium exspectámus?
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Now when John * had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples and said unto Him: Art Thou He That should come, or do we look for another?

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Tu es, qui ventúrus es, * an álium exspectámus? Dícite Joánni quæ vidístis: Ad lumen rédeunt cæci, mórtui resúrgunt, páuperes evangelizántur, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Art thou he that art to come * or look we for another? Go and relate to John what you have seen: the blind see, the dead rise again, to the poor the gospel is preached. Alleluia.

prima.antiphon.label: Antíphona
prima.antiphon.lat: Ecce in núbibus cæli * Dóminus véniet cum potestáte magna, allelúja.
prima.antiphon.eng: Behold, the Lord * cometh in the clouds of heaven with great power. Alleluia.

tertia.antiphon.label: Antíphona
tertia.antiphon.lat: Ecce in núbibus cæli * Dóminus véniet cum potestáte magna, allelúja.
tertia.antiphon.eng: Behold, the Lord * cometh in the clouds of heaven with great power. Alleluia.

sexta.antiphon.label: Antíphona
sexta.antiphon.lat: Ecce in núbibus cæli * Dóminus véniet cum potestáte magna, allelúja.
sexta.antiphon.eng: Behold, the Lord * cometh in the clouds of heaven with great power. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Urbs fortitúdinis * nostræ Sion, Salvátor ponétur in ea murus et antemurále: aperíte portas, quia nobíscum Deus, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Our Zion is a strong city, * the Saviour will God appoint in her for walls and bulwarks; open ye the gates, for God is with us. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ecce apparébit * Dóminus, et non mentiétur: si moram fécerit, exspécta eum, quia véniet, et non tardábit, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Behold, the Lord * shall appear and not lie though He tarry, wait for Him, because He will come and will not tarry. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Montes et colles * cantábunt coram Deo laudem, et ómnia ligna silvárum plaudent mánibus: quóniam véniet Dominátor Dóminus in regnum ætérnum, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The mountains and the hills * shall break forth before God into singing, and all the trees of the wood shall clap their hands for the Lord the Ruler cometh, and He shall reign for ever and ever. Alleluia, Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Behold, our Lord * cometh with power, and He shall lighten the eyes of His servants. Alleluia.

laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Gaudéte in Dómino semper: íterum dico, gaudéte. Modéstia vestra nota sit ómnibus homínibus: Dóminus enim prope est.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: Rejoice in the Lord always; again, I say, rejoice. Let your modesty be known to all men. The Lord is nigh.

sexta.capitulum.eng: Be nothing solicitous; but in every thing, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God.

nona.capitulum.lat: Et pax Dei, quæ exsúperat omnem sensum, custódiat corda vestra, et intellegéntias vestras in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
nona.capitulum.eng: And the peace of God, which surpasseth all understanding, keep your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Beáta es, María, * quæ credidísti Dómino: perficiéntur in te, quæ dicta sunt tibi a Dómino, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Blessed art thou, * O Mary, who hast believed the Lord, for there shall be a performance of those things which were told thee from the Lord. Alleluia.

prima.antiphon.label: Antíphona

prima.antiphon.eng: The Lord will come, * and will not tarry; He both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make Himself manifest to all people. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Rejoice greatly, O Jerusalem, * for thy Saviour cometh unto thee. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: I will place salvation in Zion, * and My glory in Jerusalem. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Every mountain and hill * shall be made low, and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come and make no tarrying. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: We should live * righteously and godly, looking for that blessed hope and the coming of the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Montes et omnes colles * humiliabúntur: et erunt prava in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas: veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Every mountain and hill * shall be made low, and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come and make no tarrying. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Juste et pie * vivámus, exspectántes beátam spem, et advéntum Dómini.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: We should live * righteously and godly, looking for that blessed hope and the coming of the Lord.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Phil 4:4-5)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Gaudéte in Dómino semper: íterum dico, gaudéte. Modéstia vestra nota sit ómnibus homínibus: Dóminus enim prope est.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: The sceptre shall not be taken away from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he comes that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Aurem tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, précibus nostris accómmoda: et mentis nostræ ténebras, grátia tuæ visitatiónis illústra:
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, mercifully incline thine ears unto our prayers, and lighten the darkness of our minds by the grace of thy heavenly visitation.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dicit Dóminus: * Pœniténtian ágite, appropinquábit enim regnum cœlórum, allelúia.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: There shall come forth a rod * out of the stem of Jesse, and the whole earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord, and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Beátam me dicent * omnes generatiónes, quia ancíllam húmilem respéxit Deus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: All generations shall call me blessed, * for God hath regarded the lowliness of His hand-maiden.

prima.antiphon.label: Antíphona
prima.antiphon.lat: Véniet Dóminus, * et non tardábit, et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit se ad omnes gentes, allelúja.
prima.antiphon.eng: The Lord shall come * and shall not delay, and shall bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and shall manifest himself to all nations, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Egrediétur * virga de radíce Jesse, et replébitur omnis terra glória Dómini: et vidébit omnis caro salutáre Dei.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Thou, Bethlehem, * in the land of Judah, shalt not be the least (among the princes of Judah) for out of thee shall come a Ruler, That shall rule my people Israel.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Behold the handmaid * of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut redemptiónis nostræ ventúra solémnitas et præséntis nobis vitæ subsídia cónferat, et ætérnæ beatitúdinis prǽmia largiátur.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that the solemn Feast of our redemption, which is now at hand, may both help us in the life which now is, and further us toward the attaining of thine eternal joy in that which is to come.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Vigiláte * ánimo, in próximo est Dóminus Deus noster.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Let your soul watch, * the Lord our God is nigh at hand.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Lætámini * cum Jerúsalem, et exsultáte in ea, omnes qui dilígitis eam, in ætérnum.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Rejoice ye with Jerusalem, * and be glad with her, all ye that love her for ever.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ex quo facta est * vox salutatiónis tuæ in áuribus meis, exsultávit in gáudio infans in útero meo, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: As soon as the voice of thy salutation * sounded in mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Hoc est testimónium, * quod perhíbuit Joánnes: Qui post me venit, ante me factus est.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: John bare witness of Him, * saying He That cometh after me is preferred before me.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Constántes estóte, * vidébitis auxílium Dómini super vos.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Exalt ye the Lord * our God, and worship him upon his holy mountain.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, poténtiam tuam, et veni: ut hi, qui in tua pietáte confídunt, ab omni cítius adversitáte liberéntur:
collect.eng: Stir up, O Lord, we pray thee, thy might, and come among us; that we, trusting only in thy mercy, may by thee be speedily delivered from all adversity.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Omnis vallis implébitur, * et omnis mons, et collis humiliábitur, et vidébit omnis caro salutáre Dei.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: O thou Angel of God, * how shall this be, seeing I know not a man? Hear, O Virgin Mary! the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee!

prima.antiphon.label: Antíphona
prima.antiphon.lat: Véniet Dóminus, * et non tardábit, et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit se ad omnes gentes, allelúja.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Roráte coeli désuper, * et nubes pluant Justum : aperiátur terra, et gérminet Salvatórem.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Let the children of Sion * be joyful in their king.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nostra pravitáte afflígimur: concéde propítius; ut ex tua visitatióne consolémur:
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that by reason of our sins we are sorely afflicted, mercifully grant unto us by thy visitation effectually to be comforted.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 4:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Sic nos exístimet homo ut minístros Christi, et dispensatóres mysteriórum Dei. Hic jam quǽritur inter dispensatóres, ut fidélis quis inveniátur.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: Let a man so account of us as of the ministers of Christ, and the dispensers of the mysteries of God. Here now it is required among the dispensers, that a man be found faithful.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 4:3)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Mihi autem pro mínimo est, ut a vobis júdicer, aut ab humáno die: sed neque meípsum júdico.
sexta.capitulum.eng: But to me it is a very small thing to be judged by you, or by man's day; but neither do I judge my own self.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 4:5)
nona.capitulum.lat: Itaque nolíte ante tempus judicáre, quoadúsque véniat Dóminus: qui et illuminábit abscóndita tenebrárum, et manifestábit consília córdium: et tunc laus erit unicuíque a Deo.
nona.capitulum.eng: Therefore judge not before the time; until the Lord come, who both will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and will make manifest the counsels of the hearts; and then shall every man have praise from God.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ave, María, * grátia plena: Dóminus tecum: benedícta tu in muliéribus, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Hail, Mary, full of grace, * the Lord is with thee; blessed art thou among women. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Cánite tuba * in Sion, quia prope est dies Dómini: ecce véniet ad salvándum nos, allelúja, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Sound the trumpet * in Sion, for the day of the Lord is near: behold, he shall come to save us, alleluia, alleluia.

prima.antiphon.label: Antíphona
prima.antiphon.lat: Cánite tuba * in Sion, quia prope est dies Dómini: ecce véniet ad salvándum nos, allelúja, allelúja.
prima.antiphon.eng: Blow ye the trumpet * in Zion, for the day of the Lord is nigh at hand: behold, He cometh to save us! Alleluia, Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Blow ye the trumpet * in Zion, for the day of the Lord is nigh at hand: behold, He cometh to save us! Alleluia, Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Ecce véniet * desiderátus cunctis géntibus: et replébitur glória domus Dómini, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Behold, the desire * of all nations shall come; and the house of the Lord shall be filled with glory. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Erunt prava * in dirécta, et áspera in vias planas: veni, Dómine, et noli tardáre, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The crooked * shall be made straight, and the rough places plain; O Lord, come, and make no tarrying. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Dóminus véniet, * occúrrite illi, dicéntes: Magnum princípium, et regni ejus non erit finis: Deus, Fortis, Dominátor, Princeps pacis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The Lord cometh! * Go ye out to meet Him, and say: How great is His dominion, and of His kingdom there shall be no end! He is the mighty God, the Ruler, the Prince of Peace. Alleluia, Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Omnípotens Sermo tuus, * Dómine, a regálibus sédibus véniet, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Thine Almighty Word, * O Lord, shall leap down out of thy royal throne. Alleluia.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
O gente felix hóspita,
Augústa sedes Názaræ,
Quæ fovit alma Ecclésiæ
Et prótulit primórdia.

Sol, qui perérrat áureo
Terras jacéntes lúmine,
Nil grátius per sǽcula
Hac vidit æde, aut sánctius.

Ad hanc frequéntes cónvolant
Cæléstis aulæ núntii,
Virtútis hoc sacrárium
Visunt, revísunt, éxcolunt.

Qua mente Jesus, qua manu,
Optáta patris pérficit!
Quo Virgo gestit gáudio
Matérna obíre múnera!

Adest amóris párticeps
Curǽque Joseph cónjugi,
Quos mille jungit néxibus
Virtútis auctor grátia.

Hi diligéntes ínvicem
In Jesu amórem cónfluunt,
Utríque Jesus mútuæ
Dat caritátis prǽmia.

Sic fiat, ut nos cáritas
Jungat perénni fœ́dere,
Pacémque alens domésticam
Amára vitæ témperet!

Jesu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
O house of Nazareth the blest,
Fair hostess of the Lord,
The Church was nurtured at Thy breast
And shared thy scanty hoard.

In all the spreading lands of earth
The wandering sun may see
No dearer spot, no ampler worth
Than erst was found in thee!

We know thy humble tenement
Was heaven’s hermitage:
Celestial heralds came and went
In endless embassage.

There, whatsoever Joseph asks
Christ hastens to fulfill;
While Mary loves the household tasks
That wait her joyous will.

There, Joseph toileth at her side
Her joys and griefs to share,
With thousand ties knit to his bride,
Of love and work and prayer.

Yet how their bosoms constant burn
And deeper ardors prove
In love of Christ, whose eyes return
Tokens of mutual love.

O then, in all the homes of earth,
Be Love the bond of life:
May it enthrone at every hearth
The peace that husheth strife.

All praise to Thee, O Jesus,
who parents dost obey;
Praise to the sovereign Father
and Paraclete for aye.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
O lux beáta cǽlitum
Et summa spes mortálium,
Jesu, o cui doméstica
Arrísit orto cáritas:

María, dives grátia,
O sola quæ casto potes
Fovére Jesum péctore,
Cum lacte donans óscula:

Tuque ex vetústis pátribus
Delécte custos Vírginis
Dulci patris quem nómine
Divína Proles ínvocat:

De stirpe Jesse nóbili
Nati in salútem géntium,
Audíte nos qui súpplices
Vestras ad aras sístimus.

Dum sol redux ad vésperum
Rebus nitórem détrahit,
Nos hic manéntes íntimo
Ex corde vota fúndimus.

Qua vestra sedes flóruit
Virtútis omnis grátia,
Hanc detur in domésticis
Reférre posse móribus.

Jesu, tuis obédiens
Qui factus es paréntibus,
Cum Patre summo ac Spíritu
Semper tibi sit glória.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
O highest hope of mortals,
Blest Light of Saints above,
O Jesu, on whose boyhood
Home smiled with kindly love;

And thou whose bosom nursed him,
O Mary, highly graced,
Whose breast gave milk to Jesus,
Whose arms thy God embraced;

And thou of all men chosen
To guard the Virgin’s fame,
To whom God’s Son refused not
A Father’s gracious name;

Born for the nation’s healing,
Of Jesse’s lineage high,
Behold the suppliants kneeling,
O hear the sinners’ cry!

The sun returned to evening,
Dusks all the twilight air:
We, lingering here before you,
Pour out our heartfelt prayer.

Your home was as a garden
Made glad with fairest flowers;
May life thus blossom sweetly
In every home of ours.

All praise to Thee, O Jesus,
who parents dost obey;
Praise to the sovereign Father
and Paraclete for aye.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Illúmina nos, Dómine, * exémplis Famíliæ tuæ, et dírige pedes nostros in viam pacis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Enlighten us, O Lord, * by the example of thy family, and direct our feet into the way of peace.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: María autem * conservábat ómnia verba hæc, cónferens in corde suo.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But Mary * kept all these words, pondering them in her heart.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.lat: Ponam univérsos fílios tuos doctos a Dómino.
laudes.versicle.eng: All thy children shall be taught of the Lord.
laudes.versicle.engR: And great shall be the peace of thy children.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Post tríduum * invenérunt Jesum in templo sedéntem in médio doctórum, audiéntem illos, et interrogántem eos.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: After three days, * they found him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, hearing them, and asking them questions.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Dixit mater Jesu * ad illum: Fili, quid fecísti nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The mother of Jesus said * to him: Son, why hast thou done so to us? Behold thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Descéndit Jesus * cum eis, et venit Názareth, et erat súbditus illis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Jesus went down * with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Et Jesus proficiébat * sapiéntia, et ætáte, et grátia apud Deum et hómines.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: And Jesus advanced * in wisdom, and age, and grace with God and men.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Et dicébant: * Unde huic sapiéntia hæc, et virtútes? Nonne hic est fabri fílius?
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: And they said: * How came this man by this wisdom and miracles? Is not this the carpenter's son?

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph virum Maríæ; de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: And Jacob * begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Angelus Dómini * appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Joseph, fili David, noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est.;;112
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The angel of the Lord * appeared to Joseph in his sleep, saying: Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife, for that which is conceived in her, is of the Holy Ghost.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Pastóres venérunt * festinántes, et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio.;;121
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The shepherds came * with haste; and they found Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Magi, intrántes domum, * invenérunt Púerum cum María, matre ejus.;;126
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The Magi, entering into the house, * found the child with Mary his mother.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Erat Pater ejus * et Mater mirántes super his quæ dicebántur de illo.;;147
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: His father * and mother were wondering at those things which were spoken concerning him.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Luc 2:51)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Descéndit Jesus cum María et Joseph, et venit Názareth: et erat súbditus illis.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Jesus went down with Mary and Joseph, and came to Nazareth, and was subject to them.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Dómine Jesu Christe, qui, Maríæ et Joseph súbditus, domésticam vitam ineffabílibus virtútibus consecrásti: fac nos, utriúsque auxílio, Famíliæ sanctæ tuæ exémplis ínstrui; et consórtium cónsequi sempitérnum:
collect.eng: Lord Jesus Christ, who subject to Mary and Joseph, didst consecrate family life by thy unspeakable virtues, aid us by their united intercession to profit by the examples of thy Holy Family, and attain to their everlasting companionship:

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Núptiæ factæ sunt * in Cana Galilǽæ, et erat ibi Jesus cum María matre sua.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: There was a marriage * in Cana of Galilee: and Jesus was there, with Mary, his mother.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Deficiénte vino, * jussit Jesus impléri hýdrias aqua, quæ in vinum convérsa est, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The wine failing, * Jesus commanded the water pots to be filled with water, which was changed into wine, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui cæléstia simul et terréna moderáris: supplicatiónes pópuli tui cleménter exáudi; et pacem tuam nostris concéde tempóribus.
collect.eng: Almighty and eternal God, as thou govern all things in heaven and on earth; in thy mercy hear the supplication of thy people, and grant thy peace in our times.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum descendísset Jesus * de monte, ecce leprósus véniens adorábat eum, dicens: Dómine, si vis, potes me mundáre: et exténdens manum, tétigit eum, dicens: Volo, mundáre.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When Jesus was come down from the mountain, * behold, there came a leper, and worshipped Him, saying: Lord, if Thou wilt, Thou canst make me clean. And Jesus put forth His Hand, and touched him, saying: I will; be thou clean.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dómine, * si vis, potes me mundáre: et ait Jesus: Volo, mundáre.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Lord, if Thou wilt, * Thou canst make me clean; and Jesus saith to him: I will; be thou clean.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, infirmitátem nostram propítius réspice: atque, ad protegéndum nos, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, mercifully look upon our infirmities, and in all our dangers and necessities stretch forth the right hand of thy Majesty to help and defend us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ascendénte Jesu * in navículam, ecce motus magnus factus est in mari: et suscitavérunt eum discípuli ejus, dicéntes: Dómine, salva nos, perímus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When Jesus was entered into a ship, * there arose a great tempest in the sea and His disciples awoke Him, saying: Lord, save us; we perish.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dómine, salva nos, * perímus: ímpera, et fac, Deus, tranquillitátem.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Lord, save us: * we perish; give the word, O God, and let there be a great calm!

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui nos in tantis perículis constitútos, pro humána scis fragilitáte non posse subsístere: da nobis salútem mentis et córporis; ut ea, quæ pro peccátis nostris pátimur, te adjuvánte vincámus.
collect.eng: O God, Who knowest us to be set in the midst of so many and great dangers, that, by reason of the frailty of our nature, we cannot always stand upright; grant to us such health of mind and body, that by thy strength and protection we may overcome all evils, whereby for our sins we are justly afflicted.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dómine, * nonne bonum semen seminásti in agro tuo? unde ergo habet zizánia? Et ait illis: Hoc fecit inimícus homo.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? * From whence then hath it tares? And he saith unto them: An enemy hath done this.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Collígite * primum zizánia, et alligáte ea in fascículos ad comburéndum: tríticum autem congregáte in hórreum meum, dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The master saith: Gather ye together first the tares, * and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Famíliam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, contínua pietáte custódi: ut, quæ in sola spe grátiæ cœléstis innítitur, tua semper protectióne muniátur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee to keep thy family continually in godliness, that they who do lean only upon the hope of thine heavenly grace, may evermore be defended by thy mighty power.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Símile est * regnum cælórum grano sinápis, quod mínimum est ómnibus semínibus: cum autem créverit, majus est ómnibus oléribus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The kingdom of heaven * is like to a grain of mustard-seed, which is the least of all seeds, but, when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Símile est * regnum cælórum ferménto, quod accéptum múlier abscóndit in farínæ satis tribus, donec fermentátum est totum.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The kingdom of heaven * is like unto leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, semper rationabília meditántes, quæ tibi sunt plácita, et dictis exsequámur et factis.
collect.eng: Grant us, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, ever to think such things as be reasonable, and in every word and work of ours, to do always that is well pleasing in thy sight.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Quanto témpore heres párvulus est, nihil differt a servo, cum sit dóminus ómnium: sed sub tutóribus et actóribus est usque ad præfínitum tempus a patre.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: As long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by the father.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:4-5)
sexta.capitulum.lat: At ubi venit plenitúdo témporis, misit Deus Fílium suum factum ex mulíere, factum sub lege, ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redímeret, ut adoptiónem filiórum reciperémus.
sexta.capitulum.eng: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law: That he might redeem them who were under the law: that we might receive the adoption of sons.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:7)
nona.capitulum.lat: Itaque jam non est servus, sed fílius: quod si fílius, et hæres per Deum.
nona.capitulum.eng: Therefore now he is not a servant, but a son. And if a son, an heir also through God.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
Natum María Vírgine.

Beátus auctor sǽculi
Servíle corpus índuit:
Ut carne carnem líberans,
Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

Castæ Paréntis víscera
Cæléstis intrat grátia:
Venter Puéllæ bájulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

Domus pudíci péctoris
Templum repénte fit Dei:
Intácta nésciens virum,
Concépit alvo Fílium.

Enítitur puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem ventre Matris géstiens,
Baptísta clausum sénserat.

Fœno jacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Et lacte módico pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

Gaudet chorus cæléstium,
Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Lo, the dim shadows of the night are waning;
Lightsome and blushing, dawn of day returneth;
Fervent in spirit, to the world’s Creator
Pray we devoutly:

That he may pity sinners in their sighing,
Banish all troubles, kindly health bestowing;
And may he grant us, of his countless blessings,
Peace that is endless.

This be our portion, God forever blessed,
Father eternal, Son, and Holy Spirit,
Whose is the glory, which through all creation
Ever resoundeth.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Quem lucis ante oríginem
Parem patérnæ glóriæ
Pater suprémus édidit.

Tu lumen, et splendor Patris,
Tu spes perénnis ómnium,
Inténde quas fundunt preces
Tui per orbem sérvuli.

Meménto, rerum Cónditor,
Nostri quod olim córporis,
Sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

Testátur hoc præsens dies,
Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus e sinu Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
Hunc omne, quod cælo subest,
Salútis auctórem novæ
Novo salútat cántico.

Et nos, beáta quos sacri
Rigávit unda sánguinis,
Natális ob diem tui
Hymni tribútum sólvimus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
O blest Creator of the light,
Who mak’st the day with radiance bright,
And o’er the forming world didst call
The light from chaos first of all;

Whose wisdom joined in meet array
The morn and eve, and named them day:
Night comes with all its darkling fears;
Regard thy people’s prayers and tears.

Lest, sunk in sin, and whelmed with strife,
They lose the gift of endless life;
While thinking but the thoughts of time,
They weave new chains of woe and crime.

But grant them grace that they may strain
The heavenly gate and prize to gain:
Each harmful lure aside to cast,
And purge away each error past.

* O Father, that we ask be done,
Through Jesus Christ, thine only Son;
Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,
Doth live and reign eternally.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dum médium siléntium * tenérent ómnia, et nox in suo cursu médium iter perágeret, omnípotens Sermo tuus, Dómine, a regálibus sédibus venit, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: While all things were in quiet silence * and that night was in the midst of her swift course, thine Almighty Word, O Lord, leapt down out of thy Royal Throne.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Puer Jesus * proficiébat ætáte et sapiéntia coram Deo et homínibus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And Jesus advanced in wisdom * and age, and grace with God and men.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: The Word was made flesh, alleluia.
laudes.versicle.engR: And dwelt among us, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: The Word was made flesh, alleluia.
vesperae.versicle.engR: And dwelt among us, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Quem vidístis, * pastóres? dícite, annuntiáte nobis, in terris quis appáruit? Natum vídimus, et choros Angelórum collaudántes Dóminum, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O ye shepherds, speak, * and tell us what ye have seen; who is appeared in the earth? We saw the newborn Child, and angels singing praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.;;129
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.;;131
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:1-2)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Quanto témpore heres párvulus est, nihil differt a servo, cum sit dóminus ómnium: sed sub tutóribus et actóribus est usque ad præfínitum tempus a patre.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers: As long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by the father.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, dírige actus nostros in beneplácito tuo: ut in nómine dilécti Fílii tui mereámur bonis opéribus abundáre:
collect.eng: O Almighty and everlasting God, do Thou order all our actions in conformity with thy good pleasure, that through the name of thy well-beloved Son, we may worthily abound in all good works.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Phil 2:8-10)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Christus humiliávit semetípsum, factus obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Propter quod et Deus exaltávit illum, et donávit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen, ut in nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur.
laudes.capitulum.eng: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Phil 2:10-11)
sexta.capitulum.lat: In nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum: et omnis lingua confiteátur, quia Dóminus Jesus Christus in glória est Dei Patris.
sexta.capitulum.eng: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth: And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Col 3:17)
nona.capitulum.lat: Omne quodcúmque fácitis in verbo, aut in ópere: ómnia in nómine Dómini Jesu Christi fácite, grátias agéntes Deo et Patri per ipsum.
nona.capitulum.eng: All whatsoever you do in word or in work, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Jesu decus angélicum,
In aure dulce cánticum,
In ore mel miríficum,
In corde nectar cǽlicum.

Qui te gustant, esúriunt;
Qui bibunt, adhuc sítiunt;
Desideráre nésciunt,
Nisi Jesum, quem díligunt.

O Jesu mi dulcíssime,
Spes suspirántis ánimæ!
Te quærunt piæ lácrimæ,
Te clamor mentis íntimæ.

Mane nobíscum, Dómine,
Et nos illústra lúmine;
Pulsa mentis calígine,
Mundum reple dulcédine.

Jesu, flos Matris Vírginis,
Amor nostræ dulcédinis,
Tibi laus, honor nóminis,
Regnum beatitúdinis.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
O Jesu, Thou the Beauty art
Of Angel worlds above;
Thy name is music to the heart,
Enchanting it with love.

Celestial Sweetness unalloyed!
Who eat thee hunger still;
Who drink of thee still feel a void,
Which naught but Thou can fill.

O my sweet Jesu! hear the sigh,
Which unto thee I send;
To thee mine inmost spirit cries
My being's hope and end!

Stay with us, Lord, and with thy light
Illume the soul's abyss;
Scatter the darkness of our night,
And fill the world with bliss.

O Jesu, spotless Virgin flower,
Our life and joy: to thee
Be praise, beatitude, and power,
Through all eternity.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Jesu, dulcis memória,
Dans vera cordis gáudia:
Sed super mel, et ómnia,
Ejus dulcis præséntia.

Nil cánitur suávius,
Nil audítur jucúndius,
Nil cogitátur dúlcius,
Quam Jesus Dei Fílius.

Jesu, spes pœniténtibus,
Quam pius es peténtibus!
Quam bonus te quæréntibus!
Sed quid inveniéntibus?

Nec lingua valet dícere,
Nec líttera exprímere:
Expértus potest crédere,
Quid sit Jesum dilígere.

Sis, Jesu, nostrum gáudium,
Qui es futúrus prǽmium:
Sit nostra in te glória,
Per cuncta semper sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Jesu, the very thought of thee
With sweetness fills my breast;
But sweeter far thy face to see,
And in thy presence rest.

Nor voice can sing, nor heart can frame,
Nor can the memory find,
A sweeter sound than thy blest Name,
O Saviour of mankind!

O Hope of every contrite heart,
O Joy of all the meek,
To those who fall, how kind Thou art!
How good to those who seek!

But what to those who find? Ah! this
Nor tongue nor pen can show:
The love of Jesus, what it is
None but his loved ones know.

Jesu, our only joy be Thou,
As Thou our prize wilt be;
Jesu, be Thou our glory now,
And through eternity.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Vocátum est * Nomen ejus Jesus, quod vocátum est ab Angelo, priúsquam in útero conciperétur.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: He gave Himself * to deliver His people, and to get Himself an everlasting Name. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Magníficet * omnis ánima Nomen tuum, Dómine, et cunctórum in eo spíritus exúltet, quóniam sanctum est, et potens depónere poténtes de sede, et exaltáre húmiles, allelúia.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Thou shalt call His Name Jesus, * for He shall save His people from their sins, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: Blessed be the Name of the Lord, alleluia.
vesperae.versicle.latR: Ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.engR: From this time forth, and for evermore, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Nomen tuum, Dómine, * decet sanctitudo in longitúdinem diérum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Thy Name is as oil * poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Oleum effúsum * Nomen tuum, ídeo adolescéntulæ dilexérunt te.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Know ye that the Lord He is God, * and His Name endureth for ever.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Magnum est * Nomen meum, et honorábile in Géntibus, dicit Dóminus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: My soul thirsteth * for thy Holy Name, O Lord.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Jesus Nazarénus * Rex Judæórum, Imperátor cœli, et Dóminus dominántium.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Blessed * is the Holy Name of thy glory, and worthy to be praised, and exalted above all for ever.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Vincénti dabo * manna abscónditum, et Nomen novum scriptum, quod nemo scit, nisi qui áccipit.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Young men and maidens, * old men and children, praise the Name of the Lord, for His Name alone is exalted.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Omnis * qui invocáverit nomen Dómini, salvus erit.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Whosoever shall call * on the name of the Lord shall be saved.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Sanctum et terríbile * nomen ejus, inítium sapiéntiæ timor Dómini.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Holy and terrible * is His Name; the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ego autem * in Dómino gaudébo, et exsultábo in Deo Jesu meo.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Yet will I rejoice * in the Lord I will joy in the God of my salvation.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: A solis ortu * usque ad occásum laudábile nomen Dómini.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: From the rising of the sun * unto the going down of the same the Lord's Name is to be praised.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Sacrificábo * hóstiam laudis, et nomen Dómini invocábo.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: I will offer * the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the Name of the Lord.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Phil 2:8-10)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Christus humiliávit semetípsum, factus obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Propter quod et Deus exaltávit illum, et donávit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen, ut in nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui unigénitum Fílium tuum constituísti humáni géneris Salvatórem, et Jesum vocári jussísti: concéde propítius; ut, cujus sanctum nomen venerámur in terris, ejus quoque aspéctu perfruámur in cælis.
collect.eng: O God, Who hast appointed thine Only-begotten Son to be the Saviour of mankind, and hast commanded that His Name should be called Jesus, mercifully grant that we who here on earth do worship that most Holy Name may be made glad in heaven by His Presence.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
laudes.capitulum.eng: God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:10)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Et: Tu in princípio, Dómine, terram fundásti: et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For he that loveth his neighbour, hath fulfilled the law.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:11-12)
nona.capitulum.lat: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
nona.capitulum.eng: Converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here. Knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things as gold or silver, but with the precious blood of Christ.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
Natum María Vírgine.

Beátus auctor sǽculi
Servíle corpus índuit:
Ut carne carnem líberans,
Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

Castæ Paréntis víscera
Cæléstis intrat grátia:
Venter Puéllæ bájulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

Domus pudíci péctoris
Templum repénte fit Dei:
Intácta nésciens virum,
Concépit alvo Fílium.

Enítitur puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem ventre Matris géstiens,
Baptísta clausum sénserat.

Fœno jacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Et lacte módico pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

Gaudet chorus cæléstium,
Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
From lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

Blest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

In that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

The mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

That Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

The manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

The heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Quem lucis ante oríginem
Parem patérnæ glóriæ
Pater suprémus édidit.

Tu lumen, et splendor Patris,
Tu spes perénnis ómnium,
Inténde quas fundunt preces
Tui per orbem sérvuli.

Meménto, rerum Cónditor,
Nostri quod olim córporis,
Sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

Testátur hoc præsens dies,
Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus e sinu Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
Hunc omne, quod cælo subest,
Salútis auctórem novæ
Novo salútat cántico.

Et nos, beáta quos sacri
Rigávit unda sánguinis,
Natális ob diem tui
Hymni tribútum sólvimus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Jesus, the Ransomer of man,
Who, ere created light began,
Didst from the sovereign Father spring,
His power and glory equalling.

The Father’s Light and Splendor Thou,
Their endless hope to Thee that bow;
Accept the prayers and praise to-day
That through the world Thy servants pay.

Salvation’s Author, call to mind
How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,
Thou in man’s flesh becam’st a Child.

Thus testifies the present day,
Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

The heavens above, the rolling main
And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

And we who, by Thy precious Blood
From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

O Lord, the Virgin-born, to Thee
Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: et vídimus glóriam ejus, glóriam quasi Unigéniti a Patre plenum grátiæ, et veritátis, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Glory be to God in the highest; * and on earth, peace to men of good will, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Hódie * Christus natus est: hódie Salvátor appáruit: hódie in terra canunt Angeli, lætántur Archángeli: hódie exsúltant justi, dicéntes: Glória in excélsis Deo, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: This day the Christ is born this day the Saviour is appeared; * this day the Angels sing praise in the earth and the Archangels rejoice; this day the righteous are glad and say: Glory to God in the highest. Alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: The Lord hath made known, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: Tomorrow the iniquity of the earth shall be blotted out.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Quem vidístis, * pastóres? dícite, annuntiáte nobis, in terris quis appáruit? Natum vídimus, et choros Angelórum collaudántes Dóminum, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O ye shepherds, speak, * and tell us what ye have seen; who is appeared in the earth? We saw the newborn Child, and angels singing praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.;;129
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.;;131
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos Unigéniti tui nova per carnem Natívitas líberet; quos sub peccáti jugo vetústa sérvitus tenet.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that the new birth of Thine only-begotten Son in the flesh may set us free, who are held by the old bondage under the yoke of sin.

laudes.capitulum.lat: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.

Natum María Vírgine.

Castæ Paréntis víscera

Venter Puéllæ bájulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

Domus pudíci péctoris

Intácta nésciens virum,
Concépit alvo Fílium.

Enítitur puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem ventre Matris géstiens,
Baptísta clausum sénserat.

Fœno jacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Et lacte módico pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.

laudes.hymn.eng:
From lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

Blest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

In that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

The mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

That Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

The manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

The heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Quem lucis ante oríginem
Parem patérnæ glóriæ
Pater suprémus édidit.

Tu lumen, et splendor Patris,
Tu spes perénnis ómnium,
Inténde quas fundunt preces
Tui per orbem sérvuli.

Meménto, rerum Cónditor,
Nostri quod olim córporis,
Sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

Testátur hoc præsens dies,
Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus e sinu Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
Hunc omne, quod cælo subest,
Salútis auctórem novæ
Novo salútat cántico.

Et nos, beáta quos sacri
Rigávit unda sánguinis,
Natális ob diem tui
Hymni tribútum sólvimus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Jesus, the Ransomer of man,
Who, ere created light began,
Didst from the sovereign Father spring,
His power and glory equalling.

The Father’s Light and Splendor Thou,
Their endless hope to Thee that bow;
Accept the prayers and praise to-day
That through the world Thy servants pay.

Salvation’s Author, call to mind
How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,
Thou in man’s flesh becam’st a Child.

Thus testifies the present day,
Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

The heavens above, the rolling main
And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

And we who, by Thy precious Blood
From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

O Lord, the Virgin-born, to Thee
Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: @Tempora/Nat26
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Glory be to God in the highest; * and on earth, peace to men of good will, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Hódie * Christus natus est: hódie Salvátor appáruit: hódie in terra canunt Angeli, lætántur Archángeli: hódie exsúltant justi, dicéntes: Glória in excélsis Deo, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: This day the Christ is born this day the Saviour is appeared; * this day the Angels sing praise in the earth and the Archangels rejoice; this day the righteous are glad and say: Glory to God in the highest. Alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: The Lord hath made known, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: Tomorrow the iniquity of the earth shall be blotted out.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Quem vidístis, * pastóres? dícite, annuntiáte nobis, in terris quis appáruit? Natum vídimus, et choros Angelórum collaudántes Dóminum, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O ye shepherds, speak, * and tell us what ye have seen; who is appeared in the earth? We saw the newborn Child, and angels singing praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

Per quem nec ales ésurit.

Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

In sempitérna sǽcula.

To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

Blest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

In that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

The mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

That Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

The manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

The heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

Tui per orbem sérvuli.

Nostri quod olim córporis,
Sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus e sinu Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
Hunc omne, quod cælo subest,
Salútis auctórem novæ
Novo salútat cántico.

Rigávit unda sánguinis,

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Glória in excélsis Deo, * et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: While all things were in quiet silence * and that night was in the midst of her swift course, thine Almighty Word, O Lord, leapt down out of thy Royal Throne.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Hódie * Christus natus est: hódie Salvátor appáruit: hódie in terra canunt Angeli, lætántur Archángeli: hódie exsúltant justi, dicéntes: Glória in excélsis Deo, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And Jesus advanced in wisdom * and age, and grace with God and men.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: The Word was made flesh, alleluia.
laudes.versicle.engR: And dwelt among us, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: The Word was made flesh, alleluia.
vesperae.versicle.engR: And dwelt among us, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Quem vidístis, * pastóres? dícite, annuntiáte nobis, in terris quis appáruit? Natum vídimus, et choros Angelórum collaudántes Dóminum, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O ye shepherds, speak, * and tell us what ye have seen; who is appeared in the earth? We saw the newborn Child, and angels singing praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.;;129
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.;;131
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:1-2)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Quanto témpore heres párvulus est, nihil differt a servo, cum sit dóminus ómnium: sed sub tutóribus et actóribus est usque ad præfínitum tempus a patre.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers: As long as the heir is a child, he differeth nothing from a servant, though he be lord of all; But is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by the father.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut nos Unigéniti tui nova per carnem Natívitas líberet; quos sub peccáti jugo vetústa sérvitus tenet.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech You, almighty God, that the new birth, in the flesh, of Your only-begotten Son may deliver us whom the bondage of old keeps under the yoke of sin.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
laudes.capitulum.eng: God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:10)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Et: Tu in princípio, Dómine, terram fundásti: et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Owe no man any thing, but to love one another. For he that loveth his neighbour, hath fulfilled the law.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:11-12)
nona.capitulum.lat: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
nona.capitulum.eng: Converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here. Knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things as gold or silver, but with the precious blood of Christ.

Natum María Vírgine.

Servíle corpus índuit:

Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

Venter Puéllæ bájulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

Concépit alvo Fílium.

Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: And very early in the morning * the first day of the week, they come to the sepulchre, the sun being now risen, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And looking * they saw the stone rolled back, for it was very great, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: And his countenance * was as lightning and his raiment as snow, alleluia, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: And for fear of him * the guards were struck with terror and became as dead men, alleluia.
