vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Respóndens autem Angelus, * dixit muliéribus: Nolíte timére: scio enim quod Jesum quǽritis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: And the angel answering * said to the women: Fear not you: for I know that you seek Jesus, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui hodiérna die per Unigénitum tuum æternitátis nobis áditum devícta morte reserásti: vota nostra, quæ præveniéndo aspíras, étiam adjuvándo proséquere.
collect.eng: God, who on this day, through thy Only-begotten Son, overcame death, and opened to us the gate of everlasting life: as by thy anticipating grace, thou breathest good desires into our hearts, so also, by thy gracious help, bring them to good effect.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Jesus junxit se * discípulis suis in via, et ibat cum illis: óculi autem eórum tenebántur, ne eum agnóscerent: et increpávit eos, dicens: O stulti et tardi corde ad credéndum in his, quæ locúti sunt Prophétæ, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: While they walked * Jesus drew near, and went with His disciples: but their eyes were holden that they should not know Him: and He rebuked them, saying: O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the Prophets have spoken! Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Qui sunt hi sermónes * quos confértis ad ínvicem ambulántes, et estis tristes? allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: What manner of communications are these * that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui solemnitáte pascháli, mundo remédia contulísti: pópulum tuum, quǽsumus, cælésti dono proséquere; ut et perféctam libertátem cónsequi mereátur, et ad vitam profíciat sempitérnam.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost heal the sick world by the solemn gladness of the Passover, continue, we beseech thee, to pour forth thine heavenly gifts upon thy people, till the same shall bring them into perfect liberty, and finally avail them unto life everlasting.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Stetit Jesus * in médio discipulórum suórum, et dixit eis: Pax vobis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus stood in the midst of His disciples * and said unto them: Peace be unto you, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Obtulérunt * discípuli Dómino partem piscis assi, et favum mellis, allelúia, allelúia.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Behold My Hands * and my Feet, that it is I myself, alleluia, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam novo semper fœtu multíplicas: concéde fámulis tuis; ut sacraméntum vivéndo téneant, quod fide percepérunt.
collect.eng: O God, Who art ever multiplying the Children of thy Church, grant unto the same thy servants that they may lead the rest of their lives according to this beginning wherein Thou hast given them faith to receive the Sacrament of the New Birth.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Míttite in déxteram * navígii rete, et inveniétis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Cast the net on the right side of the ship, * and ye shall find, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dixit Jesus * discípulis suis: Afférte de píscibus, quos prendidístis nunc. Ascéndit autem Simon Petrus, et traxit rete in terram plenum magnis píscibus, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Jesus saith * unto His disciples: Bring of the fish which ye have now caught. Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui nos resurrectiónis Domínicæ ánnua solemnitáte lætíficas: concéde propítius; ut per temporália festa quæ ágimus, perveníre ad gáudia ætérna mereámur.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost every year fill us with holy gladness for the rising-again of the Lord, mercifully grant that these Feast-days which we are now keeping here in time, may be to us a mean whereby in the end we may worthily attain unto those pleasures which are at thy right hand for evermore.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: María stabat * ad monuméntum plorans, et vidit duos Angelos in albis, sedéntes, et sudárium quod fúerat super caput Jesu, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Mary stood without at the Sepulchre weeping, * and saw two Angels in white, sitting, and the napkin that had been about the Head of Jesus, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Tulérunt Dóminum meum, * et néscio ubi posuérunt eum: si tu sustulísti eum, dícito mihi, allelúja: et ego eum tollam, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: They have taken away my Lord, * and I know not where they have laid Him: if thou have borne Him hence, tell me, alleluia, and I will take Him away, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui diversitátem géntium in confessióne tui nóminis adunásti: da, ut renátis fonte baptísmatis una sit fides méntium et píetas actiónum.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost make all nations, how diverse soever they be, to become one family in giving of praise to thy Name, grant unto all them that are born again in the fountain of baptism to live ever in oneness of faith, and godliness of works.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Undecim discípuli * in Galilǽa vidéntes Dóminum adoravérunt, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When the eleven disciples * saw the Lord in Galilee, they worshipped Him, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Data est mihi * omnis potéstas in cælo et in terra, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: All power is given unto Me * in heaven and in earth, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui paschále sacraméntum in reconciliatiónis humánæ fœ́dere contulísti: da méntibus nostris; ut quod professióne celebrámus, imitémur efféctu.
collect.eng: Almighty and eternal God, in the Easter sacrament thou instituted the covenant, whereby thou forgavest mankind; grant to our souls, that what we outwardly profess we may show forth in our deeds.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Currébant duo simul, * et ille álius discípulus præcucúrrit cítius Petro, et venit prior ad monuméntum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: They ran both together, * and that other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the Sepulchre, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui festa paschália venerándo égimus, per hæc contíngere ad gáudia ætérna mereámur.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who have kept worshipfully the Easter solemnities, may at last worthily pass from keeping Feasts unto thee here to the everlasting jubilation hereafter.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Joann. 5:4)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Omne, quod natum est ex Deo, vincit mundum: et hæc est victória, quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra.
laudes.capitulum.eng: My beloved: For whatsoever is born of God, overcometh the world: and this is the victory which overcometh the world, our faith.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Joann. 5:5-6)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Quis est autem qui vincit mundum, nisi qui credit quóniam Jesus est Fílius Dei? hic est, qui venit per aquam et sánguinem, Jesus Christus: non in aqua solum, sed in aqua et sánguine.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Who is he that overcometh the world, but he that believeth that Jesus is the Son of God? This is he that came by water and blood, Jesus Christ: not by water only, but by water and blood.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Joann. 5:9-10)
nona.capitulum.lat: Si testimónium hóminum accípimus, testimónium Dei majus est: quóniam hoc est testimónium Dei, quod majus est, quóniam testificátus est de Fílio suo. Qui credit in Fílium Dei, habet testimónium Dei in se.
nona.capitulum.eng: If we receive the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater. For this is the testimony of God, which is greater, because he hath testified of his Son. He that believeth in the Son of God, hath the testimony of God in himself.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum esset sero * die illa una sabbatórum, et fores essent clausæ, ubi erant discípuli congregáti in unum, stetit Jesus in médio, et dixit eis: Pax vobis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Now when it was late * the same day, the first of the week, and the doors were shut, where the disciples were gathered together, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst and said to them: Peace be to you, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Post dies octo * jánuis clausis ingréssus Dóminus dixit eis: Pax vobis, allelúja, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: After eight days * came the Lord, the doors being shut, and said unto them: Peace be unto you, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Joann. 5:4)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Omne, quod natum est ex Deo, vincit mundum: et hæc est victória, quæ vincit mundum, fides nostra.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: My beloved: For whatsoever is born of God, overcometh the world: and this is the victory which overcometh the world, our faith.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Surgens Jesus * mane prima sábbati, appáruit primo Maríæ Magdalénæ, de qua ejécerat septem dæmónia, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: He rising * early the first day of the week, appeared first to Mary Magdalen; out of whom he had cast seven devils, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Pax vobis, * ego sum, allelúja: nolíte timére, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Peace be with you, * it is I, alleluia: do not be afraid, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Præcédam vos * in Galilǽam, ibi me vidébitis, sicut dixi vobis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I go before you into Galilee, * there shall ye see Me, as I said unto you. Alleluia, Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Mitte manum tuam, * et cognósce loca clavórum, allelúja: et noli esse incrédulus, sed fidélis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Reach hither thine hand * and feel the print of the nails. Alleluia. And be not faithless but believing. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ego sum vitis vera, * allelúja: et vos pálmites veri, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I am the True Vine. * Alleluia. And ye are My branches indeed.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Quia vidísti me, * Thoma, credidísti: beáti qui non vidérunt, et credidérunt, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Thomas because thou hast seen Me, thou hast believed * blessed are they that have not seen and yet have believed. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ardens est cor meum, * desídero vidére Dóminum meum: quæro, et non invénio, ubi posuérunt eum, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Mine heart is on fire: * I would that I might see my Lord: I seek Him, and know not where they have laid Him. Alleluia, Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Misi dígitum meum * in fixúras clavórum, et manum meam in latus ejus, et dixi: Dóminus meus, et Deus meus, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I have put my finger into the print of the nails, * and my hand into His Side, and I have said: My Lord, and my God! Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Venérunt ad monuméntum * María Magdaléne, et áltera María, vidére sepúlcrum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary * came to see the Sepulchre. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Post dies octo * jánuis clausis ingréssus Dóminus dixit eis: Pax vobis, allelúja, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: After eight days * came the Lord, the doors being shut, and said unto them: Peace be unto you, alleluia, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Illúmine, Dómine * sedéntes in ténebris et umbra mortis, et dírige pedes nostros in viam pacis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: O Lord, give light * to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, and guide our feet into the way of peace

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut qui paschália festa perégimus, hæc, te largiénte, móribus et vita teneámus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech Thee, almighty God, that we who have celebrated the Paschal Feast, may, by Thy bounty, retain its fruits in our daily habits and behaviour.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 2:21-22)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Christus passus est pro nobis, vobis relínquens exémplum ut sequámini vestígia ejus. Qui peccátum non fecit, nec invéntus est dolus in ore ejus.
laudes.capitulum.eng: My beloved: Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example that you should follow his steps. Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 2:23-24)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Tradébat autem judicánti se injúste: qui peccáta nostra ipse pértulit in córpore suo super lignum: ut peccátis mórtui, justítiæ vivámus: cujus livóre sanáti sumus.
sexta.capitulum.eng: He delivered himself to him that judged him unjustly. Who his own self bore our sins in his body upon the tree: that we, being dead to sins, should live to justice: by whose stripes you were healed.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 2:25)
nona.capitulum.lat: Erátis enim sicut oves errántes, sed convérsi estis nunc ad pastórem et epíscopum animárum vestrárum.
nona.capitulum.eng: For you were as sheep going astray; but you are now converted to the shepherd and bishop of your souls.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ego sum pastor óvium: * ego sum via, véritas, et vita: ego sum pastor bonus, et cognósco oves meas, et cognóscunt me meæ, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I am the Shepherd of the Sheep: * I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life: I am the Good Shepherd, and know My Sheep, and am known of Mine. Alleluia, Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ego sum pastor bonus, * qui pasco oves meas, et pro óvibus meis pono ánimam meam, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I am the Good Shepherd, * Who feed My sheep: and I lay down My life for My sheep. Alleluia.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 2:21-22)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Christus passus est pro nobis, vobis relínquens exémplum ut sequámini vestígia ejus. Qui peccátum non fecit, nec invéntus est dolus in ore ejus.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: My beloved: Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example that you should follow his steps. Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui in Fílii tui humilitáte jacéntem mundum erexísti: fidélibus tuis perpétuam concéde lætítiam; ut, quos perpétuæ mortis eripuísti cásibus, gáudiis fácias pérfrui sempitérnis.
collect.eng: O God, Whose Son hath humbled Himself, and Who hast through Him raised up the whole world, grant to thy faithful people everlasting joy; and as Thou hast delivered them from the bitter pains of eternal death, make them to be glad for ever in thy presence.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-1
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Go * into the whole world, alleluia: and teach all the nations, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-1
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The good shepherd * gives his life to his sheep, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui in Fílii tui humilitáte jacéntem mundum erexísti: fidélibus tuis perpétuam concéde lætítiam; ut, quos perpétuæ mortis eripuísti cásibus, gáudiis fácias pérfrui sempitérnis.
collect.eng: O God, Whose Son hath humbled Himself, and Who hast through Him raised up the whole world, grant to thy faithful people everlasting joy; and as Thou hast delivered them from the bitter pains of eternal death, make them to be glad for ever in thy presence.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-2
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Going therefore * teach ye all nations; baptising them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-2
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But the hireling * and he that is not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and flieth: and the wolf catcheth, and scattereth the sheep, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui in Fílii tui humilitáte jacéntem mundum erexísti: fidélibus tuis perpétuam concéde lætítiam; ut, quos perpétuæ mortis eripuísti cásibus, gáudiis fácias pérfrui sempitérnis.
collect.eng: O God, Whose Son hath humbled Himself, and Who hast through Him raised up the whole world, grant to thy faithful people everlasting joy; and as Thou hast delivered them from the bitter pains of eternal death, make them to be glad for ever in thy presence.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gen 49:26)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Benedictiónes patris tui confortátæ sunt benedictiónibus patrum ejus, donec veníret Desidérium cóllium æternórum: fiant in cápite Joseph, et in vértice Nazarǽi inter fratres suos.
laudes.capitulum.eng: The blessings of thy father are strengthened with the blessings of his fathers: until the desire of the everlasting hills should come; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gen 49:25)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Deus patris tui erit adjútor tuus, et Omnípotens benedícet tibi benedictiónibus cæli désuper.
sexta.capitulum.eng: The blessings of thy father are strengthened with the blessings of his fathers: until the desire of the everlasting hills should come; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gen 49:22)
nona.capitulum.lat: Fílius accréscens Joseph, fílius accréscens, et decórus aspéctu: fíliæ discurrérunt super murum.
nona.capitulum.eng: Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough and comely to look upon, whose branches run over the wall.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Cǽlitum Joseph, decus atque nostræ
Certa spes vitæ, columénque mundi,
Quas tibi læti cánimus, benígnus
Súscipe laudes.

Te Sator rerum státuit pudícæ
Vírginis sponsum, voluítque Verbi
Te patrem dici, dedit et minístrum
Esse salútis.

Tu Redemptórem stábulo jacéntem,
Quem chorus Vatum cécinit futúrum,
Aspicis gaudens, humilísque natum
Numen adóras.

Rex Deus regum, Dominátor orbis,
Cujus ad nutum tremit inferórum
Turba, cui pronus famulátur æther,
Se tibi subdit.

Laus sit excélsæ Tríadi perénnis,
Quæ tibi præbens súperos honóres,
Det tuis nobis méritis beátæ
Gáudia vitæ.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
The morn had spread her crimson rays,
When rang the skies with shouts of praise;
Earth joined the joyful hymn to swell,
That brought despair to vanquished hell.

He comes victorious from the grave,
The Lord omnipotent to save,
And brings with him to light of day
The saints who long imprisoned lay.

Vain is the cavern’s three-fold ward —
The stone, the seal, the armed guard;
O death, no more thine arm we fear,
The Victor’s tomb is now thy bier.

Let hymns of joy to grief succeed,
We know that Christ is risen indeed;
We hear his white-robed angel’s voice,
And in our risen Lord rejoice.

With Christ we died, with Christ we rose,
When at the font his name we chose;
Oh, let not sin our robes defile,
And turn to grief the paschal smile.

* To God the Father let us sing,
To God the Son, our risen King,
And equally let us adore
The Spirit, God forevermore.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Te, Joseph, célebrent ágmina cǽlitum,
Te cuncti résonent christíadum chori,
Qui clarus méritis, junctus est ínclitæ
Casto fœ́dere Vírgini.

Almo cum túmidam gérmine cónjugem
Admírans, dúbio tángeris ánxius,
Afflátu súperi Fláminis Angelus
Concéptum Púerum docet.

Tu natum Dóminum stringis, ad éxteras
Ægýpti prófugum tu séqueris plagas;
Amíssum Sólymis quæris, et ínvenis,
Miscens gáudia flétibus.

Post mortem réliquos sors pia cónsecrat,
Palmámque eméritos glória súscipit:
Tu vivens, Súperis par, frúeris Deo,
Mira sorte beátior.

Nobis, summa Trias, parce precántibus,
Da Joseph méritis sídera scándere:
Ut tandem líceat nos tibi pérpetim
Gratum prómere cánticum.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
At the Lamb’s high feast we sing
Praise to our victorious King,
Who hath washed us in the tide
Flowing from his piercèd side.

Praise we him whose love divine
Gives the guests his blood for wine,
Gives his body for the feast,
Love the victim, love the priest.

Where the paschal blood is poured,
Death’s dark angel sheathes his sword;
Israel’s hosts triumphant go
Through the wave that drowns the foe.

Christ, the Lamb whose blood was shed,
Paschal victim, paschal bread;
With sincerity and love
Eat we manna from above.

Mighty victim from the sky,
Powers of hell beneath thee lie;
Death is conquered in the fight;
Thou hast brought us life and light.

Now thy banner thou dost wave;
Vanquished Satan and the grave;
Angels join his praise to tell —
See o’erthrown the prince of hell.

Paschal triumph, paschal joy,
Only sin can this destroy;
From the death of sin set free,
Souls re-born, dear Lord, in Thee.

* Hymns of glory, songs of praise,
Father, unto thee we raise;
Risen Lord, all praise to thee,
Ever with the Spirit be.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Joseph, fili David, * noli timére accípere Maríam cónjugem tuam; quod enim in ea natum est, de Spíritu Sancto est, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Joseph, thou Son of David, * fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife; for That Which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Fili, quid fecísti * nobis sic? Ecce pater tuus et ego doléntes quærebámus te, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Son * why hast Thou thus dealt with us? Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. Alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.lat: Dedísti mihi protectiónem salútis tuæ, allelúja.
laudes.versicle.eng: Thou hast given me the shield of thy salvation, alleluia
laudes.versicle.latR: Et déxtera tua suscépit me, allelúja.
laudes.versicle.engR: And thy right hand hath holden me up, alleluia

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.lat: Sub umbra illíus, quem desideráveram, sedi, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.eng: I sat under His shadow in Whom I delighted. Alleluia.
vesperae.versicle.latR: Et fructus ejus dulcis gútturi meo, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.engR: To my taste. And His fruit was sweet Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph, virum Maríæ, de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: And Jacob begat Joseph, * the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, Who is called Christ. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Missus est * Ángelus Gábriel a Deo in civitátem Galilǽæ, cui nomen Názareth, ad Vírginem desponsátam viro, cui nomen erat Joseph, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Angel Gabriel * was sent from God, unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, to a Virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ascéndit autem * Joseph a Galilǽa de civitáte Názareth in Judǽam, in civitátem David, quæ vocátur Béthlehem, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: And Joseph also went up * from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, unto Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Et venérunt festinántes, * et invenérunt Maríam, et Joseph, et Infántem pósitum in præsépio, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: And they came with haste, * and found Mary and Joseph, and the Babe lying in a manger. Alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Et ipse Jesus * erat incípiens quasi annórum trigínta, ut putabátur, fílius Joseph, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: And Jesus Himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the Son of Joseph. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Jacob autem * génuit Joseph, virum Maríæ, de qua natus est Jesus, qui vocátur Christus, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: And Jacob begat Joseph, * the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, Who is called Christ. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Angel Gabriel * was sent from God, unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth, to a Virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ascéndit autem * Joseph a Galilǽa de civitáte Názareth in Judǽam, in civitátem David, quæ vocátur Béthlehem, allelúja.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: And they came with haste, * and found Mary and Joseph, and the Babe lying in a manger. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Et ipse Jesus * erat incípiens quasi annórum trigínta, ut putabátur, fílius Joseph, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: And Jesus Himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the Son of Joseph. Alleluia.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gen 49:26)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Benedictiónes patris tui confortátæ sunt benedictiónibus patrum ejus, donec veníret Desidérium cóllium æternórum: fiant in cápite Joseph, et in vértice Nazarǽi inter fratres suos.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: The blessings of thy father are strengthened with the blessings of his fathers: until the desire of the everlasting hills should come; may they be upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the Nazarite among his brethren

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui ineffábili providéntia beátum Joseph sanctíssimæ Genitrícis tuæ sponsum elígere dignátus es: præsta, quǽsumus; ut quem protectórem venerámur in terris, intercessórem habére mereámur in cælis:
collect.eng: God, Who in thine unspeakable foreknowledge didst choose thy blessed servant Joseph to be the husband of thine Own most holy Mother; mercifully grant that now that he is in heaven with thee, we who on earth do reverence him for our Defender, may worthily be holpen by the succour of his prayers to thee on our behalf;

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 2:11)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Obsecro vos tamquam ádvenas et peregrínos abstinére vos a carnálibus desidériis, quæ mílitant advérsus ánimam.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 2:13-14)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Subjécti ígitur estóte omni humánæ creatúræ propter Deum: sive regi quasi præcellénti: sive dúcibus tamquam ab eo missis ad vindíctam malefactórum, laudem vero bonórum.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Be ye subject therefore to every human creature for God's sake: whether it be to the king as excelling; Or to governors as sent by him for the punishment of evildoers, and for the praise of the good.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 2:18-19)
nona.capitulum.lat: Servi, súbditi estóte in omni timóre dóminis, non tantum bonis et modéstis, sed étiam dýscolis. Hæc est enim grátia in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
nona.capitulum.eng: Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward. For this is thankworthy, if for conscience towards God, a man endure sorrows, suffering wrongfully.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Módicum * et non vidébitis me, dicit Dóminus: íterum módicum, et vidébitis me, quia vado ad Patrem, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: A little while * and you shall not see me; and again a little while, and you shall see me, saith the Lord, because I go to the Father, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Amen dico vobis, * quia plorábitis et flébitis vos: mundus autem gaudébit, vos vero contristabímini, sed tristítia vestra convertétur in gáudium, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Amen, amen I say to you * that you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice; and you shall be made sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 2:11)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Obsecro vos tamquam ádvenas et peregrínos abstinére vos a carnálibus desidériis, quæ mílitant advérsus ánimam.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui errántibus, ut in viam possint redíre justítiæ, veritátis tuæ lumen osténdis: da cunctis, qui christiána professióne censéntur, et illa respúere, quæ huic inimíca sunt nómini; et ea, quæ sunt apta, sectári.
collect.eng: Almighty God, Who showest to them that be in error the light of thy truth, to the intent that they may return into the way of righteousness grant unto all them that are admitted into the fellowship of Christ's Religion, that they may eschew those things that are contrary to their profession, and follow all such things as are agreeable to the same.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Et intrávit * cum illis: et factum est, dum recumberet cum illis, accépit panem, et benedíxit, ac fregit, et porrigébat illis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: And He went in with them. * And it came to pass, as He sat at meat with them, He took bread, and blessed it and brake, and gave to them. Alleluia, Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Amen, amen dico vobis, * íterum vidébo vos, et gaudébit cor vestrum, et gáudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Amen, Amen, I say unto you, that I will see you again, * am your heart shall rejoice, and your jo; no man taketh from you. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui errántibus, ut in viam possint redíre justítiæ, veritátis tuæ lumen osténdis: da cunctis, qui christiána professióne censéntur, et illa respúere, quæ huic inimíca sunt nómini; et ea, quæ sunt apta, sectári.
collect.eng: Almighty God, Who showest to them that be in error the light of thy truth, to the intent that they may return into the way of righteousness grant unto all them that are admitted into the fellowship of Christ's Religion, that they may eschew those things that are contrary to their profession, and follow all such things as are agreeable to the same.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cognovérunt * Dóminum Jesum, allelúja, in fractióne panis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: They knew the Lord Jesus * Alin the breaking of bread Alleluia Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: @Tempora/Pasc3-0
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Amen, amen I say to you * that you shall lament and weep, but the world shall rejoice; and you shall be made sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui errántibus, ut in viam possint redíre justítiæ, veritátis tuæ lumen osténdis: da cunctis, qui christiána professióne censéntur, et illa respúere, quæ huic inimíca sunt nómini; et ea, quæ sunt apta, sectári.
collect.eng: Almighty God, Who showest to them that be in error the light of thy truth, to the intent that they may return into the way of righteousness grant unto all them that are admitted into the fellowship of Christ's Religion, that they may eschew those things that are contrary to their profession, and follow all such things as are agreeable to the same.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Jas 1:17)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Omne datum óptimum, et omne donum perféctum desúrsum est, descéndens a Patre lúminum, apud quem non est transmutátio, nec vicissitúdinis obumbrátio.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Beloved: Every best gift, and every perfect gift, is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change, nor shadow of alteration.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Jas 1:19-20)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Scitis, fratres mei dilectíssimi. Sit autem omnis homo velox ad audiéndum: tardus autem ad loquéndum, et tardus ad iram. Ira enim viri justítiam Dei non operátur.
sexta.capitulum.eng: You know, my dearest brethren. And let every man be swift to hear, but slow to speak, and slow to anger. For the anger of man worketh not the justice of God.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Jas 1:21)
nona.capitulum.lat: Propter quod abiciéntes omnem immundítiam, et abundántiam malítiæ, in mansuetúdine suscípite ínsitum verbum, quod potest salváre ánimas vestras.
nona.capitulum.eng: Wherefore casting away all uncleanness, and abundance of naughtiness, with meekness receive the ingrafted word, which is able to save your souls.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Iterum autem * vidébo vos, et gaudébit cor vestrum, allelúja, et gáudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I go My way to Him That sent Me, * and none of you asketh Me: Whither goest Thou? Alleluia, Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Vado ad eum * qui misit me: sed quia hæc locútus sum vobis, tristítia implévit cor vestrum, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I go My way to Him That sent Me, * but because I have said this to you, sadness has filled your hearts, alleluia.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Jas 1:17)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Omne datum óptimum, et omne donum perféctum desúrsum est, descéndens a Patre lúminum, apud quem non est transmutátio, nec vicissitúdinis obumbrátio.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Beloved: Every best gift, and every perfect gift, is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no change, nor shadow of alteration.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.
collect.eng: O God, of Whom it cometh that the minds of thy faithful people be all of one will, grant unto the same thy people that they may love the thing which Thou commandest, and desire that which Thou dost promise, that so, amid the sundry and manifold changes of the world, our hearts may surely there be fixed, where true joys are to be found.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-1
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Did not our heart burn within us, at the thought of Jesus, * while he talked with us by the way? Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-1
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I tell you the truth: * it is expedient for you that I go away, for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-2
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Peace be unto you, * it is I, alleluia; fear not, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-2
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: When the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, is come, * He will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.
collect.eng: O God, of Whom it cometh that the minds of thy faithful people be all of one will, grant unto the same thy people that they may love the thing which Thou commandest, and desire that which Thou dost promise, that so, amid the sundry and manifold changes of the world, our hearts may surely there be fixed, where true joys are to be found.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-3
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: A spirit hath not flesh and bones, * as ye see Me to have: now believe. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-3
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. * Howbeit, when He, the Spirit of truth, is come, He will guide you into all truth. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.
collect.eng: O God, of Whom it cometh that the minds of thy faithful people be all of one will, grant unto the same thy people that they may love the thing which Thou commandest, and desire that which Thou dost promise, that so, amid the sundry and manifold changes of the world, our hearts may surely there be fixed, where true joys are to be found.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-4
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The disciples gave the Lord a piece * of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-4
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: For He shall not speak of Himself; * but whatsoever He shall hear, that shall He speak and He will show you things to come, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.
collect.eng: O God, of Whom it cometh that the minds of thy faithful people be all of one will, grant unto the same thy people that they may love the thing which Thou commandest, and desire that which Thou dost promise, that so, amid the sundry and manifold changes of the world, our hearts may surely there be fixed, where true joys are to be found.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: @Tempora/Pasc1-5
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: These are the words * which I spake unto you, while I was with you. Alleluia, Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Vado ad eum * qui misit me: sed quia hæc locútus sum vobis, tristítia implévit cor vestrum, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I go My way to Him That sent Me, * but because I have said this to you, sadness has filled your hearts, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.
collect.eng: O God, of Whom it cometh that the minds of thy faithful people be all of one will, grant unto the same thy people that they may love the thing which Thou commandest, and desire that which Thou dost promise, that so, amid the sundry and manifold changes of the world, our hearts may surely there be fixed, where true joys are to be found.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Jac 1:22-24)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Estóte factóres verbi, et non auditóres tantum: falléntes vosmetípsos. Quia si quis audítor est verbi, et non factor, hic comparábitur viro consideránti vultum nativitátis suæ in spéculo: considerávit enim se, et ábiit, et statim oblítus est qualis fúerit.
laudes.capitulum.eng: My beloved: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves. For if a man be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he shall be compared to a man beholding his own countenance in a glass. For he beheld himself, and went his way, and presently forgot what manner of man he was.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Jas 1:25)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Qui autem perspéxerit in legem perféctam libertátis, et permánserit in ea, non audítor obliviósus factus, sed factor operis: hic beátus in facto suo erit.
sexta.capitulum.eng: But he that hath looked into the perfect law of liberty, and hath continued therein, not becoming a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work; this man shall be blessed in his deed.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Jas 1:27)
nona.capitulum.lat: Relígio munda et immaculáta apud Deum et Patrem, hæc est: visitáre pupíllos et víduas in tribulatióne eórum, et immaculátum se custodíre ab hoc sǽculo.
nona.capitulum.eng: Religion clean and undefiled before God and the Father, is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their tribulation: and to keep one's self unspotted from this world.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Usque modo * non petístis quidquam in nómine meo: pétite, et accipiétis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Hitherto * have ye asked nothing in My Name, ask, and ye shall receive. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Pétite, et accipiétis, * ut gáudium vestrum sit plenum: ipse enim Pater amat vos, quia vos me amástis, et credidístis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Ask, and ye shall receive, * that your joy may be full; for the Father Himself loveth you, because ye have loved Me, and have believed in Me, alleluia.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Jac 1:22-24)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Estóte factóres verbi, et non auditóres tantum: falléntes vosmetípsos. Quia si quis audítor est verbi, et non factor, hic comparábitur viro consideránti vultum nativitátis suæ in spéculo: considerávit enim se, et ábiit, et statim oblítus est qualis fúerit.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: My beloved: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves. For if a man be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he shall be compared to a man beholding his own countenance in a glass. For he beheld himself, and went his way, and presently forgot what manner of man he was.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, a quo bona cuncta procédunt, largíre supplícibus tuis: ut cogitémus, te inspiránte, quæ recta sunt; et, te gubernánte, éadem faciámus.
collect.eng: O God, from Whom all good things do come, grant to us thy humble servants that by thy holy inspiration we may think those things that be good, and by thy merciful guiding may perform the same.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Pétite, et accipiétis: * quǽrite, et inveniétis: pulsáte, et aperiétur vobis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Ask, and ye shall receive; * seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ipse enim Pater amat * vos, quia vos me amástis, et credidístis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The Father Himself loveth you, * because ye have loved Me, and have believed in Me. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, a quo bona cuncta procédunt, largíre supplícibus tuis: ut cogitémus, te inspiránte, quæ recta sunt; et, te gubernánte, éadem faciámus.
collect.eng: O God, from Whom all good things do come, grant to us thy humble servants that by thy holy inspiration we may think those things that be good, and by thy merciful guiding may perform the same.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Oportébat * pati Christum, et resúrgere a mórtuis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Christ ought to have suffered, * and to have risen again from the dead. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Exívi a Patre, * et veni in mundum: íterum relínquo mundum, et vado ad Patrem, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I came forth from the Father, * and am come into the world; again I leave the world, and go to the Father. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, a quo bona cuncta procédunt, largíre supplícibus tuis: ut cogitémus, te inspiránte, quæ recta sunt; et, te gubernánte, éadem faciámus.
collect.eng: O God, from Whom all good things do come, grant to us thy humble servants that by thy holy inspiration we may think those things that be good, and by thy merciful guiding may perform the same.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Pater, venit hora, * clarífica Fílium tuum claritáte quam hábui, priúsquam mundus esset, apud te, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Father, the hour is come, * glorify thy Son, with the glory which I had, before the world was, with thee, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, a quo bona cuncta procédunt, largíre supplícibus tuis: ut cogitémus, te inspiránte, quæ recta sunt; et, te gubernánte, éadem faciámus.
collect.eng: O God, from Whom all good things do come, grant to us thy humble servants that by thy holy inspiration we may think those things that be good, and by thy merciful guiding may perform the same.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Act. 1:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Primum quidem sermónem feci de ómnibus, o Theóphile, quæ cœpit Jesus fácere et docére usque in diem, qua præcípiens Apóstolis per Spíritum Sanctum, quos elégit, assúmptus est.
laudes.capitulum.eng: The former treatise I made, O Theophilus, of all things which Jesus began to do and to teach, Until the day on which, giving commandments by the Holy Ghost to the apostles whom he had chosen, he was taken up.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Act. 1:4-5)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Et convéscens, præcépit eis, ab Jerosólymis ne discéderent, sed exspectárent promissiónem Patris, quam audístis (inquit) per os meum: quia Joánnes quidem baptizávit aqua, vos autem baptizabímini Spíritu Sancto non post multos hos dies.
sexta.capitulum.eng: And eating together with them, he commanded them, that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but should wait for the promise of the Father, which you have heard (saith he) by my mouth. For John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost, not many days hence.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Act. 1:11)
nona.capitulum.lat: Viri Galilǽi, quid statis aspiciéntes in cælum? Hic Jesus qui assúmptus est a vobis in cælum, sic véniet, quemádmodum vidístis eum eúntem in cælum.
nona.capitulum.eng: Ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up to heaven? This Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, as you have seen him going into heaven.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Jesu, volúptas córdium
Orbis redémpti Cónditor,
Et casta lux amántium:

Qua victus es cleméntia,
Ut nostra ferres crímina?
Mortem subíres ínnocens,
A morte nos ut tólleres?

Perrúmpis inférnum chaos:
Vinctis caténas détrahis;
Victor triúmpho nóbili
Ad déxteram Patris sedes.

Te cogat indulgéntia,
Ut damna nostra sárcias,
Tuíque vultus cómpotes
Dites beáto lúmine.

Tu, dux ad astra, et sémita,
Sis meta nostris córdibus,
Sis lacrimárum gáudium,
Sis dulce vitæ prǽmium.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Hail, thou who man's Redeemer art,
Jesu, the joy of every heart;
Great Maker of the world's wide frame,
And purest love's delight and flame:

What nameless mercy thee o'ercame,
To bear our load of sin and shame?
For guiltless, thou thy life didst give,
That sinful erring man might live.

The realms of woe are forced by thee,
Its captives from their chains set free;
And thou, amid thy ransomed train,
At God's right hand dost victor reign.

Let mercy sweet with thee prevail,
To cure the wounds we now bewail;
Oh, bless us with thy holy sight,
And fill us with eternal light.

Our guide, our way to heavenly rest,
Be thou the aim of every breast;
Be thou the soother of our tears,
Our sweet reward above the spheres.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I ascend to my Father * and to your Father: to my God and your God, alleluia.

collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui hodiérna die Unigénitum tuum, Redemptórem nostrum, ad cælos ascendísse crédimus; ipsi quoque mente in cæléstibus habitémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that just as we do believe thine Only-Begotten Son, our Saviour, to have this day ascended into the heavens, so we may also in heart and mind thither ascend, and with Him continually dwell.

collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui hodiérna die Unigénitum tuum, Redemptórem nostrum, ad cælos ascendísse crédimus; ipsi quoque mente in cæléstibus habitémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that just as we do believe thine Only-Begotten Son, our Saviour, to have this day ascended into the heavens, so we may also in heart and mind thither ascend, and with Him continually dwell.

sexta.capitulum.eng: And eating together with them, he commanded them, that they should not depart from Jerusalem, but should wait for the promise of the Father, which you have heard (saith he) by my mouth. For John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost, not many days hence.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Act. 1:11)
nona.capitulum.lat: Viri Galilǽi, quid statis aspiciéntes in cælum? Hic Jesus qui assúmptus est a vobis in cælum, sic véniet, quemádmodum vidístis eum eúntem in cælum.
nona.capitulum.eng: Ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up to heaven? This Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, as you have seen him going into heaven.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Jesu, volúptas córdium
Orbis redémpti Cónditor,
Et casta lux amántium:

Qua victus es cleméntia,
Ut nostra ferres crímina?
Mortem subíres ínnocens,
A morte nos ut tólleres?

Perrúmpis inférnum chaos:
Vinctis caténas détrahis;
Victor triúmpho nóbili
Ad déxteram Patris sedes.

Te cogat indulgéntia,
Ut damna nostra sárcias,
Tuíque vultus cómpotes
Dites beáto lúmine.

Tu, dux ad astra, et sémita,
Sis meta nostris córdibus,
Sis lacrimárum gáudium,
Sis dulce vitæ prǽmium.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Hail, thou who man's Redeemer art,
Jesu, the joy of every heart;
Great Maker of the world's wide frame,
And purest love's delight and flame:

What nameless mercy thee o'ercame,
To bear our load of sin and shame?
For guiltless, thou thy life didst give,
That sinful erring man might live.

The realms of woe are forced by thee,
Its captives from their chains set free;
And thou, amid thy ransomed train,
At God's right hand dost victor reign.

Let mercy sweet with thee prevail,
To cure the wounds we now bewail;
Oh, bless us with thy holy sight,
And fill us with eternal light.

Our guide, our way to heavenly rest,
Be thou the aim of every breast;
Be thou the soother of our tears,
Our sweet reward above the spheres.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ascéndo ad Patrem meum, * et Patrem vestrum: Deum meum, et Deum vestrum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I ascend to my Father * and to your Father: to my God and your God, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: O Rex glóriæ, * Dómine virtútum, qui triumphátor hódie super omnes cælos ascendísti, ne derelínquas nos órphanos; sed mitte promíssum Patris in nos, Spíritum veritátis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: O King of glory, Lord of hosts, * Who hast this day exalted thine Own Self, with great triumph, above all the heavens, leave us not orphans but send unto us the Promise of the Father, even the Spirit of truth, alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: The Lord in heaven, alleluia.
laudes.versicle.engR: Hath prepared his throne, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Cumque intueréntur * in cælum eúntem illum, dixérunt, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: And while they looked * steadfastly towards heaven, as He went up, they said, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Elevátis mánibus, * benedíxit eis, et ferebátur in cælum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: He lifted up His Hands, * and blessed them, and was carried up into heaven, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Exaltáte Regem regum, * et hymnum dícite Deo, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Extol the King of kings, * and ascribe praise to God, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Vidéntibus illis, * elevátus est, et nubes suscépit eum in cælo, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: While they beheld, * He was taken up, and a cloud received Him in heaven, alleluia.

laudes.capitulum.eng: My beloved: Be prudent, therefore, and watch in prayers. But before all things have a constant mutual charity among yourselves: for charity covereth a multitude of sins.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Petri 4:7-8)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Hospitáles ínvicem sine murmuratióne. Unusquísque, sicut accépit grátiam, in altérutrum illam administrántes, sicut boni dispensatóres multifórmis grátiæ Dei.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Using hospitality one towards another, without murmuring, as every man hath received grace, ministering the same one to another: as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Petri 4:11)
nona.capitulum.lat: Si quis lóquitur, quasi sermónes Dei: si quis minístrat, tamquam ex virtúte, quam adminístrat Deus: ut in ómnibus honorificétur Deus per Jesum Christum, Dóminum nostrum.
nona.capitulum.eng: If any man speak, let him speak, as the words of God. If any man minister, let him do it, as of the power, which God administereth: that in all things God may be honoured through Jesus Christ our Lord.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum vénerit Paráclitus, * quem ego mittam vobis Spíritum veritátis, qui a Patre procédit, ille testimónium perhibébit de me, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: But when the Comforter is come * Whom I will send unto you from the Father, He shall testify of Me, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Hæc locútus sum * vobis, ut cum vénerit hora eórum, reminiscámini quia ego dixi vobis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: These things have I told * you, that, when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them, alleluia.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Jesu, volúptas córdium
Orbis redémpti Cónditor,
Et casta lux amántium:

Qua victus es cleméntia,
Ut nostra ferres crímina?
Mortem subíres ínnocens,
A morte nos ut tólleres?

Perrúmpis inférnum chaos:
Vinctis caténas détrahis;
Victor triúmpho nóbili
Ad déxteram Patris sedes.

Te cogat indulgéntia,
Ut damna nostra sárcias,
Tuíque vultus cómpotes
Dites beáto lúmine.

Tu, dux ad astra, et sémita,
Sis meta nostris córdibus,
Sis lacrimárum gáudium,
Sis dulce vitæ prǽmium.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Hail, thou who man's Redeemer art,
Jesu, the joy of every heart;
Great Maker of the world's wide frame,
And purest love's delight and flame:

What nameless mercy thee o'ercame,
To bear our load of sin and shame?
For guiltless, thou thy life didst give,
That sinful erring man might live.

The realms of woe are forced by thee,
Its captives from their chains set free;
And thou, amid thy ransomed train,
At God's right hand dost victor reign.

Let mercy sweet with thee prevail,
To cure the wounds we now bewail;
Oh, bless us with thy holy sight,
And fill us with eternal light.

Our guide, our way to heavenly rest,
Be thou the aim of every breast;
Be thou the soother of our tears,
Our sweet reward above the spheres.
Amen.
