collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus: fac nos tibi semper et devótam gérere voluntátem; et majestáti tuæ sincéro corde servíre.
collect.eng: O Almighty and everlasting God, grant that our will be ever meekly subject unto thy will, and our heart ever honestly ready to serve thy majesty.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Act. 2:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Cum compleréntur dies Pentecóstes, erant omnes discípuli páriter in eódem loco: et factus est repénte de cælo sonus, tamquam adveniéntis spíritus veheméntis, et replévit totam domum, ubi erant sedéntes.
laudes.capitulum.eng: When the day of Pentecost was fully come, the disciples were all with one accord in one place and suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a rushing mighty wind and it filled all the house where they were sitting.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Act. 2:6)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Facta autem hac voce, convénit multitúdo, et mente confúsa est, quóniam audiébat unusquísque lingua sua illos loquéntes.
sexta.capitulum.eng: When this was noised abroad, the multitude came together, and were confounded, because that every man heard them speak in his own language.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Act. 2:11)
nona.capitulum.lat: Judǽi quoque et Prosélyti, Cretes et Arabes: audívimus eos loquéntes nostris linguis magnália Dei.
nona.capitulum.eng: Jews also, and Proselytes, Cretes and Arabians, we do hear them speak in our tongues the wonderful works of God.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Anni redúxit órbita,
Cum Spíritus Paráclitus
Illápsus est Apóstolis.

Ignis vibránte lúmine
Linguæ figúram détulit,
Verbis ut essent próflui,
Et caritáte férvidi.

Linguis loquúntur ómnium;
Turbæ pavent Gentílium,
Musto madére députant
Quos Spíritus repléverat.

Patráta sunt hæc mýstice,
Paschæ perácto témpore,
Sacro diérum círculo,
Quo lege fit remíssio.

Te nunc, Deus piíssime,
Vultu precámur cérnuo:
Illápsa nobis cǽlitus
Largíre dona Spíritus.

Dudum sacráta péctora
Tua replésti grátia:
Dimítte nostra crímina,
Et da quiéta témpora.

* Deo Patri sit glória,
Et Fílio, qui a mórtuis
Surréxit, ac Paráclito,
In sæculórum sǽcula.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Round roll the weeks our hearts to greet,
With blissful joy returning;
For lo! the Holy Paraclete
On twelve bright brows sits burning:

With quivering flame he lights on each,
In fashion like a tongue, to teach
That eloquent they are of speech,
Their hearts with true love yearning.

While with all tongues they speak to all,
The nations deem them maddened,
And drunk with wine the prophets call,
Whom God's good Spirit gladdened;

A marvel this—in mystery done—
The holy paschaltide outrun,
By numbers told, whose reckoning won
Remission for the saddened.

O God most Holy, thee we pray,
With reverent brow low bending,
Grant us the Spirit's gifts today
The gifts from heaven descending;

And, since, thy grace hath deigned to bide
Within our breasts once sanctified,
Deign, Lord, to cast our sins aside,
Henceforth calm seasons sending.

To God the Father, laud and praise,
Praise to the Son be given;
Praise to the Spirit of all grace,
The fount of graces seven—

As was of old, all worlds before,
Is now and shall be evermore,
When time and change are spent and o'er
All praise in earth and heaven.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat: @Psalterium/Special/Minor Special:Hymnus Pasc7 Tertia
vesperae.hymn.eng:
/:The first verse of the following hymn is said genuflecting.:/
v. Creator Spirit, all Divine,
Come, visit every soul of Thine,
And fill with Thy celestial flame
The hearts which Thou Thyself didst frame.

O gift of God, Thine is the sweet
Consoling name of Paraclete
And spring of life and fire and love
And unction flowing from above.

The mystic sevenfold gifts are Thine,
Finger of God's right hand divine;
The Father's promise sent to teach
The tongue a rich and heavenly speech.

Kindle with fire brought from above
Each sense, and fill our hearts with love;
And grant our flesh, so weak and frail,
The strength of Thine which cannot fail.

Drive far away our deadly foe,
And grant us Thy true peace to know;
So we, led by Thy guidance still,
May safely pass through every ill.

To us, through Thee, the grace be shown
To know the Father and the Son;
And Spirit of Them both, may we
Forever rest our faith in Thee.

To Sire and Son be praises meet,
And to the Holy Paraclete;
And may Christ send us from above
That Holy Spirit's gift of love.
Amen

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Accípite * Spíritum Sanctum: quorum remiséritis peccáta, remittúntur eis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Receive ye the Holy Ghost; * whoseoever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Hódie * compléti sunt dies Pentecóstes, allelúja: hódie Spíritus Sanctus in igne discípulis appáruit, et tríbuit eis charísmatum dona: misit eos in univérsum mundum prædicáre, et testificári: Qui credíderit et baptizátus fúerit, salvus erit, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: This day * the day of Pentecost is fully come, alleluia. This day the Holy Ghost appeared in fire unto the disciples, and gave unto them gifts of grace. He sent them into all the world, to preach and to testify that he who believeth, and is baptized, shall be saved, alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.lat: Repléti sunt omnes Spíritu Sancto, allelúja.
laudes.versicle.eng: They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, alleluia.
laudes.versicle.engR: And began to speak, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: The Apostles spoke in diverse tongues, alleluia.
vesperae.versicle.engR: The wonderful works of God, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Cum compleréntur * dies Pentecóstes, erant omnes páriter in eódem loco, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: When the day of Pentecost was fully come * they were all with one accord in one place, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Spíritus Dómini * replévit orbem terrárum, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Spirit of the Lord * filleth the world, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Repléti sunt omnes * Spíritu Sancto, et cœpérunt loqui, allelúja, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: They were all filled * with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Fontes, et ómnia * quæ movéntur in aquis, hymnum dícite Deo, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: See ye fountains, * and all that move in the waters, ascribe ye praise to God, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Loquebántur * váriis linguis Apóstoli magnália Dei, allelúja, allelúja, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The Apostles spoke in diverse tongues * the wonderful works of God, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Act. 2:1-2)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Cum compleréntur dies Pentecóstes, erant omnes discípuli páriter in eódem loco: et factus est repénte de cælo sonus, tamquam adveniéntis spíritus veheméntis, et replévit totam domum, ubi erant sedéntes.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: When the day of Pentecost was fully come, the disciples were all with one accord in one place and suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a rushing mighty wind and it filled all the house where they were sitting.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui hodiérna die corda fidélium Sancti Spíritus illustratióne docuísti: da nobis in eódem Spíritu recta sápere; et de ejus semper consolatióne gaudére.
collect.eng: O God, Who on this day didst teach the hearts of thy faithful people, by the sending to them the light of thine Holy Spirit, grant us by the same Spirit to have a right judgment in all things, and evermore to rejoice in His holy comfort.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Sic Deus * diléxit mundum, ut Fílium suum unigénitum daret: ut omnis, qui credit in ipsum, non péreat, sed hábeat vitam ætérnam, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: God so loved the world * that He gave His Only-begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Si quis díligit me, * sermónem meum servábit; et Pater meus díliget eum, et ad eum veniémus, et mansiónem apud eum faciémus, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: If a Man love Me * he will keep My word and My Father will love him, and We will come unto him, and make Our abode with him. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Apóstolis tuis Sanctum dedísti Spíritum: concéde plebi tuæ piæ petitiónis efféctum; ut, quibus dedísti fidem, largiáris et pacem.
collect.eng: O God, Who didst give thine Holy Spirit unto thine Apostles, grant unto thy people the effectual fruit of their godly supplications, and as Thou hast given them faith, give them also peace.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ego sum óstium, * dicit Dóminus: per me si quis introíerit, salvábitur, et páscua invéniet, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I am the Door * saith the Lord, by Me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall find pasture. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Pacem * relínquo vobis, pacem meam do vobis: non quómodo mundus dat, ego do vobis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Peace I leave with you, * My peace I give unto you; not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Adsit nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, virtus Spíritus Sancti: quæ et corda nostra cleménter expúrget, et ab ómnibus tueátur advérsis.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, that thy Holy Spirit may dwell in us in much power, mercifully cleansing our hearts, and shielding us from all things hurtful.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ego sum panis vivus, * dicit Dóminus, qui de cælo descéndi, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I am the Living Bread * Which came down from heaven, saith the Lord. Alleluia, Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ego sum panis vivus, * dicit Dóminus, qui de cælo descéndi: si quis manducáverit ex hoc pane, vivet in ætérnum: et panis, quem ego dabo, caro mea est pro mundi vita, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I am the Living Bread Which came down from heaven; * if any man eat of this Bread, he shall live for ever, and the Bread that I will give is My Flesh, Which I will give for the life of the world. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Mentes nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, Paráclitus, qui a te procédit, illúminet: et indúcat in omnem, sicut tuus promísit Fílius, veritátem:
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, that the Comforter, Which proceeded from thee, may enlighten our minds, and lead us into all truth, even as thy Son hath promised unto us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Convocátis Jesus * duódecim discípulis suis, dedit illis virtútem et potestátem super ómnia dæmónia, et ut languóres curárent: et misit illos prædicáre regnum Dei, et sanáre infírmos, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus called His twelve disciples * together, * and gave them power and authority over all devils, and to cure diseases and He sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Spíritus, * qui a Patre procédit, allelúja: ille me clarificábit, allelúja, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The Comforter, * Which proceedeth from the Father, alleluia, He shall glorify Me, alleluia, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui hodiérna die corda fidélium Sancti Spíritus illustratióne docuísti: da nobis in eódem Spíritu recta sápere; et de ejus semper consolatióne gaudére.
collect.eng: O God, Who on this day didst teach the hearts of thy faithful people, by the sending to them the light of thine Holy Spirit, grant us by the same Spirit to have a right judgment in all things, and evermore to rejoice in His holy comfort.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dixit Jesus: * Ut sciátis autem quia Fílius hóminis habet potestátem in terra dimitténdi peccáta, ait paralýtico: Tibi dico, surge: tolle lectum tuum, et vade in domum tuam, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: But that ye may know * that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, He said unto the sick of the palsy: I say unto thee, Arise, take up thy couch, and go into thine house. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Paráclitus autem * Spíritus Sanctus, quem mittet Pater in nómine meo, ille vos docébit ómnia, et súggeret vobis ómnia, quæcúmque díxero vobis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But the Comforter which is the Holy Ghost, * Whom the Father will send in My Name, He shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Da, quǽsumus, Ecclésiæ tuæ, miséricors Deus: ut, Sancto Spíritu congregáta, hostíli nullátenus incursióne turbétur.
collect.eng: O most merciful God, we beseech thee to grant unto thy Church that, forasmuch as she is gathered together in the Holy Ghost, no assaults of her enemies may be able to trouble her.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cáritas Dei * diffúsa est in córdibus nostris, per inhabitántem Spíritum ejus in nobis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The charity of God * is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost, who is given to us.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Méntibus nostris, quǽsumus, Dómine, Spíritum Sanctum benígnus infúnde: cujus et sapiéntia cónditi sumus, et providéntia gubernámur.
collect.eng: We beseech Thee, O Lord, mercifully to pour into our hearts Thy Holy Spirit, by Whose Wisdom we have been created, and by Whose Providence all our ways are ordered.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Rom 11:33)
laudes.capitulum.lat: O Altitúdo divitiárum sapiéntiæ, et sciéntiæ Dei, quam incomprehensibília sunt judícia ejus, et investigábiles viæ ejus!
laudes.capitulum.eng: O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments, and how unsearchable his ways!

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Tu, Trinitátis Unitas,
Orbem poténter quæ regis,
Atténde laudis cánticum,
Quod excubántes psállimus.

Ortus refúlget Lúcifer,
Præítque solem núntius:
Cadunt ténebræ nóctium:
Lux sancta nos illúminet.

Deo Patri sit glória,
Ejúsque soli Fílio,
Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
Nunc, et per omne sǽculum.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
O thou, who dost all nature sway,
Dread Trinity in Unity,
Accept the trembling praise we pay
To thy eternal majesty.

The star that heralds in the dawn
Is slowly fading in the skies;
The darkness melts; O thou true light,
Upon our darkened souls arise.

To God the Father glory be,
And to the sole-begotten Son,
And Holy Ghost co-equally,
While everlasting ages run.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Tu, lux perénnis, Únitas,
Nostris, beáta Trínitas,
Infúnde lumen córdibus.

Te mane laudum cármine,
Te deprecámur véspere;
Dignéris ut te súpplices
Laudémus inter cǽlites.

Patri, simúlque Fílio,
Tibíque, Sancte Spíritus,
Sicut fuit, sit júgiter
Sæclum per omne glória.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
As fades the glowing orb of day,
To thee, great source of light, we pray;
Blest Three in One, to every heart
Thy beams of life and love impart.

At early dawn, at close of day,
To thee our vows we humbly pay;
May we, mid joys that never end,
With thy bright saints in homage bend.

To God the Father, and the Son,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One,
Be endless glory, as before
The world began, so evermore.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Benedícta sit * sancta creátrix et gubernátrix ómnium, sancta et indivídua Trínitas, nunc, et semper, et per infiníta sǽcula sæculórum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Blessed be the Holy One * the Maker and Lord of all things. Blessed be the Holy and Undivided Trinity, now and always, and unto unending ages of ages.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Te Deum * Patrem ingénitum, te Fílium unigénitum, te Spíritum Sanctum Paráclitum, sanctam et indivíduam Trinitátem, toto corde et ore confitémur, laudámus, atque benedícimus: tibi glória in sǽcula.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: With all our heart * and with all our voice do we acknowledge thee, praise thee, and bless thee, O God the Father the Unbegotten, O God the Only-Begotten Son, O God the Holy Ghost the Comforter, One Holy and Undivided Trinity, To thee be glory for ever.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.lat: Benedicámus Patrem et Fílium cum Sancto Spíritu.
laudes.versicle.eng: Bless we the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost.
laudes.versicle.latR: Laudémus et superexaltémus eum in sǽcula.
laudes.versicle.engR: Let us praise Him and exalt Him above all for ever.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.lat: Benedíctus es, Dómine, in firmaménto cæli.
vesperae.versicle.eng: Bless we the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Ghost.
vesperae.versicle.latR: Et laudábilis et gloriósus in sǽcula.
vesperae.versicle.engR: Let us praise Him and exalt Him above all for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Glória tibi, Trínitas * æquális, una Déitas, et ante ómnia sǽcula, et nunc et in perpétuum.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Glory be to thee, O equal Trinity * one Deity, from before all ages, so now and for evermore.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Laus et perénnis glória * Deo Patri, et Fílio, Sancto simul Paráclito, in sæculórum sǽcula.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Praise and endless glory be * to God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Paraclete, for ever and ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Glória laudis * résonet in ore ómnium, Patri, genitǽque Proli, Spirítui Sancto páriter resúltet laude perénni.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Let the glory of praise * be heard from the mouth of all to the Father, and to the begotten Son; let it equally resound with perpetual praise to the Holy Spirit.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Laus Deo Patri, * parilíque Proli, et tibi, Sancte, stúdio perénni, Spíritus, nostro résonet ab ore, omne per ævum.;;112
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Praise be to God the Father, * and to his co-equal Son, and to thee, O Holy Ghost: with perpetual delight may it resound from our lips for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Ex quo ómnia, * per quem ómnia, in quo ómnia: ipsi glória in sǽcula.;;116
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: From whom are all things, * through whom are all things, and in whom are all things: to him be glory for evermore.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Rom 11:33)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: O Altitúdo divitiárum sapiéntiæ, et sciéntiæ Dei, quam incomprehensibília sunt judícia ejus, et investigábiles viæ ejus!
vesperae.capitulum.eng: O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God! How incomprehensible are his judgments, and how unsearchable his ways!

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui dedísti fámulis tuis in confessióne veræ fídei, ætérnæ Trinitátis glóriam agnóscere, et in poténtia majestátis adoráre Unitátem: quǽsumus; ut, ejúsdem fídei firmitáte, ab ómnibus semper muniámur advérsis.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, you have given thy servants in the confession of the true faith, to acknowledge the glory of the Eternal Trinity, and to adore the unity in the power of thy Majesty; grant, that by steadfastness in this faith we may ever be defended from all adversities.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 11:23-24)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Ego enim accépi a Dómino quod et trádidi vobis, quóniam Dóminus Jesus, in qua nocte tradebátur, accépit panem, et grátias agens fregit, et dixit: Accípite et manducáte: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur: hoc fácite in meam commemoratiónem.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread. And giving thanks, broke, and said: Take ye, and eat: this is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this do for the commemoration of me.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 11:26)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Quotiescúmque enim manducábitis panem hunc, et cálicem bibétis, mortem Dómini annuntiábitis donec véniat.
sexta.capitulum.eng: As often as ye eat this Bread, and drink this Cup, ye do show the Lord's death till He come.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 11:27)
nona.capitulum.lat: Quicúmque manducáverit panem hunc, vel bíberit cálicem Dómini indígne, reus erit córporis et sánguinis Dómini.
nona.capitulum.eng: Whosoever shall eat this bread, or drink the chalice of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Nec Patris linquens déxteram,
Ad opus suum éxiens,
Venit ad vitæ vésperam.

In mortem a discípulo
Suis tradéndus ǽmulis,
Prius in vitæ férculo
Se trádidit discípulis.

Quibus sub bina spécie
Carnem dedit et sánguinem;
Ut dúplicis substántiæ
Totum cibáret hóminem.

Se nascens dedit sócium,
Convéscens in edúlium,
Se móriens in prétium,
Se regnans dat in prǽmium.

O salutáris hóstia,
Quæ cæli pandis óstium,
Bella premunt hostília;
Da robur, fer auxílium.

Uni trinóque Dómino,
Sit sempitérna glória:
Qui vitam sine término
Nobis donet in pátria.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
The heav'nly Word proceeding forth,
Yet leaving not the Father's side,
And going to his work on earth
Had reached at length life's eventide.

By false disciple to be given
To foemen for his blood athirst,
Himself, the living bread from heaven,
He gave to his disciples first.

To them he gave, in twofold kind,
His very flesh, his very blood:
In love's own fullness thus designed
Of the whole man to be the food.

By birth, our fellow-man was he;
Our meat, while sitting at the board;
He died, our ransomer to be;
He ever reigns, our great reward.

O saving victim, opening wide
The gate of heaven to man below,
Our foes press on from every side,
Thine aid supply, thy strength bestow.

To thy great name be endless praise,
Immortal Godhead, One in Three;
O grant us endless length of days
In our true native land, with thee.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Córporis mystérium,
Sanguinísque pretiósi,
Quem in mundi prétium
Fructus ventris generósi
Rex effúdit géntium.

Nobis datus, nobis natus
Ex intácta Vírgine,
Et in mundo conversátus,
Sparso verbi sémine,
Sui moras incolátus
Miro clausit órdine.

In suprémæ nocte cenæ
Recúmbens cum frátribus,
Observáta lege plene
Cibis in legálibus,
Cibum turbæ duodénæ
Se dat suis mánibus.

Verbum caro, panem verum
Verbo carnem éfficit;
Fitque sanguis Christi merum:
Et si sensus déficit,
Ad firmándum cor sincérum
Sola fides súfficit.

!Sequens stropha, si coram Sanctissimo exposito Officium persolvatur, dicitur flexis genibus.

Tantum ergo Sacraméntum
Venerémur cérnui:
Et antíquum documéntum
Novo cedat rítui:

And the Son who reigns on high,
With the Holy Ghost proceeding
Forth from each eternally,
Be salvation, honour, blessing,
Might, and endless majesty.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ego sum * panis vivus, qui de cælo descéndi: si quis manducáverit ex hoc pane, vivet in ætérnum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I am the living Bread Which came down from heaven; * if any man eat of this Bread, he shall live for ever, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: O sacrum convívium, * in quo Christus súmitur: recólitur memória passiónis ejus: mens implétur grátia: et futúræ glóriæ nobis pignus datur, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Holy exceedingly is the Supper of the Lord, * wherein we do feed on Christ, do show His death till He come, do get grace abundantly to our souls, and do take pledge of the glory which shall hereafter be revealed in us, alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: He maketh peace in thy borders, alleluia.
laudes.versicle.latR: Et ádipe fruménti sátiat te, allelúja.
laudes.versicle.engR: And filleth thee with the finest of wheat, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.lat: Panem de cælo præstitísti eis, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.eng: Thou didst send them from heaven, alleluia.
vesperae.versicle.latR: Omne delectaméntum in se habéntem, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.engR: Bread able to content every man's delight, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Sapiéntia * ædificávit sibi domum, míscuit vinum et pósuit mensam, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Wisdom hath builded her house, * she hath mingled her wine, she hath also furnished her table, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Angelórum esca * nutrivísti pópulum tuum, et panem de cælo præstitísti eis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Thou feddest thine Own people * with Angels' food, and didst send them bread from heaven, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Pinguis est panis * Christi, et præbébit delícias régibus, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Out of Christ His bread shall be fat, * and He shall yield royal dainties, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Sacerdótes sancti * incénsum et panes ófferunt Deo, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The Priests shall be holy; * for the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and the bread of their God, they do offer, [therefore they shall be holy], alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Vincénti dabo * manna abscónditum, et nomen novum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: To him that overcometh will I give of the hidden manna, * and will give him a new name, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Sacérdos in ætérnum * Christus Dóminus secúndum órdinem Melchísedech, panem et vinum óbtulit.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Christ the Lord, being made an High Priest for ever * after the order of Melchisedec, hath offered bread and wine.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Miserátor Dóminus * escam dedit timéntibus se in memóriam suórum mirabílium.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: He hath made His wonderful works to be remembered; * the Lord is gracious and full of compassion. He hath given meat unto them that fear Him.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Cálicem salutáris * accípiam: et sacrificábo hóstiam laudis.;;115
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: I will take the cup of salvation, * and offer the sacrifice of thanksgiving.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Sicut novéllæ olivárum, * Ecclésiæ fílii sint in circúitu mensæ Dómini.;;127
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Let the children of the Church be like olive-plants * round about the table of the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Qui pacem * ponit fines Ecclésiæ, fruménti ádipe sátiat nos Dóminus.;;147
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The Lord, That maketh peace in the borders of the Church, * filleth her with the finest of the wheat.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 11:23-24)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Ego enim accépi a Dómino quod et trádidi vobis, quóniam Dóminus Jesus, in qua nocte tradebátur, accépit panem, et grátias agens fregit, et dixit: Accípite et manducáte: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur: hoc fácite in meam commemoratiónem.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread. And giving thanks, broke, and said: Take ye, and eat: this is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this do for the commemoration of me.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui nobis sub Sacraménto mirábili passiónis tuæ memóriam reliquísti: tríbue, quǽsumus, ita nos Córporis, et Sánguinis tui sacra mystéria venerári; ut redemptiónis tuæ fructum in nobis júgiter sentiámus:
collect.eng: O God, under a marvelous sacrament you have left us the memorial of thy Passion; grant us, we beseech thee, so to venerate the sacred mysteries of thy Body and Blood, that we may ever perceive within us the fruit of thy Redemption.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Joann. 3:13-14)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Nolíte mirári, si odit vos mundus. Nos scimus quóniam transláti sumus de morte ad vitam, quóniam dilígimus fratres.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Wonder not, brethren, if the world hate you. We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not, abideth in death.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Joann. 3:16)
sexta.capitulum.lat: In hoc cognóvimus caritátem Dei: quóniam ille ánimam suam pro nobis pósuit, et nos debémus pro frátribus ánimas pónere.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Hereby perceive we the love of God, because He laid down His life for us and we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Joann. 3:18)
nona.capitulum.lat: Filíoli mei, non diligámus verbo neque lingua, sed ópere et veritáte.
nona.capitulum.eng: My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue, but in deed, and in truth.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Córporis mystérium,
Sanguinísque pretiósi,
Quem in mundi prétium
Fructus ventris generósi
Rex effúdit géntium.

Nobis datus, nobis natus
Ex intácta Vírgine,
Et in mundo conversátus,
Sparso verbi sémine,
Sui moras incolátus
Miro clausit órdine.

In suprémæ nocte cenæ
Recúmbens cum frátribus,
Observáta lege plene
Cibis in legálibus,
Cibum turbæ duodénæ
Se dat suis mánibus.

Verbum caro, panem verum
Verbo carnem éfficit;
Fitque sanguis Christi merum:
Et si sensus déficit,
Ad firmándum cor sincérum
Sola fides súfficit.

!Sequens stropha, si coram Sanctissimo exposito Officium persolvatur, dicitur flexis genibus.

Tantum ergo Sacraméntum
Venerémur cérnui:
Et antíquum documéntum
Novo cedat rítui:
Præstet fides suppleméntum
Sénsuum deféctui.

Genitóri, Genitóque
Laus et jubilátio,
Salus, honor, virtus quoque
Sit et benedíctio:
Procedénti ab utróque
Compar sit laudátio.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Sing, my tongue, the Saviour's glory,
Of his flesh the mystery sing;
Of the blood, all price exceeding,
Shed by our immortal King,
Destined, for the world's redemption,
From a noble womb to spring.

Of a pure and spotless Virgin
Born for us on earth below,
He, as man, with man conversing,
Stayed, the seeds of truth to sow;
Then he closed in solemn order
Wondrously his life of woe.

On the night of that last supper
Seated with his chosen band,
He, the paschal victim eating,
First fulfills the law's command:
Then as food to all his brethren
Gives himself with his own hand.

Word made flesh, the bread of nature
By his word to flesh he turns;
Wine into his blood he changes:
What though sense no change discerns?
Only be the heart in earnest,
Faith her lesson quickly learns.

!If the Office is celebrated before the exposed Blessed Sacrament, the following verses are said on bended knee.

Down in adoration falling,
Lo! the sacred Host we hail;
Lo! o'er ancient forms departing,
Newer rites of grace prevail;
Faith for all defects supplying,
Where the feeble senses fail.

To the everlasting Father,
And the Son who reigns on high,
With the Holy Ghost proceeding
Forth from each eternally,
Be salvation, honour, blessing,
Might, and endless majesty.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Homo quidam * fecit cenam magnam, et vocávit multos: et misit servum suum hora cenæ dícere invitátis ut venírent, quia ómnia paráta sunt, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: A certain man made a great supper, * and bade many and sent his servant at suppertime to say to them that were bidden: Come, for all things are now ready.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Exi cito * in platéas et vicos civitátis: et páuperes ac débiles, cæcos et claudos compélle intráre, ut impleátur domus mea, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Go out quickly into the streets * and lanes of the city, and compel the poor and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind, to come in that my house may be full, alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: He gave them of the bread of heaven, alleluia.
laudes.versicle.engR: Man did eat Angels' bread, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.lat: Cibávit illos ex ádipe fruménti, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.eng: He fed them with the finest of the wheat. Alleluia.
vesperae.versicle.latR: Et de petra, melle saturávit eos, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.engR: And with honey out of the rock did He satisfy them. Alleluia.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Joann. 3:13-14)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi: Nolíte mirári, si odit vos mundus. Nos scimus quóniam transláti sumus de morte ad vitam, quóniam dilígimus fratres.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Wonder not, brethren, if the world hate you. We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not, abideth in death.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Sancti nóminis tui, Dómine, timórem páriter et amórem fac nos habére perpétuum: quia nunquam tua gubernatióne destítuis, quos in soliditáte tuæ dilectiónis instítuis.
collect.eng: O Lord, Who never failest to help and govern them whom Thou dost bring up in thy steadfast fear and love keep us, we beseech thee, under the protection of thy good providence, and make us to have a perpetual fear and love of thy Holy Name.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 11:23-24)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Ego enim accépi a Dómino quod et trádidi vobis, quóniam Dóminus Jesus, in qua nocte tradebátur, accépit panem, et grátias agens fregit, et dixit: Accípite et manducáte: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur: hoc fácite in meam commemoratiónem.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread. And giving thanks, broke, and said: Take ye, and eat: this is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this do for the commemoration of me.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 11:26)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Quotiescúmque enim manducábitis panem hunc, et cálicem bibétis, mortem Dómini annuntiábitis donec véniat.
sexta.capitulum.eng: As often as ye eat this Bread, and drink this Cup, ye do show the Lord's death till He come.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 11:27)
nona.capitulum.lat: Quicúmque manducáverit panem hunc, vel bíberit cálicem Dómini indígne, reus erit córporis et sánguinis Dómini.
nona.capitulum.eng: Whosoever shall eat this bread, or drink the chalice of the Lord unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and of the blood of the Lord.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Nec Patris linquens déxteram,
Ad opus suum éxiens,
Venit ad vitæ vésperam.

In mortem a discípulo
Suis tradéndus ǽmulis,
Prius in vitæ férculo
Se trádidit discípulis.

Quibus sub bina spécie
Carnem dedit et sánguinem;
Ut dúplicis substántiæ
Totum cibáret hóminem.

Se nascens dedit sócium,
Convéscens in edúlium,
Se móriens in prétium,
Se regnans dat in prǽmium.

O salutáris hóstia,
Quæ cæli pandis óstium,
Bella premunt hostília;
Da robur, fer auxílium.

Uni trinóque Dómino,
Sit sempitérna glória:
Qui vitam sine término
Nobis donet in pátria.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
The heav'nly Word proceeding forth,
Yet leaving not the Father's side,
And going to his work on earth
Had reached at length life's eventide.

By false disciple to be given
To foemen for his blood athirst,
Himself, the living bread from heaven,
He gave to his disciples first.

To them he gave, in twofold kind,
His very flesh, his very blood:
In love's own fullness thus designed
Of the whole man to be the food.

By birth, our fellow-man was he;
Our meat, while sitting at the board;
He died, our ransomer to be;
He ever reigns, our great reward.

O saving victim, opening wide
The gate of heaven to man below,
Our foes press on from every side,
Thine aid supply, thy strength bestow.

To thy great name be endless praise,
Immortal Godhead, One in Three;
O grant us endless length of days
In our true native land, with thee.
Amen.

Carnem dedit et sánguinem;
Ut dúplicis substántiæ
Totum cibáret hóminem.

Convéscens in edúlium,
Se móriens in prétium,
Se regnans dat in prǽmium.

O salutáris hóstia,
Quæ cæli pandis óstium,
Bella premunt hostília;
Da robur, fer auxílium.

Sit sempitérna glória:
Qui vitam sine término
Nobis donet in pátria.

Yet leaving not the Father's side,
And going to his work on earth
Had reached at length life's eventide.

To foemen for his blood athirst,

He gave to his disciples first.

To them he gave, in twofold kind,
His very flesh, his very blood:
In love's own fullness thus designed
Of the whole man to be the food.

By birth, our fellow-man was he;
Our meat, while sitting at the board;
He died, our ransomer to be;
He ever reigns, our great reward.

The gate of heaven to man below,
Our foes press on from every side,
Thine aid supply, thy strength bestow.

Immortal Godhead, One in Three;

In our true native land, with thee.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus

Córporis mystérium,
Sanguinísque pretiósi,
Quem in mundi prétium
Fructus ventris generósi
Rex effúdit géntium.

Nobis datus, nobis natus
Ex intácta Vírgine,
Et in mundo conversátus,
Sparso verbi sémine,
Sui moras incolátus
Miro clausit órdine.

In suprémæ nocte cenæ
Recúmbens cum frátribus,
Observáta lege plene
Cibis in legálibus,
Cibum turbæ duodénæ
Se dat suis mánibus.

Verbum caro, panem verum
Verbo carnem éfficit;
Fitque sanguis Christi merum:
Et si sensus déficit,
Ad firmándum cor sincérum
Sola fides súfficit.

Venerémur cérnui:

Novo cedat rítui:
Præstet fides suppleméntum
Sénsuum deféctui.

Genitóri, Genitóque
Laus et jubilátio,
Salus, honor, virtus quoque
Sit et benedíctio:
Procedénti ab utróque
Compar sit laudátio.
Amen.

Sing, my tongue, the Saviour's glory,
Of his flesh the mystery sing;
Of the blood, all price exceeding,
Shed by our immortal King,
Destined, for the world's redemption,
From a noble womb to spring.

Of a pure and spotless Virgin
Born for us on earth below,
He, as man, with man conversing,
Stayed, the seeds of truth to sow;
Then he closed in solemn order
Wondrously his life of woe.

Seated with his chosen band,
He, the paschal victim eating,
First fulfills the law's command:
Then as food to all his brethren
Gives himself with his own hand.

By his word to flesh he turns;
Wine into his blood he changes:
What though sense no change discerns?
Only be the heart in earnest,
Faith her lesson quickly learns.

Might, and endless majesty.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Wisdom hath builded her house, * she hath mingled her wine, she hath also furnished her table, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Angelórum esca * nutrivísti pópulum tuum, et panem de cælo præstitísti eis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Thou feddest thine Own people * with Angels' food, and didst send them bread from heaven, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Pinguis est panis * Christi, et præbébit delícias régibus, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Out of Christ His bread shall be fat, * and He shall yield royal dainties, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Sacerdótes sancti * incénsum et panes ófferunt Deo, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The Priests shall be holy; * for the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and the bread of their God, they do offer, [therefore they shall be holy], alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Vincénti dabo * manna abscónditum, et nomen novum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: To him that overcometh will I give of the hidden manna, * and will give him a new name, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Christ the Lord, being made an High Priest for ever * after the order of Melchisedec, hath offered bread and wine.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Miserátor Dóminus * escam dedit timéntibus se in memóriam suórum mirabílium.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: He hath made His wonderful works to be remembered; * the Lord is gracious and full of compassion. He hath given meat unto them that fear Him.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Cálicem salutáris * accípiam: et sacrificábo hóstiam laudis.;;115
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: I will take the cup of salvation, * and offer the sacrifice of thanksgiving.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Let the children of the Church be like olive-plants * round about the table of the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Qui pacem * ponit fines Ecclésiæ, fruménti ádipe sátiat nos Dóminus.;;147
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The Lord, That maketh peace in the borders of the Church, * filleth her with the finest of the wheat.

He ever reigns, our great reward.

O saving victim, opening wide
The gate of heaven to man below,
Our foes press on from every side,
Thine aid supply, thy strength bestow.

To thy great name be endless praise,
Immortal Godhead, One in Three;
O grant us endless length of days
In our true native land, with thee.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Córporis mystérium,
Sanguinísque pretiósi,
Quem in mundi prétium
Fructus ventris generósi
Rex effúdit géntium.

Nobis datus, nobis natus
Ex intácta Vírgine,
Et in mundo conversátus,
Sparso verbi sémine,
Sui moras incolátus
Miro clausit órdine.

In suprémæ nocte cenæ
Recúmbens cum frátribus,
Observáta lege plene
Cibis in legálibus,
Cibum turbæ duodénæ
Se dat suis mánibus.

Verbum caro, panem verum
Verbo carnem éfficit;
Fitque sanguis Christi merum:
Et si sensus déficit,
Ad firmándum cor sincérum
Sola fides súfficit.

!Sequens stropha, si coram Sanctissimo exposito Officium persolvatur, dicitur flexis genibus.

Tantum ergo Sacraméntum
Venerémur cérnui:
Et antíquum documéntum
Novo cedat rítui:
Præstet fides suppleméntum
Sénsuum deféctui.

Genitóri, Genitóque
Laus et jubilátio,
Salus, honor, virtus quoque
Sit et benedíctio:
Procedénti ab utróque
Compar sit laudátio.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Sing, my tongue, the Saviour's glory,
Of his flesh the mystery sing;
Of the blood, all price exceeding,
Shed by our immortal King,
Destined, for the world's redemption,
From a noble womb to spring.

Of a pure and spotless Virgin
Born for us on earth below,
He, as man, with man conversing,
Stayed, the seeds of truth to sow;
Then he closed in solemn order
Wondrously his life of woe.

On the night of that last supper
Seated with his chosen band,
He, the paschal victim eating,
First fulfills the law's command:
Then as food to all his brethren
Gives himself with his own hand.

Word made flesh, the bread of nature
By his word to flesh he turns;
Wine into his blood he changes:
What though sense no change discerns?
Only be the heart in earnest,
Faith her lesson quickly learns.

!If the Office is celebrated before the exposed Blessed Sacrament, the following verses are said on bended knee.

Down in adoration falling,
Lo! the sacred Host we hail;
Lo! o'er ancient forms departing,
Newer rites of grace prevail;
Faith for all defects supplying,
Where the feeble senses fail.

To the everlasting Father,
And the Son who reigns on high,
With the Holy Ghost proceeding
Forth from each eternally,
Be salvation, honour, blessing,
Might, and endless majesty.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ego sum * panis vivus, qui de cælo descéndi: si quis manducáverit ex hoc pane, vivet in ætérnum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I am the living Bread Which came down from heaven; * if any man eat of this Bread, he shall live for ever, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: O sacrum convívium, * in quo Christus súmitur: recólitur memória passiónis ejus: mens implétur grátia: et futúræ glóriæ nobis pignus datur, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Holy exceedingly is the Supper of the Lord, * wherein we do feed on Christ, do show His death till He come, do get grace abundantly to our souls, and do take pledge of the glory which shall hereafter be revealed in us, alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: He maketh peace in thy borders, alleluia.
laudes.versicle.latR: Et ádipe fruménti sátiat te, allelúja.
laudes.versicle.engR: And filleth thee with the finest of wheat, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.lat: Panem de cælo præstitísti eis, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.eng: Thou didst send them from heaven, alleluia.
vesperae.versicle.latR: Omne delectaméntum in se habéntem, allelúja.
vesperae.versicle.engR: Bread able to content every man's delight, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Sapiéntia * ædificávit sibi domum, míscuit vinum et pósuit mensam, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Wisdom hath builded her house, * she hath mingled her wine, she hath also furnished her table, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Angelórum esca * nutrivísti pópulum tuum, et panem de cælo præstitísti eis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Thou feddest thine Own people * with Angels' food, and didst send them bread from heaven, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Pinguis est panis * Christi, et præbébit delícias régibus, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Out of Christ His bread shall be fat, * and He shall yield royal dainties, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Sacerdótes sancti * incénsum et panes ófferunt Deo, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: The Priests shall be holy; * for the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and the bread of their God, they do offer, [therefore they shall be holy], alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Vincénti dabo * manna abscónditum, et nomen novum, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: To him that overcometh will I give of the hidden manna, * and will give him a new name, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Sacérdos in ætérnum * Christus Dóminus secúndum órdinem Melchísedech, panem et vinum óbtulit.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Christ the Lord, being made an High Priest for ever * after the order of Melchisedec, hath offered bread and wine.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Miserátor Dóminus * escam dedit timéntibus se in memóriam suórum mirabílium.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: He hath made His wonderful works to be remembered; * the Lord is gracious and full of compassion. He hath given meat unto them that fear Him.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Cálicem salutáris * accípiam: et sacrificábo hóstiam laudis.;;115
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: I will take the cup of salvation, * and offer the sacrifice of thanksgiving.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Sicut novéllæ olivárum, * Ecclésiæ fílii sint in circúitu mensæ Dómini.;;127
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Let the children of the Church be like olive-plants * round about the table of the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Qui pacem * ponit fines Ecclésiæ, fruménti ádipe sátiat nos Dóminus.;;147
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The Lord, That maketh peace in the borders of the Church, * filleth her with the finest of the wheat.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 11:23-24)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Ego enim accépi a Dómino quod et trádidi vobis, quóniam Dóminus Jesus, in qua nocte tradebátur, accépit panem, et grátias agens fregit, et dixit: Accípite et manducáte: hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis tradétur: hoc fácite in meam commemoratiónem.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread. And giving thanks, broke, and said: Take ye, and eat: this is my body, which shall be delivered for you: this do for the commemoration of me.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui nobis sub Sacraménto mirábili passiónis tuæ memóriam reliquísti: tríbue, quǽsumus, ita nos Córporis, et Sánguinis tui sacra mystéria venerári; ut redemptiónis tuæ fructum in nobis júgiter sentiámus:
collect.eng: O God, under a marvelous sacrament you have left us the memorial of thy Passion; grant us, we beseech thee, so to venerate the sacred mysteries of thy Body and Blood, that we may ever perceive within us the fruit of thy Redemption.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:8-9)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brethren: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; and to make all men see what is the fellowship of the Mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:14-17)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Hujus rei grátia flecto génua mea ad Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, ut det vobis secúndum divítias glóriæ suæ virtúte corroborári per Spíritum ejus in interiórem hóminem: Christum habitáre per fidem in córdibus vestris.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:17-19)
nona.capitulum.lat: In caritáte radicáti et fundáti, ut possítis comprehéndere cum ómnibus sanctis, quæ sit latitúdo et longitúdo, et sublímitas et profúndum; scire étiam supereminéntem sciéntiæ caritátem Christi, ut impleámini in omnem plenitúdinem Dei.
nona.capitulum.eng: Being rooted and grounded in love, may ye be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height: and to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fullness of God.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Cor, arca legem cóntinens
Non servitútis véteris,
Sed grátiæ, sed véniæ,
Sed et misericórdiæ.

Cor, sanctuárium novi
Intemerátum fœ́deris,
Templum vetústo sánctius,
Velúmque scisso utílius.

Te vulnerátum cáritas
Ictu paténti vóluit,
Amóris invisíbilis
Ut venerémur vúlnera.

Hoc sub amóris sýmbolo
Passus cruénta et mýstica,
Utrúmque sacrifícium
Christus sacérdos óbtulit.

Quis non amántem rédamet?
Quis non redémptus díligat,
Et Corde in isto séligat
Ætérna tabernácula?

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui Corde fundis grátiam,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Jesus, behind thy temple's veil,
Hid in an ark of gold,
On stones engraven, lay the law
thy finger wrote of old.

But in thy body's temple new,
thy life-blood's throbbing shrine,
Held, upon fleshly tables graved,
The law of love divine.

And when that heart in death was stilled,
Each temple's veil was riven:
And lo, within thy love's red shrine,
To us to look was given.

There make us gaze and see the love
Which drew thee, for our sake,
O great high-priest, thyself to God
A sacrifice to make.

Thou, Saviour, cause that every soul
Which thou hast loved so well,
May will within thine open heart
In life and death to dwell.

Grant it, O Father, only Son,
And Spirit, God of grace,
To whom all worship shall be done,
In every time and place.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
En, ut supérba críminum
Et sæva nostrórum cohors
Cor sauciávit ínnocens
Meréntis haud tale Dei!

Vibrántis hastam mílitis
Peccáta nostra dírigunt,
Ferrúmque diræ cúspidis
Mortále crimen ácuit.

Ex Corde scisso Ecclésia,
Christo jugáta, náscitur:
Hoc óstium arcæ in látere est
Genti ad salútem pósitum.

Ex hoc perénnis grátia,
Ceu septifórmis flúvius,
Stolas ut illic sórdidas
Lavémus Agni in sánguine.

Turpe est redíre ad crímina,
Quæ Cor beátum lácerent:
Sed æmulémur córdibus
Flammas amóris índices.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui Corde fundis grátiam,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Lo, how the savage crew
Of our proud sins hath rent
The heart of our all-gracious God,
That heart so innocent.

The soldier's quivering lance
Our guilt it was that drave,
Our wicked deeds that to its point
Such cruel sharpness gave.

O wounded heart, whence sprang
The Church, the Saviour's bride;
Thou door of our salvation's ark
Set in its mystic side.

Thou holy fount, whence flows
The sacred sevenfold flood,
Where we our filthy robes may cleanse
In the Lamb's saving blood:

By sorrowful relapse,
thee will we rend no more;
But like the flames, those types of love,
Strive heavenward to soar.

Father and Son supreme
And Spirit, hear our cry;
Whose is the kingdom, praise and power,
Through all eternity.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Facta sunt * enim hæc ut Scriptúra implerétur quæ dicit: Vidébunt in quem transfixérunt.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: For these things were done * that the Scripture should be fulfilled which saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ad Jesum autem * cum veníssent, ut vidérunt eum jam mórtuum, non fregérunt ejus crura, sed unus mílitum láncea latus ejus apéruit et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But when they came to Jesus * and saw that he was dead already, they broke not his legs, but one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out Blood and Water.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: With joy shall ye draw water.
laudes.versicle.engR: Out of the fountains of the Saviour.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: With joy shall ye draw water.
vesperae.versicle.engR: Out of the fountains of the Saviour.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Unus mílitum * láncea latus ejus apéruit et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: One of the soldiers * with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out Blood and Water.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Stans Jesus * clamábat dicens: Si quis sitit, véniat ad me et bibat.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Jesus stood * and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: In caritáte perpétua * diléxit nos Deus, ídeo, exaltátus a terra, attráxit nos ad Cor suum, míserans.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: With an everlasting love * hath God loved us, and from the day that he was lifted up over the earth, he hath drawn us with loving-kindness unto his Heart.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Veníte ad me * omnes qui laborátis et oneráti estis et ego refíciam vos.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Come unto me, * all ye that travail and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Fili, * præbe mihi cor tuum, et óculi tui custódiant vias meas.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: My son, * give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Suávi jugo tuo * domináre, Dómine, in médio inimicórum tuórum.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Put thy easy yoke * upon all mankind, O Lord, and be thou ruler, even in the midst of thine enemies.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Miséricors * et miserátor Dóminus: escam dedit timéntibus se.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: This merciful * and gracious Lord hath given Meat unto them that fear him..

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis; miséricors et miserátor Dóminus.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Unto the godly * there ariseth up light in the darkness, even the Lord merciful and gracious.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Quid retríbuam * Dómino pro ómnibus quæ retríbuit mihi?;;115
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: What reward shall I give * unto the Lord for all the benefits that he hath done unto me?

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Apud Dóminum * propitiátio est et copiósa apud eum redémptio.;;129
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:8-9)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brethren: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; and to make all men see what is the fellowship of the Mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui nobis in Corde Fílii tui, nostris vulneráto peccátis, infinítos dilectiónis thesáuros misericórditer largíri dignáris; concéde, quǽsumus, ut illi devótum pietátis nostræ præstántes obséquium, dignæ quoque satisfactiónis exhibeámus offícium.
collect.eng: O God, who hast suffered the Heart of thy Son to be wounded by our sins, and in that very Heart hast bestowed on us the abundant riches of thy love: grant that the devout homage of our hearts, which we render unto him, may of thy mercy be deemed a recompence acceptable in thy sight.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:8-9)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brethren: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; and to make all men see what is the fellowship of the Mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:14-17)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Hujus rei grátia flecto génua mea ad Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, ut det vobis secúndum divítias glóriæ suæ virtúte corroborári per Spíritum ejus in interiórem hóminem: Christum habitáre per fidem in córdibus vestris.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:17-19)
nona.capitulum.lat: In caritáte radicáti et fundáti, ut possítis comprehéndere cum ómnibus sanctis, quæ sit latitúdo et longitúdo, et sublímitas et profúndum; scire étiam supereminéntem sciéntiæ caritátem Christi, ut impleámini in omnem plenitúdinem Dei.
nona.capitulum.eng: Being rooted and grounded in love, may ye be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height: and to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fullness of God.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: With an everlasting love * hath God loved us, and from the day that he was lifted up over the earth, he hath drawn us with loving-kindness unto his Heart.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Veníte ad me * omnes qui laborátis et oneráti estis et ego refíciam vos.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Come unto me, * all ye that travail and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Fili, * præbe mihi cor tuum, et óculi tui custódiant vias meas.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: My son, * give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Suávi jugo tuo * domináre, Dómine, in médio inimicórum tuórum.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Put thy easy yoke * upon all mankind, O Lord, and be thou ruler, even in the midst of thine enemies.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Miséricors * et miserátor Dóminus: escam dedit timéntibus se.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: This merciful * and gracious Lord hath given Meat unto them that fear him..

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis; miséricors et miserátor Dóminus.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Unto the godly * there ariseth up light in the darkness, even the Lord merciful and gracious.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Quid retríbuam * Dómino pro ómnibus quæ retríbuit mihi?;;115
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: What reward shall I give * unto the Lord for all the benefits that he hath done unto me?

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Apud Dóminum * propitiátio est et copiósa apud eum redémptio.;;129
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:8-9)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brethren: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; and to make all men see what is the fellowship of the Mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui nobis in Corde Fílii tui, nostris vulneráto peccátis, infinítos dilectiónis thesáuros misericórditer largíri dignáris; concéde, quǽsumus, ut illi devótum pietátis nostræ præstántes obséquium, dignæ quoque satisfactiónis exhibeámus offícium.
collect.eng: O God, who hast suffered the Heart of thy Son to be wounded by our sins, and in that very Heart hast bestowed on us the abundant riches of thy love: grant that the devout homage of our hearts, which we render unto him, may of thy mercy be deemed a recompence acceptable in thy sight.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 5:6-7)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Caríssimi, humiliámini sub poténti manu Dei, ut vos exáltet in témpore visitatiónis; omnem sollicitúdinem vestram proiciéntes in eum, quóniam ipsi cura est de vobis.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Dearly beloved, humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time: casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 5:8-9)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Sóbrii estóte, et vigiláte: quia adversárius vester diábolus tamquam leo rúgiens círcuit, quærens quem dévoret: cui resístite fortes in fide, sciéntes eámdem passiónem ei, quæ in mundo est, vestræ fraternitáti fíeri.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Pet 5:10-11)
nona.capitulum.lat: Deus autem omnis grátiæ, qui vocávit nos in ætérnam suam glóriam in Christo Jesu, módicum passos ipse perfíciet, confirmábit solidabítque. Ipsi glória et impérium in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
nona.capitulum.eng: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil goeth about as a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour; whom resist stedfast in the Faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Cor, arca legem cóntinens
Non servitútis véteris,
Sed grátiæ, sed véniæ,
Sed et misericórdiæ.

Cor, sanctuárium novi
Intemerátum fœ́deris,
Templum vetústo sánctius,
Velúmque scisso utílius.

Te vulnerátum cáritas
Ictu paténti vóluit,
Amóris invisíbilis
Ut venerémur vúlnera.

Hoc sub amóris sýmbolo
Passus cruénta et mýstica,
Utrúmque sacrifícium
Christus sacérdos óbtulit.

Quis non amántem rédamet?
Quis non redémptus díligat,
Et Corde in isto séligat
Ætérna tabernácula?

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui Corde fundis grátiam,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Jesus, behind thy temple's veil,
Hid in an ark of gold,
On stones engraven, lay the law
thy finger wrote of old.

But in thy body's temple new,
thy life-blood's throbbing shrine,
Held, upon fleshly tables graved,
The law of love divine.

And when that heart in death was stilled,
Each temple's veil was riven:
And lo, within thy love's red shrine,
To us to look was given.

There make us gaze and see the love
Which drew thee, for our sake,
O great high-priest, thyself to God
A sacrifice to make.

Thou, Saviour, cause that every soul
Which thou hast loved so well,
May will within thine open heart
In life and death to dwell.

Grant it, O Father, only Son,
And Spirit, God of grace,
To whom all worship shall be done,
In every time and place.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
En, ut supérba críminum
Et sæva nostrórum cohors
Cor sauciávit ínnocens
Meréntis haud tale Dei!

Vibrántis hastam mílitis
Peccáta nostra dírigunt,
Ferrúmque diræ cúspidis
Mortále crimen ácuit.

Ex Corde scisso Ecclésia,
Christo jugáta, náscitur:
Hoc óstium arcæ in látere est
Genti ad salútem pósitum.

Ex hoc perénnis grátia,
Ceu septifórmis flúvius,
Stolas ut illic sórdidas
Lavémus Agni in sánguine.

Turpe est redíre ad crímina,
Quæ Cor beátum lácerent:
Sed æmulémur córdibus
Flammas amóris índices.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui Corde fundis grátiam,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Lo, how the savage crew
Of our proud sins hath rent
The heart of our all-gracious God,
That heart so innocent.

The soldier's quivering lance
Our guilt it was that drave,
Our wicked deeds that to its point
Such cruel sharpness gave.

O wounded heart, whence sprang
The Church, the Saviour's bride;
Thou door of our salvation's ark
Set in its mystic side.

Thou holy fount, whence flows
The sacred sevenfold flood,
Where we our filthy robes may cleanse
In the Lamb's saving blood:

By sorrowful relapse,
thee will we rend no more;
But like the flames, those types of love,
Strive heavenward to soar.

Father and Son supreme
And Spirit, hear our cry;
Whose is the kingdom, praise and power,
Through all eternity.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Quis ex vobis * homo, qui habet centum oves et, si perdíderit unam ex illis, nonne dimíttit nonagínta novem in desérto et vadit ad illam quæ períerat, donec invéniat eam? Allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: What man of you * that hath an hundred sheep, and if he shall lose one of them, doth he not leave the ninety-nine in the desert and go after that which was lost, until he find it? Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Quæ múlier * habens drachmas decem, et si perdíderit drachmam unam, nonne accéndit lucérnam et evérrit domum et quærit diligénter, donec invéniat?
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: What woman * having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it?

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle

vesperae.capitulum.eng: Dearly beloved, humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time: casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Protéctor in te sperántium, Deus, sine quo nihil est válidum, nihil sanctum; multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, te rectóre, te duce, sic transeámus per bona temporália, ut non amittámus ætérna.
collect.eng: O God, the Protector of those that hope in Thee, without Whom nothing hath strength, nothing is holy, multiply upon us Thy mercy, that with Thee as ruler and guide, we may so pass through things temporal, that we lose not things eternal.

laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:14-17)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Hujus rei grátia flecto génua mea ad Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, ut det vobis secúndum divítias glóriæ suæ virtúte corroborári per Spíritum ejus in interiórem hóminem: Christum habitáre per fidem in córdibus vestris.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:17-19)
nona.capitulum.lat: In caritáte radicáti et fundáti, ut possítis comprehéndere cum ómnibus sanctis, quæ sit latitúdo et longitúdo, et sublímitas et profúndum; scire étiam supereminéntem sciéntiæ caritátem Christi, ut impleámini in omnem plenitúdinem Dei.
nona.capitulum.eng: Being rooted and grounded in love, may ye be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height: and to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fullness of God.

collect.eng: O God, who hast suffered the Heart of thy Son to be wounded by our sins, and in that very Heart hast bestowed on us the abundant riches of thy love: grant that the devout homage of our hearts, which we render unto him, may of thy mercy be deemed a recompence acceptable in thy sight.

sexta.capitulum.eng: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:17-19)

nona.capitulum.eng: Being rooted and grounded in love, may ye be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height: and to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fullness of God.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Cor, arca legem cóntinens
Non servitútis véteris,
Sed grátiæ, sed véniæ,
Sed et misericórdiæ.

Cor, sanctuárium novi
Intemerátum fœ́deris,
Templum vetústo sánctius,
Velúmque scisso utílius.

Te vulnerátum cáritas
Ictu paténti vóluit,
Amóris invisíbilis
Ut venerémur vúlnera.

Hoc sub amóris sýmbolo
Passus cruénta et mýstica,
Utrúmque sacrifícium
Christus sacérdos óbtulit.

Quis non amántem rédamet?
Quis non redémptus díligat,
Et Corde in isto séligat
Ætérna tabernácula?

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui Corde fundis grátiam,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Jesus, behind thy temple's veil,
Hid in an ark of gold,
On stones engraven, lay the law
thy finger wrote of old.

But in thy body's temple new,
thy life-blood's throbbing shrine,
Held, upon fleshly tables graved,
The law of love divine.

And when that heart in death was stilled,
Each temple's veil was riven:
And lo, within thy love's red shrine,
To us to look was given.

There make us gaze and see the love
Which drew thee, for our sake,
O great high-priest, thyself to God
A sacrifice to make.

Thou, Saviour, cause that every soul
Which thou hast loved so well,
May will within thine open heart
In life and death to dwell.

Grant it, O Father, only Son,
And Spirit, God of grace,
To whom all worship shall be done,
In every time and place.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
En, ut supérba críminum
Et sæva nostrórum cohors
Cor sauciávit ínnocens
Meréntis haud tale Dei!

Vibrántis hastam mílitis
Peccáta nostra dírigunt,
Ferrúmque diræ cúspidis
Mortále crimen ácuit.

Ex Corde scisso Ecclésia,
Christo jugáta, náscitur:
Hoc óstium arcæ in látere est
Genti ad salútem pósitum.

Ex hoc perénnis grátia,
Ceu septifórmis flúvius,
Stolas ut illic sórdidas
Lavémus Agni in sánguine.

Turpe est redíre ad crímina,
Quæ Cor beátum lácerent:
Sed æmulémur córdibus
Flammas amóris índices.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui Corde fundis grátiam,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Lo, how the savage crew
Of our proud sins hath rent
The heart of our all-gracious God,
That heart so innocent.

The soldier's quivering lance
Our guilt it was that drave,
Our wicked deeds that to its point
Such cruel sharpness gave.

O wounded heart, whence sprang
The Church, the Saviour's bride;
Thou door of our salvation's ark
Set in its mystic side.

Thou holy fount, whence flows
The sacred sevenfold flood,
Where we our filthy robes may cleanse
In the Lamb's saving blood:

By sorrowful relapse,
thee will we rend no more;
But like the flames, those types of love,
Strive heavenward to soar.

Father and Son supreme
And Spirit, hear our cry;
Whose is the kingdom, praise and power,
Through all eternity.
Amen.
