nona.capitulum.lat: In caritáte radicáti et fundáti, ut possítis comprehéndere cum ómnibus sanctis, quæ sit latitúdo et longitúdo, et sublímitas et profúndum; scire étiam supereminéntem sciéntiæ caritátem Christi, ut impleámini in omnem plenitúdinem Dei.
nona.capitulum.eng: Being rooted and grounded in love, may ye be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height: and to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fullness of God.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Cor, arca legem cóntinens
Non servitútis véteris,
Sed grátiæ, sed véniæ,
Sed et misericórdiæ.

Cor, sanctuárium novi
Intemerátum fœ́deris,
Templum vetústo sánctius,
Velúmque scisso utílius.

Te vulnerátum cáritas
Ictu paténti vóluit,
Amóris invisíbilis
Ut venerémur vúlnera.

Hoc sub amóris sýmbolo
Passus cruénta et mýstica,
Utrúmque sacrifícium
Christus sacérdos óbtulit.

Quis non amántem rédamet?
Quis non redémptus díligat,
Et Corde in isto séligat
Ætérna tabernácula?

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui Corde fundis grátiam,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Jesus, behind thy temple's veil,
Hid in an ark of gold,
On stones engraven, lay the law
thy finger wrote of old.

But in thy body's temple new,
thy life-blood's throbbing shrine,
Held, upon fleshly tables graved,
The law of love divine.

And when that heart in death was stilled,
Each temple's veil was riven:
And lo, within thy love's red shrine,
To us to look was given.

There make us gaze and see the love
Which drew thee, for our sake,
O great high-priest, thyself to God
A sacrifice to make.

Thou, Saviour, cause that every soul
Which thou hast loved so well,
May will within thine open heart
In life and death to dwell.

Grant it, O Father, only Son,
And Spirit, God of grace,
To whom all worship shall be done,
In every time and place.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
En, ut supérba críminum
Et sæva nostrórum cohors
Cor sauciávit ínnocens
Meréntis haud tale Dei!

Vibrántis hastam mílitis
Peccáta nostra dírigunt,
Ferrúmque diræ cúspidis
Mortále crimen ácuit.

Ex Corde scisso Ecclésia,
Christo jugáta, náscitur:
Hoc óstium arcæ in látere est
Genti ad salútem pósitum.

Ex hoc perénnis grátia,
Ceu septifórmis flúvius,
Stolas ut illic sórdidas
Lavémus Agni in sánguine.

Turpe est redíre ad crímina,
Quæ Cor beátum lácerent:
Sed æmulémur córdibus
Flammas amóris índices.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui Corde fundis grátiam,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Lo, how the savage crew
Of our proud sins hath rent
The heart of our all-gracious God,
That heart so innocent.

The soldier's quivering lance
Our guilt it was that drave,
Our wicked deeds that to its point
Such cruel sharpness gave.

O wounded heart, whence sprang
The Church, the Saviour's bride;
Thou door of our salvation's ark
Set in its mystic side.

Thou holy fount, whence flows
The sacred sevenfold flood,
Where we our filthy robes may cleanse
In the Lamb's saving blood:

By sorrowful relapse,
thee will we rend no more;
But like the flames, those types of love,
Strive heavenward to soar.

Father and Son supreme
And Spirit, hear our cry;
Whose is the kingdom, praise and power,
Through all eternity.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Facta sunt * enim hæc ut Scriptúra implerétur quæ dicit: Vidébunt in quem transfixérunt.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: For these things were done * that the Scripture should be fulfilled which saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ad Jesum autem * cum veníssent, ut vidérunt eum jam mórtuum, non fregérunt ejus crura, sed unus mílitum láncea latus ejus apéruit et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But when they came to Jesus * and saw that he was dead already, they broke not his legs, but one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out Blood and Water.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: With joy shall ye draw water.
laudes.versicle.engR: Out of the fountains of the Saviour.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: With joy shall ye draw water.
vesperae.versicle.engR: Out of the fountains of the Saviour.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Unus mílitum * láncea latus ejus apéruit et contínuo exívit sanguis et aqua.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: One of the soldiers * with a spear pierced his side, and forthwith came there out Blood and Water.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Stans Jesus * clamábat dicens: Si quis sitit, véniat ad me et bibat.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Jesus stood * and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: In caritáte perpétua * diléxit nos Deus, ídeo, exaltátus a terra, attráxit nos ad Cor suum, míserans.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: With an everlasting love * hath God loved us, and from the day that he was lifted up over the earth, he hath drawn us with loving-kindness unto his Heart.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Veníte ad me * omnes qui laborátis et oneráti estis et ego refíciam vos.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Come unto me, * all ye that travail and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Fili, * præbe mihi cor tuum, et óculi tui custódiant vias meas.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: My son, * give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Suávi jugo tuo * domináre, Dómine, in médio inimicórum tuórum.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Put thy easy yoke * upon all mankind, O Lord, and be thou ruler, even in the midst of thine enemies.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Miséricors * et miserátor Dóminus: escam dedit timéntibus se.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: This merciful * and gracious Lord hath given Meat unto them that fear him..

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis; miséricors et miserátor Dóminus.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Unto the godly * there ariseth up light in the darkness, even the Lord merciful and gracious.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Quid retríbuam * Dómino pro ómnibus quæ retríbuit mihi?;;115
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: What reward shall I give * unto the Lord for all the benefits that he hath done unto me?

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Apud Dóminum * propitiátio est et copiósa apud eum redémptio.;;129
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:8-9)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brethren: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; and to make all men see what is the fellowship of the Mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui nobis in Corde Fílii tui, nostris vulneráto peccátis, infinítos dilectiónis thesáuros misericórditer largíri dignáris; concéde, quǽsumus, ut illi devótum pietátis nostræ præstántes obséquium, dignæ quoque satisfactiónis exhibeámus offícium.
collect.eng: O God, who hast suffered the Heart of thy Son to be wounded by our sins, and in that very Heart hast bestowed on us the abundant riches of thy love: grant that the devout homage of our hearts, which we render unto him, may of thy mercy be deemed a recompence acceptable in thy sight.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:8-9)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Mihi ómnium sanctórum mínimo data est grátia hæc, in géntibus evangelizáre investigábiles divítias Christi; et illumináre omnes, quæ sit dispensátio sacraménti abscónditi a sǽculis in Deo.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brethren: Unto me, who am less than the least of all saints, is this grace given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ; and to make all men see what is the fellowship of the Mystery, which from the beginning of the world hath been hid in God.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:14-17)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Hujus rei grátia flecto génua mea ad Patrem Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, ut det vobis secúndum divítias glóriæ suæ virtúte corroborári per Spíritum ejus in interiórem hóminem: Christum habitáre per fidem in córdibus vestris.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For this cause I bow my knees unto the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, of whom the whole family in heaven and earth is named, that he would grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with might by his Spirit in the inner man, that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 3:17-19)
nona.capitulum.lat: In caritáte radicáti et fundáti, ut possítis comprehéndere cum ómnibus sanctis, quæ sit latitúdo et longitúdo, et sublímitas et profúndum; scire étiam supereminéntem sciéntiæ caritátem Christi, ut impleámini in omnem plenitúdinem Dei.
nona.capitulum.eng: Being rooted and grounded in love, may ye be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth and length and depth and height: and to know the love of Christ, which passeth knowledge, that ye might be filled with all the fullness of God.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ascéndens Jesus * in navim, et sedens docébat turbas, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus entered into the ship, * and sat down, and taught the people, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Præcéptor, * per totam noctem laborántes nihil cépimus; in verbo autem tuo laxábo rete.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Master, we have toiled all night, * and have taken nothing; nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine: ut et mundi cursus pacífice nobis tuo órdine dirigátur; et Ecclésia tua tranquílla devotióne lætétur.
collect.eng: Grant, O Lord, we beseech thee, that the course of this world may be so peaceably ordered by thy governance, that thy Church may joyfully serve thee in all godly quietness.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Nisi abundáverit * justítia vestra plus quam Scribárum, et Pharisæórum, non intrábitis in regnum cœlórum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Ye have heard that it was said * by them of old time: Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Si offers * munus tuum ad altáre et recordátus fúeris quia frater tuus habet áliquid advérsus te, relínque ibi munus tuum ante altáre, et vade prius reconciliári fratri tuo, et tunc véniens ófferes munus tuum, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: If thou bring thy gift to the Altar, * and there rememberest that thy brother hath aught against thee, leave there thy gift before the Altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui diligéntibus te bona invisibília præparásti: infúnde córdibus nostris tui amóris afféctum; ut te in ómnibus et super ómnia diligéntes, promissiónes tuas, quæ omne desidérium súperant, consequámur.
collect.eng: O God, Who hast prepared for them that love thee such good things as pass man's understanding; pour into our hearts such love toward thee, that we, loving thee in all things and above all things, may obtain thy promises, which exceed all that we can desire.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum turba multa * esset cum Jesu nec habérent quod manducárent, convocátis discípulis, ait illis: Miséreor super turbam, quia ecce jam tríduo sústinent me nec habent quod mandúcent, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The multitude being very great, * and having nothing to eat, Jesus called His disciples unto Him, and saith unto them: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with Me three days, and have nothing to eat. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Miséreor * super turbam, quia ecce jam tríduo sústinent me nec habent quod mandúcent, et, si dimísero eos jejúnos, defícient in via, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I have compassion on the multitude, * because they have now been with Me three days, and have nothing to eat; and if I send them away fasting, they will faint by the way. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus virtútum, cujus est totum quod est óptimum: ínsere pectóribus nostris amórem tui nóminis, et præsta in nobis religiónis augméntum; ut, quæ sunt bona, nútrias, ac pietátis stúdio, quæ sunt nutríta, custódias.
collect.eng: Lord of all power and might, Who art the Author and Giver of all good things, graft in our hearts the love of thy Name, increase in us true religion, nourish us with all goodness, and, of thy great mercy, keep us in the same.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Atténdite * a falsis prophétis, qui véniunt ad vos in vestiméntis óvium, intrínsecus autem sunt lupi rapáces; a frúctibus eórum cognoscétis eos, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Beware of false prophets, * which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Non potest arbor * bona fructus malos fácere, nec arbor mala fructus bonos fácere. Omnis arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidétur, et in ignem mittétur, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, * neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, is hewn down and cast into the fire. Alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, cujus providéntia in sui dispositióne non fállitur: te súpplices exorámus; ut nóxia cuncta submóveas, et ómnia nobis profutúra concédas.
collect.eng: O God, Whose never-failing Providence ordereth all things both in heaven and earth, we humbly beseech thee to put away from us all hurtful things, and to give us those things which be profitable for us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ait dóminus víllico: * Quid hoc áudio de te? redde ratiónem villicatiónis tuæ, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The lord said unto his steward: * How is it that I hear this of thee? Give an account of thy stewardship. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Quid fáciam, * quia dóminus meus aufert a me villicatiónem? Fódere non váleo, mendicáre erubésco. Scio quid fáciam, ut, cum amótus fúero a villicatióne, recípiant me in domos suas.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: What shall I do? * For my lord taketh away from me the stewardship. I cannot dig, to beg I am ashamed. I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Largíre nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, semper spíritum cogitándi quæ recta sunt, propítius et agéndi: ut, qui sine te esse non póssumus, secúndum te vívere valeámus.
collect.eng: Grant to us, Lord, we beseech thee, the spirit to think and do always such things as be rightful, that we, who cannot do anything that is good without thee, may by thee be enabled to live according to thy will.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum appropinquáret * Dóminus Jerúsalem videns civitátem flevit super illam, et dixit: Quia si cognovísses et tu, quia vénient dies in te, et circúmdabunt te inimíci tui vallo et circúmdabunt te et coangustábunt te úndique et ad terram prostérnent te: eo quod non cognovísti tempus visitatiónis tuæ, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When the Lord was come near to Jerusalem, He beheld the city, and wept * over it, saying: If thou hadst known, even thou! For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side and shall lay thee even with the ground because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Scriptum est enim: * Quia domus mea domus oratiónis est cunctis géntibus; vos autem fecístis illam spelúncam latrónum. Et erat cotídie docens in templo.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: It is written: My house is the house of prayer * for all nations but ye have made it a den of thieves. And He taught daily in the Temple.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Páteant aures misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, précibus supplicántium: et, ut peténtibus desideráta concédas; fac eos, quæ tibi sunt plácita, postuláre.
collect.eng: Let thy merciful ears, O Lord, be open to the prayers of thy humble servants; and, that they may obtain their petitions, make them to ask such things as shall please thee.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Stans a longe * publicánus, nolébat óculos ad cælum leváre, sed percutiébat pectus suum dicens: Deus, propítius esto mihi peccatóri.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The publican, standing afar off, * would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying: God, be merciful to me, a sinner.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Omnis * qui se exáltat, humiliábitur: et qui se humiliat, exaltábitur.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: This man went down to his house * justified rather than the other, for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased, and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui omnipoténtiam tuam parcéndo máxime et miserándo maniféstas: multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, ad tua promíssa curréntes, cæléstium bonórum fácias esse consórtes.
collect.eng: O God, Who declarest thine Almighty power most chiefly in showing mercy and pity, mercifully grant unto us such a measure of thy grace, that we, running the way of thy commandments, may obtain thy gracious promises, and be made partakers of thy heavenly treasure.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Quanto eis præcipiébat, * tanto magis plus prædicábant: et eo ámplius admirabántur, dicéntes: Bene ómnia fecit, et surdos fecit audíre, et mutos loqui.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When the Lord had departed from the coasts of Tyre, * He made both the deaf to hear and the dumb to speak.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Bene ómnia fecit * et surdos fecit audíre et mutos loqui.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: He hath done all things well, * He maketh both the deaf to hear and the dumb to speak.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui, abundántia pietátis tuæ, et mérita súpplicum excédis et vota: effúnde super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut dimíttas quæ consciéntia métuit, et adícias quod orátio non præsúmit.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who art always more ready to hear than we to pray, and art wont to give more than either we desire or deserve, pour down upon us the abundance of thy mercy, forgiving us those things whereof our conscience is afraid, and giving us those good things which we are not worthy to ask.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Magíster, * quid faciéndo vitam ætérnam possidébo? At ille dixit ad eum: In lege quid scriptum est? quómodo legis? Díliges Dóminum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Master, what shall I do * to inherit eternal life? He said unto him: What is written in the law? How readest thou? And he, answering, said: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Homo quidam * descendébat ab Jerúsalem in Jéricho et íncidit in latrónes, qui étiam despoliavérunt eum et, plagis impósitis, abiérunt semivívo relícto.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: A certain man went down from Jerusalem * to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, de cujus múnere venit, ut tibi a fidélibus tuis digne et laudabíliter serviátur: tríbue, quǽsumus, nobis; ut ad promissiónes tuas sine offensióne currámus.
collect.eng: Almighty and merciful God, of Whose only gift it cometh that thy faithful people do unto thee true and laudable service, grant, we beseech thee, that we may so faithfully serve thee in this life, that we fail not finally to attain thy heavenly promises.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum transíret ~
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: As Jesus passed through * a certain village, there met Him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off; and they lifted up their voices, and said: “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.”

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Unus autem * ex illis, ut vidit quod mundátus est, regréssus est cum magna voce magníficans Deum, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And one of them, * when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, da nobis fídei, spei et caritátis augméntum: et, ut mereámur ássequi quod promíttis, fac nos amáre quod prǽcipis.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, give unto us the increase of faith, hope, and charity, and that we may worthily obtain that which Thou dost promise, make us to love that which Thou dost command.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Nolíte sollíciti esse * dicéntes: Quid manducábimus aut quid bibémus? scit enim Pater vester quid vobis necésse sit, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Take no thought, saying: What shall we eat? * or: What shall we drink? For your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Quǽrite primum * regnum Dei et justítiam ejus, et hæc ómnia adiciéntur vobis, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Seek ye first the kingdom of God * and His righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Custódi, Dómine, quǽsumus, Ecclésiam tuam propitiatióne perpétua: et quia sine te lábitur humána mortálitas; tuis semper auxíliis et abstrahátur a nóxiis et ad salutária dirigátur.
collect.eng: Keep, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy Church with thy perpetual mercy, and because the frailty of man without thee cannot but fall, keep us ever by thy help from all things hurtful, and lead us to all things profitable to our salvation.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Accéssit autem Jesus, * et tétigit lóculum: hi autem qui portábant, stetérunt: et ait: Adoléscens, tibi dico, surge: et resédit qui erat mórtuus, allelúia.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus went into a city called Nain * and, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Accépit autem omnes timor, * et magnificábant Deum, dicéntes: Quia Prophéta magnus surréxit in nobis, et quia Deus visitávit plebem suam.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: A great prophet is risen up among us * and God hath visited His people.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Ecclésiam tuam, Dómine, miserátio continuáta mundet et múniat: et quia sine te non potest salva consístere; tuo semper múnere gubernétur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, let thy continual pity cleanse and defend thy Church, and because it cannot continue in safety without thy succour, preserve it evermore by thy help and goodness.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dixit Jesus * ad Legisperítos, et Pharisæos: Si licet Sábbato curáre? At illi tacuérunt; ipse vero apprehándens hydrópicum, sanávit eum, ac dimísit.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: As Jesus went into the house * of one of the chief Pharisees, to eat bread on the Sabbath Day, behold, there was a certain man before Him which had the dropsy and He took him, and healed him, and let him go.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Cum vocátus fúeris * ad núptias, recúmbe in novíssimo loco, ut dicat tibi qui te invitávit: Amíce, ascénde supérius. Et erit tibi glória coram simul discumbéntibus, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: When thou art bidden * of any man to a wedding, go and sit down in the lowest room, that he that bade thee may say: Friend, go up higher, then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Tua nos, quǽsumus, Dómine, grátia semper et prævéniat et sequátur: ac bonis opéribus júgiter præstet esse inténtos.
collect.eng: Lord, we pray thee, that thy grace may always prevent and follow us, and make us continually to be given to all good works.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Magíster, * quod est mandátum magnum in lege? Ait illi Jesus: Díliges Dóminum Deum tuum ex toto corde tuo, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Master, which is the great commandment * in the law? Jesus said unto him: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Quid vobis * vidétur de Christo? cujus fílius est? Dicunt ei omnes: David. Dicit eis Jesus: Quómodo David in spíritu vocat eum Dóminum dicens: Dixit Dóminus Dómino meo: Sede a dextris meis?
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: What think ye of Christ? Whose Son is He? * They say all unto Him: The Son of David. Jesus saith unto them: How then doth David in spirit call Him Lord, saying: The Lord said unto my Lord, Sit Thou at My right hand?

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Da, quǽsumus, Dómine, pópulo tuo diabólica vitáre contágia: et te solum Deum pura mente sectári.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, grant thy people grace to withstand the temptations of the devil, and with pure hearts to follow thee the only God.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dixit Dóminus * paralýtico: Confíde, fili, remittúntur tibi peccáta tua.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The Lord said unto the sick * of the palsy: Son, be of good cheer, thy sins be forgiven thee.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Tulit ergo * paralýticus lectum suum, in quo jacébat, magníficans Deum: et omnis plebs, ut vidit, dedit laudem Deo.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And immediately, he that had been sick of the palsy arose, * and took up his bed whereon he lay, glorifying God and all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Dírigat corda nostra, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuæ miseratiónis operátio: quia tibi sine te placére non póssumus.
collect.eng: Mercifully grant, O Lord, that thine effectual goodness may in all things direct our hearts, forasmuch as without thee we are not able to please thee.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dícite invitátis: * Ecce prándium meum parávi, veníte ad núptias, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Tell them which are bidden: * Behold, I have prepared my dinner; Come unto the marriage. Alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Núptiæ * quidem parátæ sunt, sed qui invitáti erant, non fuérunt digni. Ite ergo ad éxitus viárum, et quoscúmque invenéritis, vocáte ad núptias, dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And the King came in * to see the guests, and he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment. And he saith unto him: Friend, how camest thou in hither, not having a wedding garment?

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, univérsa nobis adversántia propitiátus exclúde: ut mente et córpore páriter expedíti, quæ tua sunt, líberis méntibus exsequámur.
collect.eng: O Almighty and most merciful God, of thy bountiful goodness keep us, we beseech thee, from all things that may hurt us; that we, being ready both in body and soul, may cheerfully accomplish those things that Thou wouldest have done.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Erat quidam régulus, * cujus fílius infirmabátur Caphárnaum. Hic cum audísset quod Jesus veníret in Galilǽam, rogábat eum ut sanáret fílium ejus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: There was a certain nobleman whose son was sick * at Capernaum. When he heard that Jesus was come into Galilee, he besought Him that He would heal his son.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Cognóvit autem pater * quia illa hora erat, in qua dixit Jesus: Fílius tuus vivit; et crédidit ipse et domus ejus tota.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: So the father knew * that it was at the same hour in which Jesus said “Thy son liveth.” And he himself believed, and his whole house.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Largíre, quǽsumus, Dómine, fidélibus tuis indulgéntiam placátus et pacem: ut páriter ab ómnibus mundéntur offénsis, et secúra tibi mente desérviant.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord, to thy faithful people pardon and peace, that they may be cleansed from all their sins, and serve thee with a quiet mind.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dixit autem * dóminus servo: Redde quod debes. Prócidens autem servus ille rogábat eum, dicens: Patiéntiam habe in me, et ómnia reddam tibi.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The lord said unto his servant: Pay me * that thou owest. But the servant fell down and besought him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Serve nequam, * omne débitum dimísi tibi, quóniam rogásti me: nonne ergo opórtuit et te miseréri consérvi tui, sicut et ego tui misértus sum? dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all * that debt, because thou desiredst me. Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellow-servant, even as I had pity on thee, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Famíliam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, contínua pietáte custódi: ut a cunctis adversitátibus te protegénte, sit líbera; et in bonis áctibus tuo nómini sit devóta.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee to keep thine household in continual godliness, that, through thy protection, it may be free from all adversities, and devoutly given to serve thee in good works, to the glory of thy Name.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Magíster, * scimus quia verax es et viam Dei in veritáte doces, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Master, we know that Thou art true, * and teachest the way of God in truth, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Réddite ergo * quæ sunt Cǽsaris Cǽsari, et quæ sunt Dei Deo, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's, * and unto God the things that are God's, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, refúgium nostrum et virtus: adésto piis Ecclésiæ tuæ précibus, auctor ipse pietátis, et præsta; ut, quod fidéliter pétimus, efficáciter consequámur.
collect.eng: O God, our Refuge and Strength, Who art the author of all godliness, be ready, we beseech thee, to hear the devout prayers of thy Church, and grant that those things which we ask faithfully, we may obtain effectually.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dicébat enim * intra se: Si tetígero fímbriam vestiménti ejus tantum, salva ero.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: For she said within herself: * If I may but touch the hem of His garment, I shall be whole.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: At Jesus convérsus * et videns eam dixit: Confíde, fília, fides tua te salvam fecit, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But Jesus turned Him about, * and when He saw her, He said: Daughter, be of good comfort; thy faith hath made thee whole, alleluia.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Absólve, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuórum delícta populórum: ut a peccatórum néxibus, quæ pro nostra fragilitáte contráximus, tua benignitáte liberémur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, absolve thy people from their offences, that through thy bountiful goodness we may all be delivered from the bands of those sins, which by our frailty we have committed.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum vidéritis * abominatiónem desolatiónis quæ dicta est a Daniéle prophéta, stantem in loco sancto: qui legit, intéllegat.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When ye shall see the abomination of desolation, * spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, stand in the Holy Place, (whoso readeth, let him understand.)

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Amen dico vobis * quia non præteríbit generátio hæc, donec ómnia fiant: cælum et terra transíbunt, verba autem mea non transíbunt, dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Amen, I say unto you, this generation shall not pass till all these things be fulfilled; * heaven and earth shall pass away, but My words shall not pass away, saith the Lord.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Excita, quǽsumus, Dómine, tuórum fidélium voluntátes: ut, divíni óperis fructum propénsius exsequéntes; pietátis tuæ remédia majóra percípiant.
collect.eng: Stir up, we beseech thee, Lord, the wills of thy faithful people, that they, plenteously bringing forth the fruit of good works, may of thee be plenteously rewarded.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 6:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Hortámur vos, ne in vácuum grátiam Dei recipiátis. Ait enim: Témpore accépto exaudívi te, et in die salútis adjúvi te.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers, we exhort you, that you receive not the grace of God in vain. For he saith: In an accepted time have I heard thee; and in the day of salvation have I helped thee.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor. 6:2-3)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Ecce nunc tempus acceptábile, ecce nunc dies salútis: némini dantes ullam offensiónem, ut non vituperétur ministérium nostrum.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For he saith: In an accepted time have I heard thee; and in the day of salvation have I helped thee. Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation, giving no offense to any man, that our ministry be not blamed.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 6:9-10)
nona.capitulum.lat: Ut castigáti, et non mortificáti: quasi tristes, semper autem gaudéntes: sicut egéntes, multos autem locupletántes tamquam nihil habéntes, et ómnia possidéntes.
nona.capitulum.eng: As dying, and behold we live; as chastised, and not killed; as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as needy, yet enriching many; as having nothing, and possessing all things.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ductus est Jesus * in desértum a Spíritu, ut tentarétur a diábolo: et cum jejunásset quadragínta diébus et quadragínta nóctibus, póstea esúriit.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus was led up of the Spirit into the wilderness, * to be tempted of the devil and when He had fasted forty days and forty nights, He was afterward hungry.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ecce nunc tempus * acceptábile, ecce nunc dies salútis: in his ergo diébus exhibeámus nosmetípsos sicut Dei minístros in multa patiéntia, in jejúniis, in vigíliis, et in caritáte non ficta.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Behold, now is the accepted time * behold, now is the day of salvation; in these days therefore let us approve ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in fastings, in watchings, and in love unfeigned.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Cor mundum * crea in me Deus, et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Create in me a clean heart, * O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: O Dómine, * salvum me fac; o Dómine, bene prosperáre.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Save me now, O Lord; * O Lord, send Thou prosperity.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Sic benedícam * te in vita mea, Dómine: et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Thus will I bless thee, * O Lord, while I live; and will lift up my hands in thy Name.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: In spíritu humilitátis, * et in ánimo contríto suscipiámur, Dómine, a te: et sic fiat sacrifícium nostrum, ut a te suscipiátur hódie, et pláceat tibi, Dómine Deus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: In an humble spirit * and a contrite heart may we be accepted by thee, O Lord; and so let our sacrifice be this day, that it may be acceptable and pleasant in thy sight, O Lord our God!

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Laudáte Deum * cæli cælórum, et aquæ omnes.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Praise God, * ye heavens of heavens, and all ye waters.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 6:1-2)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Hortámur vos, ne in vácuum grátiam Dei recipiátis. Ait enim: Témpore accépto exaudívi te, et in die salútis adjúvi te.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers, we exhort you, that you receive not the grace of God in vain. For he saith: In an accepted time have I heard thee; and in the day of salvation have I helped thee.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Veníte, benedícti * Patris mei, percípite regnum, quod vobis parátum est ab orígine mundi.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Come, ye blessed of My Father, * inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Quod uni * ex mínimis meis fecístis, mihi fecístis, dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: As long as you did it to one * of these my least brethren, you did it to me, said the Lord.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Intrávit Jesus * in templum Dei, et eiciébat omnes vendéntes et eméntes: et mensas nummulariórum, et cáthedras vendéntium colúmbas evértit.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus went into * the temple of God, * and cast out all them that sold and bought, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of them that sold doves.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Scriptum est enim, * quia domus mea, domus oratiónis est cunctis géntibus: vos autem fecístis illam spelúncam latrónum: et erat cotídie docens in templo.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: For it is written * that My house is the house of prayer * for all nations but ye have made it a den of thieves and He was daily teaching in the temple.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Generátio * hæc prava et pervérsa signum quærit: et signum non dábitur ei, nisi signum Jonæ prophétæ.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: This evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; * and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the Prophet Jonas.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Sicut fuit Jonas * in ventre ceti tribus diébus et tribus nóctibus, ita erit Fílius hóminis in corde terræ.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: As Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly, * so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Egréssus Jesus * secéssit in partes Tyri et Sidónis: et ecce múlier Chananǽa a fínibus illis egréssa, clamábat dicens: Miserére mei, Fili David.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: And Jesus went from thence * and retired into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon. And behold a woman of Canaan who came out of those coasts, crying out, said to him: Have mercy on me, O thou Son of David.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: O múlier, * magna est fides tua: fiat tibi sicut petísti.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: O woman * great is thy faith; be it unto thee even as thou wilt.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Angelus Dómini * descendébat de cælo, et movebátur aqua, et sanabátur unus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The Angel of the Lord * came down from heaven and the water was troubled, and one was made whole.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Qui me sanum fecit * ille mihi præcépit: tolle grabátum tuum, et ámbula in pace.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: He that made me whole, * the same said unto me: Take up thy bed, and walk in peace.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Assúmpsit Jesus * discípulos suos, et ascéndit in montem, et transfigurátus est ante eos.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus took His disciples, * and went up into a mountain, and was transfigured before them.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui Ecclésiam tuam ánnua quadragesimáli observatióne puríficas: præsta famíliæ tuæ; ut, quod a te obtinére abstinéndo nítitur, hoc bonis opéribus exsequátur.
collect.eng: O God, Who dost every year purge thy Church by the Fast of Forty Days, grant unto this thy family, that what things soever they strive to obtain at thy hand by abstaining from meats, they may ever turn to profit by good works.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Thess 4:1)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Rogámus vos, et obsecrámus in Dómino Jesu: ut, quemádmodum accepístis a nobis, quómodo vos opórteat ambuláre, et placére Deo, sic et ambulétis, ut abundétis magis.
laudes.capitulum.eng: For the rest therefore, brethren, we pray and beseech you in the Lord Jesus, that as you have received from us, how you ought to walk, and to please God, so also you would walk, that you may abound the more.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Thess 4:3-4)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Hæc est enim volúntas Dei, sanctificátio vestra: ut abstineátis vos a fornicatióne, ut sciat unusquísque vestrum vas suum possidére in sanctificatióne et honóre.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For this is the will of God, your sanctification; that you should abstain from fornication, that every one of you should know how to possess his vessel in sanctification and honour.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Thess 4:7)
nona.capitulum.lat: Non enim vocávit nos Deus in immundítiam, sed in sanctificatiónem, in Christo Jesu Dómino nostro.
nona.capitulum.eng: For God hath not called us unto uncleanness, but unto sanctification in Christ Jesus our Lord.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Assúmpsit Jesus * discípulos suos, et ascéndit in montem, et transfigurátus est ante eos.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus took His disciples, * and went up into a mountain, and was transfigured before them.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Visiónem quam vidístis, * némini dixéritis, donec a mórtuis resúrgat Fílius hóminis.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Tell the vision that ye have seen to no man, * until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Dómine, * lábia mea apéries, et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O Lord, open Thou my lips, * and my mouth shall show forth thy praise.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Déxtera Dómini * fecit virtútem: déxtera Dómini exaltávit me.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The right hand of the Lord * hath done valiantly, the right hand of the Lord hath exalted me.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Factus est * adjútor meus, Deus meus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: My God * hath been my help.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Trium puerórum * cantémus hymnum, quem cantábant in camíno ignis, benedicéntes Dóminum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Let us sing the Song of the Three Children, * even the Song that they sang when they blessed the Lord in the burning fiery furnace.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Státuit ea * in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: He hath established them * for ever and ever: He hath made a decree which shall not pass.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Thess 4:1)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Rogámus vos, et obsecrámus in Dómino Jesu: ut, quemádmodum accepístis a nobis, quómodo vos opórteat ambuláre, et placére Deo, sic et ambulétis, ut abundétis magis.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: For the rest therefore, brethren, we pray and beseech you in the Lord Jesus, that as you have received from us, how you ought to walk, and to please God, so also you would walk, that you may abound the more.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis omni nos virtúte destítui: intérius exteriúsque custódi; ut ab ómnibus adversitátibus muniámur in córpore, et a pravis cogitatiónibus mundémur in mente.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, keep us both outwardly in our bodies, and inwardly in our souls, that we may be defended from all adversities which may happen to the body, and from all evil thoughts which may assault and hurt the soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ego princípium, * qui et loquor vobis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The beginning, * who also speak unto you.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Qui me misit * mecum est, et non relíquit me solum; quia quæ plácita sunt ei, fácio semper.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: He That sent Me is with Me, * and hath not left Me alone, for I do always those things that please Him.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis omni nos virtúte destítui: intérius exteriúsque custódi; ut ab ómnibus adversitátibus muniámur in córpore, et a pravis cogitatiónibus mundémur in mente.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, keep us both outwardly in our bodies, and inwardly in our souls, that we may be defended from all adversities which may happen to the body, and from all evil thoughts which may assault and hurt the soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Unus est * enim magíster vester, qui in cælis est, Christus Dóminus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: For One is your Master, * Which is in heaven, even Christ the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Omnes autem * vos fratres estis: et patrem nolíte vocáre vobis super terram: unus est enim Pater vester, qui in cælis est: nec vocémini magístri, quia magíster vester unus est Christus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And all ye are brethren, * and call no man your father upon earth, for One is your Father, Which is in heaven; neither be ye called masters, for One is your Master, even Christ.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis omni nos virtúte destítui: intérius exteriúsque custódi; ut ab ómnibus adversitátibus muniámur in córpore, et a pravis cogitatiónibus mundémur in mente.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, keep us both outwardly in our bodies, and inwardly in our souls, that we may be defended from all adversities which may happen to the body, and from all evil thoughts which may assault and hurt the soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ecce ascéndimus * Jerosólymam: et Fílius hóminis tradétur ad crucifigéndum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, * and the Son of man shall be betrayed to be crucified.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Tradétur enim géntibus * ad illudéndum, et flagellándum, et crucifigéndum.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: For He shall be delivered to the Gentiles, * to mock, and to scourge, and to crucify.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis omni nos virtúte destítui: intérius exteriúsque custódi; ut ab ómnibus adversitátibus muniámur in córpore, et a pravis cogitatiónibus mundémur in mente.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, keep us both outwardly in our bodies, and inwardly in our souls, that we may be defended from all adversities which may happen to the body, and from all evil thoughts which may assault and hurt the soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Fili, recordáre, * quia recepísti bona in vita tua, et Lázarus simíliter mala.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Son, remember * that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dives ille * guttam aquæ pétiit, qui micas panis Lázaro negávit.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: That rich man * who had refused Lazarus bread-crumbs, cried for a drop of water.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis omni nos virtúte destítui: intérius exteriúsque custódi; ut ab ómnibus adversitátibus muniámur in córpore, et a pravis cogitatiónibus mundémur in mente.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, keep us both outwardly in our bodies, and inwardly in our souls, that we may be defended from all adversities which may happen to the body, and from all evil thoughts which may assault and hurt the soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Malos male perdet, * et víneam suam locábit áliis agrícolis, qui reddant ei fructum tempóribus suis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: He will miserably destroy * those wicked men, and will let out His vineyard unto other husbandmen, which shall render Him the fruits in their seasons.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Quæréntes eum tenére, * timuérunt turbam, quia sicut prophétam eum habébant.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: When they sought * to lay hands on Him, they feared the multitude, because they took Him for a Prophet.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis omni nos virtúte destítui: intérius exteriúsque custódi; ut ab ómnibus adversitátibus muniámur in córpore, et a pravis cogitatiónibus mundémur in mente.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, keep us both outwardly in our bodies, and inwardly in our souls, that we may be defended from all adversities which may happen to the body, and from all evil thoughts which may assault and hurt the soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Vadam ad Patrem meum * et dicam ei: Pater, fac me sicut unum ex mercenáriis tuis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: I will arise and go to my father, * and will say unto him: Make me as one of thine hired servants.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dixit autem pater * ad servos suos: Cito proférte stolam primam, et indúite illum, et date ánulum in manu ejus, et calceaménta in pédibus ejus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But the father said * to his servants: Bring forth quickly the first robe, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis omni nos virtúte destítui: intérius exteriúsque custódi; ut ab ómnibus adversitátibus muniámur in córpore, et a pravis cogitatiónibus mundémur in mente.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we have no power of ourselves to help ourselves, keep us both outwardly in our bodies, and inwardly in our souls, that we may be defended from all adversities which may happen to the body, and from all evil thoughts which may assault and hurt the soul.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 5:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Estóte imitatóres Dei, sicut fílii caríssimi: et ambuláte in dilectióne, sicut et Christus diléxit nos, et trádidit semetípsum pro nobis oblatiónem et hóstiam Deo in odórem suavitátis.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Be ye, therefore, followers of God, as most dear children; And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath delivered himself for us, an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 5:5)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Hoc enim scitóte intellegéntes, quod omnis fornicátor, aut immúndus, aut avarus, quod est idolórum sérvitus, non habet hereditátem in regno Christi et Dei.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For know you this and understand, that no fornicator, or unclean, or covetous person (which is a serving of idols), hath inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 5:8-9)
nona.capitulum.lat: Erátis enim aliquándo ténebræ, nunc autem lux in Dómino: ut fílii lucis ambuláte: fructus enim lucis est in omni bonitáte, et justítia, et veritáte.
nona.capitulum.eng: For you were heretofore darkness, but now light in the Lord. Walk then as children of the light. For the fruit of the light is in all goodness, and justice, and truth.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum fortis armátus * custódit átrium suum, in pace sunt ómnia quæ póssidet.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When a strong man armed keepeth his palace, * his goods are in peace.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Extóllens vocem * quædam múlier de turba, dixit: Beátus venter qui te portávit, et úbera quæ suxísti. At Jesus ait illi: Quinímmo beáti, qui áudiunt verbum Dei, et custódiunt illud.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: A certain woman of the company lifted up her voice and said: * Blessed is the womb that bare thee, and the paps which Thou hast sucked. But Jesus said unto her: Yea, rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Fac benígne * in bona voluntáte tua, ut ædificéntur, Dómine, muri Jerúsalem.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O Lord, do good in thy good pleasure * unto Zion; to build the walls of Jerusalem.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Dóminus * mihi adjútor est, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord is on my side; * I will not fear what can man do unto me.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Adhǽsit ánima mea * post te, Deus meus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: O my God, my soul cleaveth fast * after thee, O God.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Deus misereátur nostri, * et benedícat nos.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: May God have mercy * on us and bless us.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Lábia mea * laudábunt te in vita mea, Deus meus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: My lips * shall praise, thee all my life long, my God.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Eph 5:1-2)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Estóte imitatóres Dei, sicut fílii caríssimi: et ambuláte in dilectióne, sicut et Christus diléxit nos, et trádidit semetípsum pro nobis oblatiónem et hóstiam Deo in odórem suavitátis.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Be ye, therefore, followers of God, as most dear children; And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath delivered himself for us, an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: We beseech You, almighty God, hear the prayers of the humble and stretch forth the right hand of Your majesty to protect us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Amen dico vobis, * quia nemo prophéta accéptus est in pátria sua.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Amen I say unto you, * no Prophet is accepted in his own country.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Jesus autem, tránsiens * per médium illórum, ibat.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But Jesus, * passing through the midst of them, went His way.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: We beseech You, almighty God, hear the prayers of the humble and stretch forth the right hand of Your majesty to protect us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Si duo ex vobis * consénserint super terram: de omni re quamcúmque petíerint, fiet illis a Patre meo, dicit Dóminus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: If two of you shall agree on earth * as touching anything that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of My Father, saith the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ubi duo vel tres * congregáti fúerint in nómine meo, in médio eórum sum, dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Where two or three are gathered together in My Name, * there am I in the midst of them, saith the Lord.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: We beseech You, almighty God, hear the prayers of the humble and stretch forth the right hand of Your majesty to protect us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Audíte et intellégite * traditiónes, quas Dóminus dedit nobis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Hear and understand * the traditions which the Lord hath given unto us.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Non lotis mánibus * manducáre, non coínquinat hóminem.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: To eat * with unwashen hands, defileth not a man.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: We beseech You, almighty God, hear the prayers of the humble and stretch forth the right hand of Your majesty to protect us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Exíbant autem dæmónia * a multis clamántia, et dicéntia, Quia tu es Christus Fílius Dei: et íncrepans non sinébat ea loqui, quia sciébant ipsum esse Christum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: And devils also came out of many, * crying out and saying: Thou art Christ, the Son of God. And He, rebuking them, suffered them not to speak, for they knew that He was Christ.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Omnes qui habébant infírmos, * ducébant illos ad Jesum, et sanabántur.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: All they that had * any sick brought them unto Jesus, and He healed them.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: We beseech You, almighty God, hear the prayers of the humble and stretch forth the right hand of Your majesty to protect us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Aquam, quam ego dédero, * si quis bíberit ex ea, non sítiet in ætérnum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Whosoever drinketh * of the water that I shall give him, shall never thirst.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dómine, * ut vídeo, prophéta es tu: patres nostri in monte hoc adoravérunt.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Sir, I perceive * that Thou art a prophet: our fathers worshipped in this mountain.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: We beseech You, almighty God, hear the prayers of the humble and stretch forth the right hand of Your majesty to protect us.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Inclinávit se Jesus, * et scribébat in terra: Si quis sine peccáto est, mittat in eam lápidem.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus stooped down, * and wrote on the ground: He that is without sin, let him cast a stone at her.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, vota humílium réspice: atque ad defensiónem nostram, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: We beseech You, almighty God, hear the prayers of the humble and stretch forth the right hand of Your majesty to protect us.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:22-24)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Scriptum est, quóniam Abraham duos fílios hábuit: unum de ancílla, et unum de líbera: sed qui de ancílla, secúndum carnem natus est: qui autem de líbera, per repromissiónem: quæ sunt per allegoríam dicta.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For it is written that Abraham had two sons: the one by a bondwoman, and the other by a free woman. But he who was of the bondwoman, was born according to the flesh: but he of the free woman, was by promise, which things are said by an allegory.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:27)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Lætáre, stérilis, quæ non paris: erúmpe et clama, quæ non párturis: quia multi fílii desértæ, magis quam ejus, quæ habet virum.
sexta.capitulum.eng: For it is written: Rejoice, thou barren, that bearest not: break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for many are the children of the desolate, more than of her that hath a husband.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:31)
nona.capitulum.lat: Itaque, fratres, non sumus ancíllæ fílii, sed líberæ: qua libertáte Christus nos liberávit.
nona.capitulum.eng: So then, brethren, we are not the children of the bondwoman, but of the free: by the freedom wherewith Christ has made us free.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum sublevásset óculos * Jesus, et vidísset máximam multitúdinem veniéntem ad se, dixit ad Philíppum: Unde emémus panes, ut mandúcent hi? Hoc autem dicébat tentans eum: ipse enim sciébat quid esset factúrus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When Jesus lifted up His Eyes, * and saw a great company come unto Him, He saith unto Philip: Whence shall we buy bread that these may eat? And this He said to prove him; for He Himself knew what He would do.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Cum vidíssent turbæ * signum quod fécerat Jesus, dicébant: Vere hic est Prophéta, qui venit in mundum.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And Jesus went up into a mountain, * and there He sat with His disciples.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Tunc acceptábis * sacrifícium justítiæ, si avérteris fáciem tuam a peccátis meis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Then shalt Thou be pleased * with the sacrifices of righteousness, when Thou hast hidden thy face from my sins.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Bonum est * speráre in Dómino, quam speráre in princípibus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: It is better to trust * in the Lord, than to trust in princes.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Me suscépit * déxtera tua, Dómine.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Thy right hand hath * received me, O Lord.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Benedícat nos Deus, * Deus noster, benedícat nos Deus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Let God, even our own God, bless us; * let God bless us.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: In matutínis, * Dómine, meditábor in te.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: In the morning * O Lord, I shall meditate upon thee.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Gal 4:22-24)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Scriptum est, quóniam Abraham duos fílios hábuit: unum de ancílla, et unum de líbera: sed qui de ancílla, secúndum carnem natus est: qui autem de líbera, per repromissiónem: quæ sunt per allegoríam dicta.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For it is written that Abraham had two sons: the one by a bondwoman, and the other by a free woman. But he who was of the bondwoman, was born according to the flesh: but he of the free woman, was by promise, which things are said by an allegory.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui ex mérito nostræ actiónis afflígimur, tuæ grátiæ consolatióne respirémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that we who for our evil deeds are worthily punished, may, by the comfort of thy grace, mercifully be relieved.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Auférte ista hinc, * dicit Dóminus: et nolíte fácere domum Patris mei domum negotiatiónis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Thus saith the Lord: * Take these things hence; make not My Father's house an house of merchandise.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Sólvite templum hoc, * dicit Dóminus; et post tríduum reædificábo illud: hoc autem dicébat de templo córporis sui.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Thus saith the Lord: * Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. But He spoke of the temple of His Body.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui ex mérito nostræ actiónis afflígimur, tuæ grátiæ consolatióne respirémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that we who for our evil deeds are worthily punished, may, by the comfort of thy grace, mercifully be relieved.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Quid me quǽritis * interfícere, hóminem qui vera locútus sum vobis?
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Why go ye about to kill Me, * a Man that hath told you the truth?

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Nemo in eum misit manum: * quia nondum vénerat hora ejus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: No man laid hands on Him; * because His hour was not yet come.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui ex mérito nostræ actiónis afflígimur, tuæ grátiæ consolatióne respirémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that we who for our evil deeds are worthily punished, may, by the comfort of thy grace, mercifully be relieved.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Rabbi, quid peccávit * homo iste, quod cæcus natus est? Respóndit Jesus, et dixit: Neque hic peccávit, neque paréntes ejus: sed ut manifesténtur ópera Dei in illo.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Rabbi, who did sin, this man, or his parents, * that he was born blind? Jesus answered, and said: Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents; but that the works of God shall be made manifest in him.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ille homo * qui dícitur Jesus, lutum fecit ex sputo, et linívit óculos meos, et modo vídeo.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The Man that is called Jesus * made clay of His Spittle, and anointed mine eyes, and now I do see.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui ex mérito nostræ actiónis afflígimur, tuæ grátiæ consolatióne respirémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that we who for our evil deeds are worthily punished, may, by the comfort of thy grace, mercifully be relieved.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ibat Jesus * in civitátem, quæ vocátur Naim: et ecce defúnctus efferebátur fílius únicus matris suæ.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus went * into a city that is called Naim: and behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Prophéta magnus * surréxit in nobis, et quia Deus visitávit plebem suam.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: A great Prophet * is risen up among us, and God hath visited His people.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui ex mérito nostræ actiónis afflígimur, tuæ grátiæ consolatióne respirémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that we who for our evil deeds are worthily punished, may, by the comfort of thy grace, mercifully be relieved.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Lázarus amícus noster * dormit: eámus, et a somno excitémus eum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; * let us go and awake him out of sleep.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dómine, * si fuísses hic, Lázarus non esset mórtuus: ecce jam fœtet quatriduánus in monuménto.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Lord, if Thou hadst been here * Lazarus had not died; behold, by this time he stinketh, for he hath lain in the grave four days already.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui ex mérito nostræ actiónis afflígimur, tuæ grátiæ consolatióne respirémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that we who for our evil deeds are worthily punished, may, by the comfort of thy grace, mercifully be relieved.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Qui séquitur me, * non ámbulat in ténebris: sed habébit lumen vitæ, dicit Dóminus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Thus saith the Lord: * He that followeth Me walketh not in darkness, but shall have the Light of life.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ego sum * qui testimónium perhíbeo de meípso: et testimónium pérhibet de me, qui misit me, Pater.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I am One * That bear witness of Myself, and the Father That sent Me beareth witness of Me.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Concéde, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, qui ex mérito nostræ actiónis afflígimur, tuæ grátiæ consolatióne respirémus.
collect.eng: Grant, we beseech thee, Almighty God, that we who for our evil deeds are worthily punished, may, by the comfort of thy grace, mercifully be relieved.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 9:11-12)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Christus assístens Póntifex futurórum bonórum, per ámplius et perféctius tabernáculum non manu factum, id est, non hujus creatiónis: neque per sánguinem hircórum aut vitulórum, sed per próprium sánguinem introívit semel in Sancta, ætérna redemptióne invénta.
laudes.capitulum.eng: But Christ, being come an high priest of the good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hand, that is, not of this creation: Neither by the blood of goats, or of calves, but by his own blood, entered once into the holies, having obtained eternal redemption.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 9:13-14)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Si enim sanguis hircórum, et taurórum, et cinis vítulæ aspérsus inquinátos sanctíficat ad emundatiónem carnis: quanto magis sanguis Christi, qui per Spíritum Sanctum semetípsum óbtulit immaculátum Deo, emundábit consciéntiam nostram ab opéribus mórtuis, ad serviéndum Deo vivénti?
sexta.capitulum.eng: For if the blood of goats and of oxen, and the ashes of an heifer being sprinkled, sanctify such as are defiled, to the cleansing of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God, cleanse our conscience from dead works, to serve the living God?

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 9:15)
nona.capitulum.lat: Et ídeo novi testaménti mediátor est: ut, morte intercedénte, in redemptiónem eárum prævaricatiónum, quæ erant sub prióri testaménto, repromissiónem accípiant, qui vocáti sunt ætérnæ hereditátis in Christo Jesu, Dómino nostro.
nona.capitulum.eng: And therefore he is the mediator of the new testament: that by means of his death, for the redemption of those trangressions, which were under the former testament, they that are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dicébat Jesus * turbis Judæórum, et princípibus sacerdótum: Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit: proptérea vos non audítis, quia ex Deo non estis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Jesus said * unto the multitudes of the Jews and unto the Chief Priests: He that is of God heareth God's words; ye, therefore, hear them not, because ye are not of God.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Abraham pater vester * exsultávit ut vidéret diem meum: vidit, et gavísus est.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see My day * and he saw it, and was glad.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Vide, Dómine, * afflictiónem meam, quóniam eréctus est inimícus meus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O Lord, behold my affliction; * for the enemy hath magnified himself.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: In tribulatióne * invocávi Dóminum, et exaudívit me in latitúdine.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: I called upon the Lord * in my distress; and He answered me, and set me at large.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Judicásti, Dómine, * causam ánimæ meæ, defénsor vitæ meæ, Dómine Deus meus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: O Lord, Thou hast pleaded the cause of my soul; * Thou hast redeemed my life, O Lord my God.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Pópule meus, * quid feci tibi, aut quid moléstus fui? Respónde mihi.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O My people, what have I done unto thee? * or wherein have I wearied thee? testify against Me.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Numquid rédditur * pro bono malum, quia fodérunt fóveam ánimæ meæ.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Shall evil be recompensed for good? * for they have digged a pit for My soul.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 9:11-12)
