vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Christus assístens Póntifex futurórum bonórum, per ámplius et perféctius tabernáculum non manu factum, id est, non hujus creatiónis: neque per sánguinem hircórum aut vitulórum, sed per próprium sánguinem introívit semel in Sancta, ætérna redemptióne invénta.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: But Christ, being come an high priest of the good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle not made with hand, that is, not of this creation: Neither by the blood of goats, or of calves, but by his own blood, entered once into the holies, having obtained eternal redemption.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, famíliam tuam propítius réspice: ut, te largiénte, regátur in córpore; et, te servánte, custodiátur in mente.
collect.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: In die magno * festivitátis stabat Jesus, et clamábat dicens: Si quis sitit, véniat ad me, et bibat.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: In the last day, that great day of the Feast, * Jesus stood and cried, saying: If any man thirst, let Him come unto Me, and drink.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Si quis sitit, * véniat ad me, et bibat: et de ventre ejus fluent aquæ vivæ, dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: If any man thirst, let him come unto Me, * and drink, and out of his belly shall flow living water, saith the Lord.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, famíliam tuam propítius réspice: ut, te largiénte, regátur in córpore; et, te servánte, custodiátur in mente.
collect.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Tempus meum * nondum advénit, tempus autem vestrum semper est parátum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: My time is not yet come * but your time is always ready.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Vos ascéndite * ad diem festum hunc: ego autem non ascéndam, quia tempus meum nondum advénit.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Go ye up unto this Feast; * I go not up (yet) unto this Feast, for My time is not yet full come.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, famíliam tuam propítius réspice: ut, te largiénte, regátur in córpore; et, te servánte, custodiátur in mente.
collect.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Oves meæ * vocem meam áudiunt: et ego Dóminus agnósco eas.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: My sheep hear My voice, * and I, the Lord, know them.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Multa bona ópera * operátus sum vobis: propter quod opus vultis me occídere?
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Many good works have I wrought * among you, and for them ye go about to kill Me?

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, famíliam tuam propítius réspice: ut, te largiénte, regátur in córpore; et, te servánte, custodiátur in mente.
collect.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Quid molésti estis * huic mulíeri? opus enim bonum operáta est in me.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: The Master saith: My time is at hand; * I will keep the Passover at thy house with My disciples.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Desidério desiderávi * hoc Pascha manducáre vobíscum, ántequam pátiar.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: With desire I have desired * to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, famíliam tuam propítius réspice: ut, te largiénte, regátur in córpore; et, te servánte, custodiátur in mente.
collect.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Isa 53:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Quis crédidit audítui nostro? et bráchium Dómini cui revelátum est? Et ascéndet sicut virgúltum coram eo, et sicut radix de terra sitiénti.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? And he shall grow up as a tender plant before him, and as a root out of a thirsty ground.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Isa 53:5)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Ipse vulnerátus est propter iniquitátes nostras, attrítus est propter scélera nostra: disciplína pacis nostræ super eum, et livóre ejus sanáti sumus.
sexta.capitulum.eng: But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins: the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his bruises we are healed.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Isa 53:8)
nona.capitulum.lat: Generatiónem ejus quis enarrábit, quia abscíssus est de terra vivéntium; propter scelus pópuli mei percússi eum.
nona.capitulum.eng: Who shall declare his generation? because he is cut oh out of the land of the living: for the wickedness of my people have I struck him.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Mihi jam non sis amára,
Fac me tecum plángere.

Fac ut portem Christi mortem,
Passiónis fac consórtem,
Et plagas recólere.

Fac me plagis vulnerári,
Fac me cruce inebriári,
Et cruóre Fílii.

Flammis ne urar succénsus,
Per te Virgo sim defénsus
In die judícii.

Christe, cum sit hinc exíre,
Da per Matrem me veníre
Ad palmam victóriæ.

Quando corpus moriétur,
Fac ut ánimæ donétur
Paradísi glória.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Virgin of all virgins blest!
Listen to my fond request:
Let me share thy grief divine;

Let me, to my latest breath,
In my body bear the death
Of that dying Son of thine.

Wounded with his every wound,
Steep my soul till it hath swooned
In his very blood away;

Be to me, O Virgin, nigh,
Lest in flames I burn and die,
In that awful judgement day.

Christ, when thou shalt call me hence,
Be thy Mother my defence,
Be thy cross my victory;

While my body here decays,
May my soul thy goodness praise,
Safe in Paradise with thee.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Juxta crucem lacrimósa,
Dum pendébat Fílius.

Cujus ánimam geméntem,
Contristátam et doléntem,
Pertransívit gládius.

O quam tristis et afflícta
Fuit illa benedícta
Mater Unigéniti!

Quæ mœrébat, et dolébat,
Pia Mater dum vidébat
Nati pœnas ínclyti.

Quis est homo qui non fleret,
Matrem Christi si vidéret
In tanto supplício?

Quis non posset contristári,
Christi Matrem contemplári
Doléntem cum Fílio?

Pro peccátis suæ gentis
Vidit Jesum in torméntis,
Et flagéllis súbditum.

Vidit suum dulcem natum,
Moriéndo desolátum,
Dum emísit spíritum.

Eja, Mater, fons amóris,
Me sentíre vim dolóris
Fac, ut tecum lúgeam:

Fac ut árdeat cor meum
In amándo Christum Deum,
Ut sibi compláceam.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
At the cross her station keeping,
Stood the mournful Mother weeping,
Close to Jesus to the last:

Through her heart, his sorrow sharing,
All his bitter anguish bearing,
Now at length the sword had passed.

Oh, how sad and sore distressed
Was that Mother highly blest
Of the sole-begotten One!

Christ above in torment hangs;
She beneath beholds the pangs
Of her dying glorious Son.

Is there one who would not weep,
Whelmed in miseries so deep
Christ's dear Mother to behold?

Can the human heart refrain
From partaking in her pain,
In that Mother's pain untold?

Bruised, derided, cursed, defiled,
She beheld her tender Child
All with bloody scourges rent;

For the sins of his own nation,
Saw him hang in desolation,
Till his Spirit forth he sent.

O thou Mother! fount of love!
Touch my spirit from above,
Make my heart with thine accord:

Make me feel as thou hast felt;
Make my soul to glow and melt
With the love of Christ my Lord.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum vidísset Jesus * matrem stantem juxta crucem, et discípulum quem diligébat, dicit matri suæ: Múlier, ecce fílius tuus. Deínde dicit discípulo: Ecce Mater tua.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When Jesus saw His Mother, * and the disciple whom He loved, standing by the Cross, He saith unto His Mother: Woman, behold thy Son! Then saith He to the disciple: Behold thy Mother!

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Cum vidísset Jesus * matrem stantem juxta crucem, et discípulum quem diligébat, dicit matri suæ: Múlier, ecce fílius tuus. Deínde dicit discípulo: Ecce Mater tua.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: When Jesus saw His Mother, * and the disciple whom He loved, standing by the Cross, He saith unto His Mother: Woman, behold thy Son! Then saith He to the disciple: Behold thy Mother!

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: Pray for us, O Virgin most sorrowful.
laudes.versicle.engR: That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: Pray for us, O Virgin most sorrowful.
vesperae.versicle.engR: That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Vadam ad montem * myrrhæ et ad collem thuris.;;115
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, * and to the hill of frankincense.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Diléctus meus * cándidus et rubicúndus: comæ cápitis ejus sicut púrpura regis vincta canálibus.;;119
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: My beloved * is white and ruddy; the hair of his head is like kingly purple, bound in tresses.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Quo ábiit * diléctus tuus, o pulchérrima mulíerum? quo diléctus tuus declinávit.;;139
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Whither is thy beloved gone, * O thou fairest among women? Whither is thy beloved turned aside?

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Fascículus myrrhæ * diléctus meus mihi inter úbera mea commorábitur.;;140
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie betwixt my breasts.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Fulcíte me flóribus * stipáte me malis, quia amóre lángueo.;;141
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Revive me with flowers, * stay me up with apples, for I am swooning with love.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Isa 53:1-2)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Quis crédidit audítui nostro? et bráchium Dómini cui revelátum est? Et ascéndet sicut virgúltum coram eo, et sicut radix de terra sitiénti.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Who hath believed our report? and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? And he shall grow up as a tender plant before him, and as a root out of a thirsty ground.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, in cujus passióne, secúndum Simeónis prophetíam, dulcíssimam ánimam gloriósæ Vírginis et Matris Maríæ dolóris gládius pertransívit: concéde, propítius; ut qui transfixiónem ejus et passiónem venerándo recólimus, gloriósis méritis et précibus ómnium Sanctórum cruci fidéliter astántium intercedéntibus, passiónis tuæ efféctum felícem consequámur:
collect.eng: O God, at Whose Passion, according to the prophecy of Simeon, a sword of sorrow pierced through the gentle soul of the glorious Maiden and Mother Mary, mercifully grant to as many as do ever remember with awe how that her soul was pierced and Thou didst suffer, even for all such be Thou entreated, for the sake and by the prayers of all thy glorious and holy servants who stood so loyally by thy Cross, and grant unto the same, that for them thy life-giving Death may not have been in vain.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Clarífica me, Pater, * apud temetípsum claritáte, quam hábui priúsquam mundus fíeret.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Father, glorify Thou Me * with thine Own Self, with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus, famíliam tuam propítius réspice: ut, te largiénte, regátur in córpore; et, te servánte, custodiátur in mente.
collect.eng: We beseech thee, Almighty God, mercifully to look upon this thy family, that by thy great goodness they may be governed and preserved evermore, both in body and soul.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Phil 2:5-7)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Hoc enim sentíte in vobis, quod et in Christo Jesu: qui, cum in forma Dei esset, non rapínam arbitrátus est esse se æquálem Deo: sed semetípsum exinanívit, formam servi accípiens, in similitúdinem hóminum factus, et hábitu invéntus ut homo.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men, and in habit found as a man.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Phil 2:8-9)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Humiliávit semetípsum factus obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Propter quod et Deus exaltávit illum, et donávit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen.
sexta.capitulum.eng: He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even to the death of the cross. For which cause God also hath exalted him, and hath given him a name which is above all names:

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Phil 2:10-11)
nona.capitulum.lat: In nómine Jesu omne genu flectátur cæléstium, terréstrium, et infernórum: et omnis lingua confiteátur, quia Dóminus Jesus Christus in glória est Dei Patris.
nona.capitulum.eng: That in the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth, and under the earth: And that every tongue should confess that the Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Turba multa, * quæ convénerat ad diem festum, clamábat Dómino: Benedíctus qui venit in nómine Dómini: Hosánna in excélsis.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Much people that were come to the Feast, cried * unto the Lord: Blessed is He That cometh in the Name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Cœpérunt * omnes turbæ descendéntium gaudéntes laudáre Deum voce magna super ómnibus quas víderant virtútibus, dicéntes: Benedíctus qui venit Rex in nómine Dómini, pax in cœlo et glória in excélsis.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: It is written: I will smite the Shepherd, * and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad, but after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee: there shall ye see Me, saith the Lord.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Dóminus Deus * auxiliátor meus: et ídeo non sum confúsus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: The Lord God will help me * and therefore I am not confounded.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Circumdántes * circumdedérunt me: et in nómine Dómini vindicábor in eis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: They compassed me about, * yea, they compassed me about but in the Name of the Lord! I will destroy them.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Júdica causam meam: * defénde, quia potens es, Dómine.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Judge Thou my cause, * and redeem me, O Lord, for Thou art mighty to save.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Cum Angelis * et púeris fidéles inveniámur, triumphatóri mortis clamántes: Hosánna in excélsis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Fare we with Angels and men in faith to meet the Redeemer, * hailing the Slayer of death with joyful shouts of “Hosanna in the highest!”

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Confundántur * qui me persequúntur, et non confúndar ego, Dómine, Deus meus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Let them be confounded that persecute me; * but let not me be confounded, O Lord my God.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Phil 2:5-7)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Hoc enim sentíte in vobis, quod et in Christo Jesu: qui, cum in forma Dei esset, non rapínam arbitrátus est esse se æquálem Deo: sed semetípsum exinanívit, formam servi accípiens, in similitúdinem hóminum factus, et hábitu invéntus ut homo.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers: For let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: Who being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men, and in habit found as a man.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui humáno géneri, ad imitándum humilitátis exémplum, Salvatórem nostrum carnem súmere, et crucem subíre fecísti: concéde propítius; ut et patiéntiæ ipsíus habére documénta, et resurrectiónis consórtia mereámur.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who, of thy tender love towards mankind, hast sent thy Son our Saviour Jesus Christ to take upon Him our flesh and to suffer death upon the Cross, that all mankind should follow the example of His great humility; mercifully grant, that we may both follow the example of His patience, and also be made partakers of His resurrection.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Non habéres * in me potestátem, nisi désuper tibi datum fuísset.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: And now, O Father, glorify Thou Me * with thine Own Self, with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Non habéres * in me potestátem, nisi désuper tibi datum fuísset.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Thou couldest have no power * at all against Me, except it were given thee from above.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Fáciem meam * non avérti ab increpántibus, et conspuéntibus in me.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: I hid not my face * from shame and spitting.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Frámea, suscitáre * advérsus eos, qui dispérgunt gregem meum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Awake, O sword, * against them that scatter my flock.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Appendérunt * mercédem meam trigínta argénteis: quibus appretiátus sum ab eis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: They took the thirty pieces of silver, * my price, that I was prized at of them.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Inundavérunt aquæ * super caput meum: dixi, Périi: invocábo nomen tuum, Dómine Deus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Waters flowed over mine head; * I said I am cut off; I will call upon thy Name, O Lord God.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Lábia insurgéntium, * et cogitatiónes eórum vide, Dómine.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: O Lord, behold the lips * of those that rose up against me, and their device.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui humáno géneri, ad imitándum humilitátis exémplum, Salvatórem nostrum carnem súmere, et crucem subíre fecísti: concéde propítius; ut et patiéntiæ ipsíus habére documénta, et resurrectiónis consórtia mereámur.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who, of thy tender love towards mankind, hast sent thy Son our Saviour Jesus Christ to take upon Him our flesh and to suffer death upon the Cross, that all mankind should follow the example of His great humility; mercifully grant, that we may both follow the example of His patience, and also be made partakers of His resurrection.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Nemo * tollit a me ánimam meam, sed ego pono eam, et íterum sumo eam.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Now, before the Feast of the Passover, as Jesus knew that His hour was come, * having loved His Own which were in the world, He loved them unto the end.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Potestátem hábeo * ponéndi ánimam meam, et íterum suméndi eam.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: I have power * to lay down my life: and to take it up again.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Vide, Dómine, * et consídera, quóniam tríbulor: velóciter exáudi me.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Behold, O Lord, and see, * for I am in trouble; hear me speedily.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Discérne causam meam, * Dómine: ab hómine iníquo et dolóso éripe me.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Plead my cause, * O Lord; deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Dum tribulárer, * clamávi ad Dóminum de ventre ínferi, et exaudívit me.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the Lord, * and He heard me out of the belly of hell.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Dómine, vim pátior, * respónde pro me: quia néscio quid dicam inimícis meis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O Lord, I am oppressed, * undertake Thou for me; for I know not what to say unto mine enemies.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Dixérunt ímpii: * Opprimámus virum justum, quóniam contrárius est opéribus nostris.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The ungodly said Let us oppress the righteous man, * because he is clean contrary to our doings.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui humáno géneri, ad imitándum humilitátis exémplum, Salvatórem nostrum carnem súmere, et crucem subíre fecísti: concéde propítius; ut et patiéntiæ ipsíus habére documénta, et resurrectiónis consórtia mereámur.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who, of thy tender love towards mankind, hast sent thy Son our Saviour Jesus Christ to take upon Him our flesh and to suffer death upon the Cross, that all mankind should follow the example of His great humility; mercifully grant, that we may both follow the example of His patience, and also be made partakers of His resurrection.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Simon, dormis? * non potuísti una hora vigiláre mecum?
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Simon, do you sleep? * Could you not watch one hour with me?

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Ancílla dixit * Petro: Vere tu ex illis es: nam et loquéla tua maniféstum te facit.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The handmaid said to Peter: * Surely thou also art one of them; for even thy speech doth discover thee.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Líbera me * de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus meus: et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Deliver me * from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall extol thy justice.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Contumélias * et terróres passus sum ab eis: et Dóminus mecum est tamquam bellátor fortis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: I received * injuries and terrors from them: but the Lord is with me as a strong warrior.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ipsi vero * in vanum quæsierunt animam meam, introibunt in inferiora terræ.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: But thou, O Lord, * knowest all their plans to put me to death.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Omnes inimíci mei * audiérunt malum meum: Dómine, lætáti sunt, quóniam tu fecisti.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: All my enemies have heard of my evil, * they have rejoiced that thou, O Lord, hast done it.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Alliga, Dómine, * in vinculis natiónes Géntium, et reges earum in compédibus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The Lord helpeth them * to right that suffer wrong, but as for the way of the ungodly, he turneth it upside down.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui humáno géneri, ad imitándum humilitátis exémplum, Salvatórem nostrum carnem súmere, et crucem subíre fecísti: concéde propítius; ut et patiéntiæ ipsíus habére documénta, et resurrectiónis consórtia mereámur.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who, of thy tender love towards mankind, hast sent thy Son our Saviour Jesus Christ to take upon Him our flesh and to suffer death upon the Cross, that all mankind should follow the example of His great humility; mercifully grant, that we may both follow the example of His patience, and also be made partakers of His resurrection.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Tráditor autem * dedit eis signum, dicens: Quem osculátus fúero, ipse est, tenéte eum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Now he that betrayed Him * gave them a sign, saying: Whomsoever I shall kiss, That Same is He: hold Him fast.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Cenántibus autem illis * accépit Jesus panem, et benedíxit, ac fregit, dedítque discípulis suis.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And, as they were eating * Jesus took bread, and blessed, and broke it, and gave to His disciples.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.lat: Homo pacis meæ, in quo sperávi.
laudes.versicle.eng: Mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted;
laudes.versicle.latR: Qui edébat panes meos, ampliávit advérsum me supplantatiónem.
laudes.versicle.engR: Which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Justificéris, Dómine, * in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum judicáris.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O Lord, Thou shalt be justified * when Thou speakest, and be clear when Thou art judged.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Dóminus * tamquam ovis ad víctimam ductus est, et non apéruit os suum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord was brought as a lamb * to the slaughter, and He opened not His mouth.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Contrítum est * cor meum in médio mei, contremuérunt ómnia ossa mea.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Mine heart is broken within me * all my bones tremble.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Exhortátus es * in virtúte tua, et in refectióne sancta tua, Dómine.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O Lord, Thou hast spoken unto us * in thy strength, and in thy Holy Banquet.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Oblátus est * quia ipse vóluit, et peccáta nostra ipse portávit.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: He was offered up because He willed it * and He bore our sins.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Cálicem * salutáris accípiam et nomen Dómini invocábo.;;115
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: I will take the cup of salvation; * and call upon the Name of the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Cum his, * qui odérunt pacem eram pacíficus: dum loquébar illis, impugnábant me gratis.;;119
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: With them * that hate peace I was peaceable; when I spoke unto them they fought against me without a cause.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ab homínibus * iníquis líbera me, Dómine.;;139
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: O Lord, preserve me * from the wicked man.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Custódi me * a láqueo, quem statuérunt mihi, et a scándalis operántium iniquitátem.;;140
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Keep me * from the snare which they have laid for me, and the gins of the workers of iniquity.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Considerábam * ad déxteram, et vidébam, et non erat qui cognósceret me.;;141
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: I looked * on my right hand and beheld: but there was no man that would know me.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Christus factus est pro nobis obédiens usque ad mortem. _ Réspice, quǽsumus, Dómine, super hanc famíliam tuam, pro qua Dóminus noster Jesus Christus non dubitávit mánibus tradi nocéntium, et crucis subíre torméntum: (rubrica cisterciensis)
collect.eng: Christ became obedient for us unto death. _ Look down, we beseech thee, O Lord, on this thy family, for which our Lord Jesus Christ did not hesitate to be delivered up into the hands of wicked men, and to suffer the torment of the Cross.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Posuérunt * super caput ejus causam ipsíus scriptam: Jesus Nazarénus, Rex Judæórum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: They set up over his head his accusation written: * Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Cum accepísset acétum, * dixit: Consummátum est: et inclináto cápite, emísit spíritum.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: When He had received the vinegar, * he said: It is finished! and he bowed his Head, and gave up the Ghost.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: He hath set me in dark places.
laudes.versicle.engR: As they that be dead of old.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: He hath set me in dark places.
vesperae.versicle.engR: As they that be dead of old.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Próprio * Fílio suo non pepércit Deus, sed pro nobis ómnibus trádidit illum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: God spared not His Own Son * but delivered Him up for us all.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Anxiátus est super me * spíritus meus, in me turbátum est cor meum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: My spirit is overwhelmed within me; * my heart within me is troubled.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ait latro ad latrónem: * Nos quidem digna factis recípimus, hic autem quid fecit? Meménto mei, Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: One thief said unto the other: * We indeed receive the due reward of our deeds, but what hath this man done? Lord, remember me, when thou comest into thy kingdom.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Cum conturbáta fúerit * ánima mea, Dómine, misericórdiæ memor eris.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Lord, when my soul is troubled, * thou wilt remember mercy.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Meménto mei, * Dómine, dum véneris in regnum tuum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Lord, remember me * when thou comest into thy kingdom.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: @Tempora/Quad6-4
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: God spared not His Own Son * but delivered Him up for us all.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui humáno géneri, ad imitándum humilitátis exémplum, Salvatórem nostrum carnem súmere, et crucem subíre fecísti: concéde propítius; ut et patiéntiæ ipsíus habére documénta, et resurrectiónis consórtia mereámur.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who, of thy tender love towards mankind, hast sent thy Son our Saviour Jesus Christ to take upon Him our flesh and to suffer death upon the Cross, that all mankind should follow the example of His great humility; mercifully grant, that we may both follow the example of His patience, and also be made partakers of His resurrection.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Mulíeres * sedéntes ad monuméntum lamentabántur, flentes Dóminum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: There were women sitting over against the sepulchre * weeping, and making lamentation for the Lord.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: My flesh shall rest in hope.
laudes.versicle.latR: Et non dabis Sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
laudes.versicle.engR: Neither wilt Thou suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: O mors, * ero mors tua, morsus tuus ero, inférne.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O death, I will be thy death; * O grave, I will be thy destruction.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Plangent eum * quasi unigénitum, quia ínnocens Dóminus occísus est.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: They shall mourn for Him * as one mourneth for his only son, for the innocent Lord hath been put to death.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Atténdite * univérsi pópuli, et vidéte dolórem meum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: O all ye nations, behold * and see my sorrow.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: A porta ínferi * érue, Dómine, ánimam meam.;;222
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O Lord, deliver my soul * from the gates of the grave.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: O vos omnes, * qui transítis per viam, atténdite et vidéte, si est dolor sicut dolor meus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: O all ye that pass by * behold, and see if there be any sorrow like unto my sorrow.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui humáno géneri, ad imitándum humilitátis exémplum, Salvatórem nostrum carnem súmere, et crucem subíre fecísti: concéde propítius; ut et patiéntiæ ipsíus habére documénta, et resurrectiónis consórtia mereámur.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who, of thy tender love towards mankind, hast sent thy Son our Saviour Jesus Christ to take upon Him our flesh and to suffer death upon the Cross, that all mankind should follow the example of His great humility; mercifully grant, that we may both follow the example of His patience, and also be made partakers of His resurrection.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 9:24)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Nescítis quod ii qui in stádio currunt, omnes quidem currunt, sed unus áccipit bravíum? Sic cúrrite ut comprehendátis.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: Know you not that they that run in the race, all run indeed, but one receiveth the prize? So run that you may obtain.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 9:25)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Omnis autem, qui in agóne conténdit, ab ómnibus se ábstinet: et illi quidem ut corruptíbilem corónam accípiant, nos autem incorrúptam.
sexta.capitulum.eng: And every one that striveth for the mastery, refraineth himself from all things: and they indeed that they may receive a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible one.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 10:4-5)
nona.capitulum.lat: Bibébant autem de spiritáli, consequénte eos, petra: petra autem erat Christus: sed non in plúribus eórum beneplácitum est Deo.
nona.capitulum.eng: And all drank the same spiritual drink; and they drank of the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ. But with most of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the desert.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Símile est * regnum cælórum hómini patrifamílias, qui éxiit primo mane condúcere operários in víneam suam, dicit Dóminus.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Thus saith the Lord: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, * which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dixit paterfamílias * operáriis suis: Quid hic statis tota die otiósi? At illi respondéntes dixérunt: Quia nemo nos condúxit. Ite et vos in víneam meam: et quod justum fúerit, dabo vobis.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The householder saith unto his labourers: * Why stand ye here all the day idle? But they answered and said: Because no man hath hired us. Go ye also into my vineyard, and whatsoever is right, that will I give you.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: Lord, thou hast been our refuge.
laudes.versicle.engR: From generation to generation.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Miserére * mei, Deus, et a delícto meo munda me: quia tibi soli peccávi.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Have mercy upon me, * O God, and cleanse me from my sin, for against thee only have I sinned.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Confitébor * tibi, quóniam exaudísti me.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: I will praise thee, * for thou hast heard me.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo, quia factus es adjútor meus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: O God, Thou art my God, * early will I seek thee, because thou hast been my help.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Benedíctus es * in firmaménto cæli, et laudábilis in sǽcula, Deus noster.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Blessed art thou, * O our God, in the firmament of heaven, and worthy to be praised above all for ever.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Laudáte * Dóminum de cælis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Praise ye the Lord * from the heavens.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 9:24)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Nescítis quod ii qui in stádio currunt, omnes quidem currunt, sed unus áccipit bravíum? Sic cúrrite ut comprehendátis.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers: Know you not that they that run in the race, all run indeed, but one receiveth the prize? So run that you may obtain.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: ut, qui juste pro peccátis nostris afflígimur, pro tui nóminis glória misericórditer liberémur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee favourably to hear the prayers of thy people; that we, who are justly punished for our offences, may be mercifully delivered by thy goodness, for the glory of thy Name.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: @Psalterium/Special/Major Special:Feria2C Ant 3
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: These last have wrought but one hour, * and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: ut, qui juste pro peccátis nostris afflígimur, pro tui nóminis glória misericórditer liberémur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee favourably to hear the prayers of thy people; that we, who are justly punished for our offences, may be mercifully delivered by thy goodness, for the glory of thy Name.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dixit autem paterfamílias: * Amíce, non fácio tibi injúriam: nonne ex denário convenísti mecum? tolle quod tuum est, et vade.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And the householder said: * Friend, I do thee no wrong didst not thou agree with me for a penny? Take that is thine, and go thy way.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: ut, qui juste pro peccátis nostris afflígimur, pro tui nóminis glória misericórditer liberémur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee favourably to hear the prayers of thy people; that we, who are justly punished for our offences, may be mercifully delivered by thy goodness, for the glory of thy Name.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Tolle quod tuum est, * et vade; quia ego bonus sum, dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Take that thine is, * and go thy way; for I am good, saith the Lord.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: ut, qui juste pro peccátis nostris afflígimur, pro tui nóminis glória misericórditer liberémur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee favourably to hear the prayers of thy people; that we, who are justly punished for our offences, may be mercifully delivered by thy goodness, for the glory of thy Name.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Non licet mihi, * quod volo, fácere? an óculus tuus nequam est? quia ego bonus sum, dicit Dóminus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Is it not lawful for me * to do what I will? Is thine eye evil, because I am gracious?” saith the Lord.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces pópuli tui, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: ut, qui juste pro peccátis nostris afflígimur, pro tui nóminis glória misericórditer liberémur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee favourably to hear the prayers of thy people; that we, who are justly punished for our offences, may be mercifully delivered by thy goodness, for the glory of thy Name.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 11:19-20)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Libénter suffértis insipiéntes, cum sitis ipsi sapiéntes: sustinétis enim si quis vos in servitútem rédigit, si quis dévorat, si quis áccipit, si quis extóllitur, si quis in fáciem vos cædit.
laudes.capitulum.eng: For you gladly suffer the foolish; whereas yourselves are wise. For you suffer if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take from you, if a man be lifted up, if a man strike you on the face.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 11:25)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Ter virgis cæsus sum, semel lapidátus sum: ter naufrágium feci, nocte et die in profúndo maris fui.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once I was stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I was in the depth of the sea.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 12:9)
nona.capitulum.lat: Libénter ígitur gloriábor in infirmitátibus meis, ut inhábitet in me virtus Christi.
nona.capitulum.eng: And he said to me: My grace is sufficient for thee; for power is made perfect in infirmity. Gladly therefore will I glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may dwell in me.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum turba * plúrima convenírent ad Jesum, et de civitátibus properárent ad eum, dixit per similitúdinem: Exiit qui séminat, semináre semen suum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When much people were gathered together to Jesus, * and were come to Him out of every city, He spoke by a parable: A sower went out to sow his seed.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Vobis datum est * nosse mystérium regni Dei, céteris autem in parábolis, dixit Jesus discípulis suis.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Jesus said to His disciples: * Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to others in parables.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Secúndum magnam misericórdiam * tuam miserére mei, Deus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Have mercy upon me, O God, * after thy great mercy.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Si mihi Dóminus * salvátor fúerit, non timébo, quid fáciat mihi homo.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: If the Lord be my Saviour * I will not fear what man can do unto me.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: In velaménto * clamávi valde dilúculo: Deus, Deus meus, ad te de luce vígilo.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Within the veil I cried betimes: * O God, Thou art my God, early will I seek thee.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Hymnum dicámus * Dómino Deo nostro.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Let us sing praises * to the Lord our God.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: In excélsis, * laudáte Deum.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: In the high places, * praise ye God.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 11:19-20)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Libénter suffértis insipiéntes, cum sitis ipsi sapiéntes: sustinétis enim si quis vos in servitútem rédigit, si quis dévorat, si quis áccipit, si quis extóllitur, si quis in fáciem vos cædit.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: For you gladly suffer the foolish; whereas yourselves are wise. For you suffer if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take from you, if a man be lifted up, if a man strike you on the face.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nulla nostra actióne confídimus: concéde propítius; ut, contra advérsa ómnia Doctóris géntium protectióne muniámur.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we put not our trust in anything that we do, mercifully grant that through the protection of the Teacher of the Gentiles we may be defended against all adversity.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Si culmen * veri honóris quǽritis, ad illam cæléstem pátriam quantócius properáte.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: If ye would be truly honourable, * strive after our Fatherland which is in heaven.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nulla nostra actióne confídimus: concéde propítius; ut, contra advérsa ómnia Doctóris géntium protectióne muniámur.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we put not our trust in anything that we do, mercifully grant that through the protection of the Teacher of the Gentiles we may be defended against all adversity.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Semen est * verbum Dei, sator autem Christus: omnis qui invénit eum, manébit in ætérnum.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: The seed is the word of God, * and the Sower is Christ; if any man find Him, he shall never be moved.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nulla nostra actióne confídimus: concéde propítius; ut, contra advérsa ómnia Doctóris géntium protectióne muniámur.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we put not our trust in anything that we do, mercifully grant that through the protection of the Teacher of the Gentiles we may be defended against all adversity.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Quod autem cécidit * in terram bonam, hi sunt, qui in corde bono et óptimo fructum áfferunt in patiéntia.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But that on the good ground * are they which in an honest and good heart bring forth fruit with patience.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nulla nostra actióne confídimus: concéde propítius; ut, contra advérsa ómnia Doctóris géntium protectióne muniámur.
collect.eng: O God, Who seest that we put not our trust in anything that we do, mercifully grant that through the protection of the Teacher of the Gentiles we may be defended against all adversity.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 13:1)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Si linguis hóminum loquar, et Angelórum, caritátem autem non hábeam, factus sum velut æs sonans, aut cýmbalum tínniens.
laudes.capitulum.eng: Brothers: If I speak with the tongues of men, and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 13:8-9)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Cáritas nunquam éxcidit: sive prophetíæ evacuabúntur, sive linguæ cessábunt, sive sciéntia destruétur. Ex parte enim cognóscimus, et ex parte prophetámus.
sexta.capitulum.eng: Charity never falleth away: whether prophecies shall be made void, or tongues shall cease, or knowledge shall be destroyed. For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 13:13)
nona.capitulum.lat: Nunc autem manent fides, spes, cáritas, tria hæc: major autem horum est cáritas.
nona.capitulum.eng: And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Ecce ascéndimus * Jerosólymam, et consummabúntur ómnia quæ scripta sunt de Fílio hóminis: tradétur enim géntibus, et illudétur, et conspuétur: et postquam flagelláverint, occídent eum, et tértia die resúrget.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, * and all things that are written by the Prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished; for He shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked and spitted on; and they shall scourge Him, and put Him to death, and the third day He shall rise again.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Stans autem Jesus, * jussit cæcum addúci ad se, et ait illi: Quid vis ut fáciam tibi? Dómine, ut vídeam. Et Jesus ait illi: Réspice, fides tua te salvum fecit. Et conféstim vidit, et sequebátur illum, magníficans Deum.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And Jesus stood, * and commanded the blind man to be brought unto Him, and He asked him, saying: What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee? Lord, that I may receive my sight. And Jesus said unto him: Receive thy sight, thy faith hath saved thee. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Him, glorifying God.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Secúndum multitúdinem * miseratiónum tuárum, Dómine, dele iniquitátem meam.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O Lord, according to the multitude of thy tender mercies, * blot out my transgressions.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Deus meus es tu, * et confitébor tibi: Deus meus es tu, et exaltábo te.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Thou art my God, * and I will praise thee; Thou art my God, and I will exalt thee.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Ad te de luce * vígilo, Deus, ut vídeam virtútem tuam.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: O God, early will I seek thee, * to see thy power.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Hymnum dícite, * et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Sing praises, * and exalt Him above all for ever.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Omnes Angeli * ejus laudáte Dóminum de cælis.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Praise ye the Lord * from the heavens, all His angels.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (1 Cor 13:1)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Fratres: Si linguis hóminum loquar, et Angelórum, caritátem autem non hábeam, factus sum velut æs sonans, aut cýmbalum tínniens.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Brothers: If I speak with the tongues of men, and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: atque, a peccatórum vínculis absolútos, ab omni nos adversitáte custódi.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully hear our prayers; loose us from the chains of our sins and keep us from all adversity.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Et qui præíbant, * increpábant eum ut tacéret: ipse vero multo magis clamábat: Miserére mei, Fili David.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: And they that went before * rebuked him, that he should hold his peace. But he cried out so much the more: “Have mercy on me, thou Son of David.”

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: atque, a peccatórum vínculis absolútos, ab omni nos adversitáte custódi.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully hear our prayers; loose us from the chains of our sins and keep us from all adversity.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Miserére mei, * Fili David. Quid vis ut fáciam tibi? Dómine, ut vídeam.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Have mercy on me, * thou Son of David. What wouldst thou that I should do unto thee? Lord, that I may receive my sight.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: atque, a peccatórum vínculis absolútos, ab omni nos adversitáte custódi.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully hear our prayers; loose us from the chains of our sins and keep us from all adversity.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum jejunátis, * nolíte fíeri sicut hypócritæ, tristes.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When ye fast, * be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Thesaurizáte vobis * thesáuros in cælo, ubi nec ærúgo, nec tínea demolítur.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, * where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: atque, a peccatórum vínculis absolútos, ab omni nos adversitáte custódi.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully hear our prayers; loose us from the chains of our sins and keep us from all adversity.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Dómine, * puer meus jacet paralýticus in domo, et male torquétur: Amen dico tibi, ego véniam, et curábo eum.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Lord, * my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, and is grieviously tormented. Amen, I say unto thee, I will come and heal him.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Dómine, * non sum dignus ut intres sub tectum meum: sed tantum dic verbo, et sanábitur puer meus.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: O Lord, * I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, and my servant shall be healed.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: atque, a peccatórum vínculis absolútos, ab omni nos adversitáte custódi.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully hear our prayers; loose us from the chains of our sins and keep us from all adversity.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Cum facis * eleemósynam nésciat sinístra tua quid fáciat déxtera tua.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: When thou dost * alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Tu autem cum oráveris, * intra in cubículum tuum: et clauso óstio, ora Patrem tuum.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: But thou when thou shalt pray, * enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: atque, a peccatórum vínculis absolútos, ab omni nos adversitáte custódi.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully hear our prayers; loose us from the chains of our sins and keep us from all adversity.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Me étenim * de die in diem quærunt, et scire vias meas volunt.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: For they seek me * from day to day, and desire to know my ways.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Preces nostras, quǽsumus, Dómine, cleménter exáudi: atque, a peccatórum vínculis absolútos, ab omni nos adversitáte custódi.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech You, mercifully hear our prayers; loose us from the chains of our sins and keep us from all adversity.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui in Fílii tui humilitáte jacéntem mundum erexísti: fidélibus tuis perpétuam concéde lætítiam; ut, quos perpétuæ mortis eripuísti cásibus, gáudiis fácias pérfrui sempitérnis.
collect.eng: O God, Whose Son hath humbled Himself, and Who hast through Him raised up the whole world, grant to thy faithful people everlasting joy; and as Thou hast delivered them from the bitter pains of eternal death, make them to be glad for ever in thy presence.

collect.label: Orátio

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui errántibus, ut in viam possint redíre justítiæ, veritátis tuæ lumen osténdis: da cunctis, qui christiána professióne censéntur, et illa respúere, quæ huic inimíca sunt nómini; et ea, quæ sunt apta, sectári.
collect.eng: Almighty God, Who showest to them that be in error the light of thy truth, to the intent that they may return into the way of righteousness grant unto all them that are admitted into the fellowship of Christ's Religion, that they may eschew those things that are contrary to their profession, and follow all such things as are agreeable to the same.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui fidélium mentes uníus éfficis voluntátis: da pópulis tuis id amáre quod prǽcipis, id desideráre quod promíttis; ut inter mundánas varietátes ibi nostra fixa sint corda, ubi vera sunt gáudia.
collect.eng: O God, of Whom it cometh that the minds of thy faithful people be all of one will, grant unto the same thy people that they may love the thing which Thou commandest, and desire that which Thou dost promise, that so, amid the sundry and manifold changes of the world, our hearts may surely there be fixed, where true joys are to be found.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Dómine Jesu Christe, qui, Maríæ et Joseph súbditus, domésticam vitam ineffabílibus virtútibus consecrásti: fac nos, utriúsque auxílio, Famíliæ sanctæ tuæ exémplis ínstrui; et consórtium cónsequi sempitérnum:
collect.eng: Lord Jesus Christ, who subject to Mary and Joseph, didst consecrate family life by thy unspeakable virtues, aid us by their united intercession to profit by the examples of thy Holy Family, and attain to their everlasting companionship:

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui cæléstia simul et terréna moderáris: supplicatiónes pópuli tui cleménter exáudi; et pacem tuam nostris concéde tempóribus.
collect.eng: Almighty and eternal God, as thou govern all things in heaven and on earth; in thy mercy hear the supplication of thy people, and grant thy peace in our times.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, infirmitátem nostram propítius réspice: atque, ad protegéndum nos, déxteram tuæ majestátis exténde.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, mercifully look upon our infirmities, and in all our dangers and necessities stretch forth the right hand of thy Majesty to help and defend us.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui nos in tantis perículis constitútos, pro humána scis fragilitáte non posse subsístere: da nobis salútem mentis et córporis; ut ea, quæ pro peccátis nostris pátimur, te adjuvánte vincámus.
collect.eng: O God, Who knowest us to be set in the midst of so many and great dangers, that, by reason of the frailty of our nature, we cannot always stand upright; grant to us such health of mind and body, that by thy strength and protection we may overcome all evils, whereby for our sins we are justly afflicted.

collect.lat: Famíliam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, contínua pietáte custódi: ut, quæ in sola spe grátiæ cœléstis innítitur, tua semper protectióne muniátur.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee to keep thy family continually in godliness, that they who do lean only upon the hope of thine heavenly grace, may evermore be defended by thy mighty power.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Præsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut, semper rationabília meditántes, quæ tibi sunt plácita, et dictis exsequámur et factis.
collect.eng: Grant us, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, ever to think such things as be reasonable, and in every word and work of ours, to do always that is well pleasing in thy sight.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, in te sperántium fortitúdo, adésto propítius invocatiónibus nostris: et, quia sine te nihil potest mortális infírmitas, præsta auxílium grátiæ tuæ; ut, in exsequéndis mandátis tuis, et voluntáte tibi et actióne placeámus.
collect.eng: O God, the Strength of all them that put their trust in thee, mercifully accept our prayers, and because through the weakness of our mortal nature we can do no good thing without thee, grant us the help of thy grace, that in keeping of thy commandments we may please thee, both in will and deed.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Protéctor in te sperántium, Deus, sine quo nihil est válidum, nihil sanctum; multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, te rectóre, te duce, sic transeámus per bona temporália, ut non amittámus ætérna.
collect.eng: O God, the Protector of those that hope in Thee, without Whom nothing hath strength, nothing is holy, multiply upon us Thy mercy, that with Thee as ruler and guide, we may so pass through things temporal, that we lose not things eternal.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Da nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine: ut et mundi cursus pacífice nobis tuo órdine dirigátur; et Ecclésia tua tranquílla devotióne lætétur.
collect.eng: Grant, O Lord, we beseech thee, that the course of this world may be so peaceably ordered by thy governance, that thy Church may joyfully serve thee in all godly quietness.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui diligéntibus te bona invisibília præparásti: infúnde córdibus nostris tui amóris afféctum; ut te in ómnibus et super ómnia diligéntes, promissiónes tuas, quæ omne desidérium súperant, consequámur.
collect.eng: O God, Who hast prepared for them that love thee such good things as pass man's understanding; pour into our hearts such love toward thee, that we, loving thee in all things and above all things, may obtain thy promises, which exceed all that we can desire.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus virtútum, cujus est totum quod est óptimum: ínsere pectóribus nostris amórem tui nóminis, et præsta in nobis religiónis augméntum; ut, quæ sunt bona, nútrias, ac pietátis stúdio, quæ sunt nutríta, custódias.
collect.eng: Lord of all power and might, Who art the Author and Giver of all good things, graft in our hearts the love of thy Name, increase in us true religion, nourish us with all goodness, and, of thy great mercy, keep us in the same.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, cujus providéntia in sui dispositióne non fállitur: te súpplices exorámus; ut nóxia cuncta submóveas, et ómnia nobis profutúra concédas.
collect.eng: O God, Whose never-failing Providence ordereth all things both in heaven and earth, we humbly beseech thee to put away from us all hurtful things, and to give us those things which be profitable for us.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Largíre nobis, quǽsumus, Dómine, semper spíritum cogitándi quæ recta sunt, propítius et agéndi: ut, qui sine te esse non póssumus, secúndum te vívere valeámus.
collect.eng: Grant to us, Lord, we beseech thee, the spirit to think and do always such things as be rightful, that we, who cannot do anything that is good without thee, may by thee be enabled to live according to thy will.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Páteant aures misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, précibus supplicántium: et, ut peténtibus desideráta concédas; fac eos, quæ tibi sunt plácita, postuláre.
collect.eng: Let thy merciful ears, O Lord, be open to the prayers of thy humble servants; and, that they may obtain their petitions, make them to ask such things as shall please thee.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Deus, qui omnipoténtiam tuam parcéndo máxime et miserándo maniféstas: multíplica super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut, ad tua promíssa curréntes, cæléstium bonórum fácias esse consórtes.
collect.eng: O God, Who declarest thine Almighty power most chiefly in showing mercy and pity, mercifully grant unto us such a measure of thy grace, that we, running the way of thy commandments, may obtain thy gracious promises, and be made partakers of thy heavenly treasure.

collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, qui, abundántia pietátis tuæ, et mérita súpplicum excédis et vota: effúnde super nos misericórdiam tuam; ut dimíttas quæ consciéntia métuit, et adícias quod orátio non præsúmit.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, Who art always more ready to hear than we to pray, and art wont to give more than either we desire or deserve, pour down upon us the abundance of thy mercy, forgiving us those things whereof our conscience is afraid, and giving us those good things which we are not worthy to ask.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, de cujus múnere venit, ut tibi a fidélibus tuis digne et laudabíliter serviátur: tríbue, quǽsumus, nobis; ut ad promissiónes tuas sine offensióne currámus.
collect.eng: Almighty and merciful God, of Whose only gift it cometh that thy faithful people do unto thee true and laudable service, grant, we beseech thee, that we may so faithfully serve thee in this life, that we fail not finally to attain thy heavenly promises.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Omnípotens sempitérne Deus, da nobis fídei, spei et caritátis augméntum: et, ut mereámur ássequi quod promíttis, fac nos amáre quod prǽcipis.
collect.eng: Almighty and everlasting God, give unto us the increase of faith, hope, and charity, and that we may worthily obtain that which Thou dost promise, make us to love that which Thou dost command.

collect.label: Orátio
collect.lat: Custódi, Dómine, quǽsumus, Ecclésiam tuam propitiatióne perpétua: et quia sine te lábitur humána mortálitas; tuis semper auxíliis et abstrahátur a nóxiis et ad salutária dirigátur.
collect.eng: Keep, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy Church with thy perpetual mercy, and because the frailty of man without thee cannot but fall, keep us ever by thy help from all things hurtful, and lead us to all things profitable to our salvation.

collect.lat: Da, quǽsumus, Dómine, pópulo tuo diabólica vitáre contágia: et te solum Deum pura mente sectári.
collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, grant thy people grace to withstand the temptations of the devil, and with pure hearts to follow thee the only God.

collect.lat: Omnípotens et miséricors Deus, univérsa nobis adversántia propitiátus exclúde: ut mente et córpore páriter expedíti, quæ tua sunt, líberis méntibus exsequámur.
collect.eng: O Almighty and most merciful God, of thy bountiful goodness keep us, we beseech thee, from all things that may hurt us; that we, being ready both in body and soul, may cheerfully accomplish those things that Thou wouldest have done.

collect.lat: Famíliam tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, contínua pietáte custódi: ut a cunctis adversitátibus te protegénte, sit líbera; et in bonis áctibus tuo nómini sit devóta.

collect.eng: O Lord, we beseech thee, absolve thy people from their offences, that through thy bountiful goodness we may all be delivered from the bands of those sins, which by our frailty we have committed.

laudes.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:1-2)
laudes.capitulum.lat: Multifáriam, multísque modis olim Deus loquens pátribus in prophétis: novíssime diébus istis locútus est nobis in Fílio, quem constítuit herédem universórum, per quem fecit et sǽcula.
laudes.capitulum.eng: God, who, at sundry times and in diverse manners, spoke in times past to the fathers by the prophets, last of all, in these days hath spoken to us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the world.

sexta.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:10)
sexta.capitulum.lat: Et: Tu in princípio, Dómine, terram fundásti: et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
sexta.capitulum.eng: And: Thou in the beginning, O Lord, didst found the earth: and the works of thy hands are the heavens.

nona.capitulum.label: Capitulum (Heb 1:11-12)
nona.capitulum.lat: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
nona.capitulum.eng: Converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here. Knowing that you were not redeemed with corruptible things as gold or silver, but with the precious blood of Christ.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymnus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
Natum María Vírgine.

Beátus auctor sǽculi
Servíle corpus índuit:
Ut carne carnem líberans,
Ne pérderet quos cóndidit.

Castæ Paréntis víscera
Cæléstis intrat grátia:
Venter Puéllæ bájulat
Secréta, quæ non nóverat.

Domus pudíci péctoris
Templum repénte fit Dei:
Intácta nésciens virum,
Concépit alvo Fílium.

Enítitur puérpera,
Quem Gábriel prædíxerat,
Quem ventre Matris géstiens,
Baptísta clausum sénserat.

Fœno jacére pértulit:
Præsépe non abhórruit:
Et lacte módico pastus est,
Per quem nec ales ésurit.

Gaudet chorus cæléstium,
Et Angeli canunt Deo;
Palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
From lands that see the sun arise
To earth's remotest boundaries,
The Virgin-born today we sing,
The Son of Mary, Christ the King.

Blest Author of this earthly frame,
To take a servant's form He came,
That, liberating flesh by flesh,
Whom He had made might live afresh.

In that chaste parent's holy womb
Celestial grace hath found its home;
And she, as earthly bride unknown,
Yet calls that Offspring blest her own.

The mansion of the modest breast
Becomes a shrine where God shall rest:
The pure and undefilèd one
Conceived in her womb the Son.

That Son, that Royal Son she bore,
Whom Gabriel's voice had told afore;
Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
The infant Baptist had revealed.

The manger and the straw He bore,
The cradle did He not abhor;
By milk in infant portions fed,
Who gives e'en fowls their daily bread.

The heavenly chorus filled the sky,
The Angels sang to God on high,
What time to shepherds, watching lone,
They made creation's Shepherd known.

All honor, laud, and glory be,
O Jesu, Virgin-born to thee:
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymnus
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Quem lucis ante oríginem
Parem patérnæ glóriæ
Pater suprémus édidit.

Tu lumen, et splendor Patris,
Tu spes perénnis ómnium,
Inténde quas fundunt preces
Tui per orbem sérvuli.

Meménto, rerum Cónditor,
Nostri quod olim córporis,
Sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
Nascéndo, formam súmpseris.

Testátur hoc præsens dies,
Currens per anni círculum,
Quod solus e sinu Patris
Mundi salus advéneris.

Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
Hunc omne, quod cælo subest,
Salútis auctórem novæ
Novo salútat cántico.

Et nos, beáta quos sacri
Rigávit unda sánguinis,
Natális ob diem tui
Hymni tribútum sólvimus.

Jesu, tibi sit glória,
Qui natus es de Vírgine,
Cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Jesus, the Ransomer of man,
Who, ere created light began,
Didst from the sovereign Father spring,
His power and glory equalling.

The Father’s Light and Splendor Thou,
Their endless hope to Thee that bow;
Accept the prayers and praise to-day
That through the world Thy servants pay.

Salvation’s Author, call to mind
How, taking form of humankind,
Born of a Virgin undefiled,
Thou in man’s flesh becam’st a Child.

Thus testifies the present day,
Through every year in long array,
That Thou, salvation’s source alone,
Proceedest from the Father’s throne.

The heavens above, the rolling main
And all that earth’s wide realms contain,
With joyous voice now loudly sing
The glory of their new-born King.

And we who, by Thy precious Blood
From sin redeemed, are marked for God,
On this the day that saw Thy birth,
Sing the new song of ransomed earth.

O Lord, the Virgin-born, to Thee
Eternal praise and glory be,
Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.
Amen.

laudes.antiphon.benedictus.label: Ant. ad Benedictus
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.lat: Verbum caro factum est, et habitávit in nobis: et vídimus glóriam ejus, glóriam quasi Unigéniti a Patre plenum grátiæ, et veritátis, allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
laudes.antiphon.benedictus.eng: Glory be to God in the highest; * and on earth, peace to men of good will, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.label: Ant. ad Magnificat
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.lat: Hódie * Christus natus est: hódie Salvátor appáruit: hódie in terra canunt Angeli, lætántur Archángeli: hódie exsúltant justi, dicéntes: Glória in excélsis Deo, allelúja.
vesperae.antiphon.magnificat.eng: This day the Christ is born this day the Saviour is appeared; * this day the Angels sing praise in the earth and the Archangels rejoice; this day the righteous are glad and say: Glory to God in the highest. Alleluia.

laudes.versicle.label: Versicle
laudes.versicle.eng: The Lord hath made known, alleluia.

vesperae.versicle.label: Versicle
vesperae.versicle.eng: Tomorrow the iniquity of the earth shall be blotted out.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Quem vidístis, * pastóres? dícite, annuntiáte nobis, in terris quis appáruit? Natum vídimus, et choros Angelórum collaudántes Dóminum, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: O ye shepherds, speak, * and tell us what ye have seen; who is appeared in the earth? We saw the newborn Child, and angels singing praise to the Lord, alleluia, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Génuit puérpera * Regem, cui nomen ætérnum, et gáudia matris habens cum virginitátis honóre: nec primam símilem visa est, nec habére sequéntem, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Mother brought forth the King, * Whose name is called The Eternal; the joy of a Mother was hers, remaining a Virgin unsullied; neither before nor henceforth hath there been or shall be such another, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Angelus ad pastóres * ait: Annúntio vobis gáudium magnum: quia natus est vobis hódie Salvátor mundi, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: The Angel said unto the shepherds * I bring you good tidings of great joy; for unto you is born this day a Saviour of the world, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Facta est cum Angelo * multitúdo cæléstis exércitus laudántium Deum, et dicéntium: Glória in excélsis Deo, et in terra pax homínibus bonæ voluntátis, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: There was with the Angel a multitude of the heavenly host, * praising God, and saying Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, to men of good will, alleluia.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Párvulus fílius * hódie natus est nobis: et vocábitur Deus, Fortis, allelúja, allelúja.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Unto us this day a little Child is born, * and His name shall be called the Mighty God, alleluia, alleluia.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Tecum princípium * in die virtútis tuæ, in splendóribus sanctórum, ex útero ante lucíferum génui te.;;109
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Thine shall be the dominion * in the day of thy power, amid the brightness of the saints, from the womb, before the day-star, have I begotten thee.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.lat: Redemptiónem * misit Dóminus pópulo suo: mandávit in ætérnum testaméntum suum.;;110
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The Lord sent redemption * unto His people, He hath commanded His covenant for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Exórtum est * in ténebris lumen rectis corde: miséricors, et miserátor, et justus Dóminus.;;111
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Unto the upright there ariseth * light in the darkness; the Lord is gracious, and full of compassion, and righteous.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Apud Dóminum * misericórdia, et copiósa apud eum redémptio.;;129
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: With the Lord * there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: De fructu * ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.;;131
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Of the fruit * of thy body will I set upon thy throne.

Whom, in His mother yet concealed,
